RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 Out - Merit List PDF & Category-Wise Cut Off Released

The wait is finally over for thousands of aspirants who appeared in the Rajasthan Village Development Officer recruitment process. The Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB) has officially announced the RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 on 24 June 2026 at its official website rssb.rajasthan.gov.in. Candidates who participated in the Document Verification (DV) stage under Advertisement No. 03/2025 can now download the final selected candidates' merit list in PDF format and verify their selection status using their roll number.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 - Key Highlights at a Glance

Before diving into the step-by-step process, here is a quick summary of all essential details related to the RSSB VDO Result 2026 that every candidate must know.

Detail Information
Conducting Body Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB)
Exam Name Rajasthan Village Development Officer (VDO) Recruitment 2025
Post Name Village Development Officer (VDO / Gram Vikas Adhikari)
Total Vacancies 850
Advertisement Number 03/2025
DV Process Held December 2025
Final Result Release Date 24 June 2026
Result Mode Online (PDF Format)
Official Website rssb.rajasthan.gov.in

What Is the RSSB VDO Final Result 2026?

This section explains what the final result means and who it is relevant to.

The RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 is the last and conclusive stage of the Rajasthan Village Development Officer recruitment cycle. After candidates cleared the written examination and subsequently appeared for Document Verification (DV) conducted in December 2025, the board has now released the definitive list of 850 candidates who have been formally selected for appointment to the post of Village Development Officer across Rajasthan. This result is released in the form of a downloadable PDF containing roll numbers of all finally selected candidates, along with the category-wise final cut off marks.

Direct Link to Download RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 PDF

Candidates can access the official result directly through the link below. The PDF contains roll numbers of finally selected candidates for all 850 VDO posts.

Official Result Link: RSSB VDO Final Result 2026

Once you open the PDF, press Ctrl + F on your keyboard and type your roll number to instantly search for your name in the selected candidates list.

How to Check RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 - Step-by-Step Process

This section provides a simple, clear guide to help candidates check and download their result without confusion.

Checking the RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 is straightforward. Follow these steps carefully:

Step 1 - Visit the official RSSB website at rssb.rajasthan.gov.in.

Step 2 - On the homepage, navigate to the "Latest News" or "Results" section.

Step 3 - Look for the link titled "Village Development Officer 2025: List of Selected Candidates for Village Development Officer (VDO)" and click on it.

Step 4 - A PDF file will open on your screen containing the final merit list.

Step 5 - Download the PDF and use Ctrl + F to search for your roll number.

Step 6 - If your roll number appears in the list, you have been provisionally selected for the VDO post.

RSSB VDO Result 2026 - Tie-Breaking Rules

In cases where two or more candidates obtain identical marks in the selection process, RSSB has established a clear tie-breaking policy to determine final merit ranking fairly.

When marks are equal between candidates, the following rules apply in sequence:

  • The candidate who has scored higher marks in the main or subject-specific section of the examination is given priority.
  • If the tie still persists after the above step, the candidate who is older in age will be ranked higher.
  • In any remaining cases of tie, additional criteria as specified by the board will be applied.

What Happens After RSSB VDO Final Result 2026?

Many candidates are curious about the steps that follow the declaration of the final result. This section outlines the complete post-result process for selected candidates.

Once the RSSB VDO Final Result 2026 is declared, the selection process moves into the appointment phase. The following steps will typically be carried out for finally selected candidates:

  • Final document verification by the concerned department
  • Departmental and district allocation based on merit and preference
  • Issuance of official appointment/joining letters
  • Induction training as per government norms
  • Posting and formal joining as Village Development Officer

Candidates are advised to keep all original documents ready, including educational certificates, caste certificates (if applicable), identity proof, and any other documents submitted during the DV stage.

Important Notice for Candidates Who Did Not Find Their Roll Number

If a candidate's roll number does not appear in the RSSB VDO Final Merit List PDF, it indicates that they have not been selected in this particular recruitment cycle. Candidates are encouraged to keep an eye on upcoming RSSB recruitment notifications and continue their preparation for future government job opportunities in Rajasthan.

RBI Office Attendant Written Exam 2026 - Background

Before checking the result, it helps to know the context of the exam for which it has been declared. The Reserve Bank of India conducted the Office Attendant Online Test on 1st March 2026 to fill vacancies across various Regional Offices in India under Panel Year 2025. Following the completion of the examination and evaluation process, RBI has now declared the result in PDF format on its official website on 22nd June 2026.

How to Download RBI Office Attendant Result 2026 PDF

This section explains the step-by-step process candidates need to follow to check and download their result from the official RBI website.

  1. Visit the official RBI website: rbi.org.in
  2. On the homepage, look for the link "Recruitment for the Post of Office Attendant - Panel Year 2025."
  3. Click on the link "Roll Numbers of Provisionally Shortlisted Candidates."
  4. The result will open in PDF format on the screen.
  5. Press Ctrl + F to open the search box and type your roll number to locate it quickly.
  6. Download and save the PDF, or take a printout for future reference.

Alternatively, candidates can use the direct download links provided above to access the result PDF without navigating through the website.

What Details Are Mentioned in the RBI Office Attendant Result PDF?

This section explains what kind of information candidates will find once they open the result PDF. The RBI Office Attendant Result 2026 PDF typically contains:

  • Roll numbers of provisionally shortlisted candidates
  • Regional Office applied for by the candidate
  • Exam name and post name
  • Exam conducting authority name
  • Qualifying status (Provisionally Shortlisted)

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in this list are provisionally shortlisted for the written exam stage and become eligible for the Language Proficiency Test (LPT).

Documents Required for the Next Stage

Provisionally shortlisted candidates must submit the following documents within 10 days of result declaration at the respective Regional Office.

OBC Candidates OBC Declaration (original) and latest OBC Caste Certificate

RBI Office Attendant Selection Process 2026: What Comes Next

This section outlines the stages that follow the declaration of the online test result, so qualified candidates know what to prepare for next. The RBI Office Attendant recruitment process involves the following stages:

  1. Online Test (CBT) - Already conducted on 1st March 2026.
  2. Language Proficiency Test (LPT) - Qualifying in nature; tests knowledge of the local/official language of the Regional Office applied for.
  3. Document Verification - Submission of all required educational, category, and identity documents.
  4. Medical Examination - Candidates must be found medically fit.
  5. Final Appointment - Subject to clearing all stages.

Candidates who fail to clear the LPT will be disqualified from the recruitment process even if they have passed the online test. Candidates are advised to keep checking the official RBI website for notices regarding dates and venues for the Language Proficiency Test.

Important Points to Remember

  • The RBI Office Attendant Result 2026 was released on 22nd June 2026 in online/PDF format only; no physical copy or postal communication is sent to candidates.
  • The result PDF is released Office-wise (Regional Office-wise); candidates must check their respective Regional Office list.
  • Provisionally shortlisted candidates must submit required documents within 10 days of the result declaration.
  • It is recommended to download and save a copy of the result PDF for future reference during document verification.
  • Only the official RBI website rbi.org.in should be used to verify the authenticity of the result.

About the MPSC Advertisement No. 130/2022 Recruitment

MPSC Advertisement No. 130/2022 was issued for filling Group-A (Junior) level positions in the Information and Public Relations department of the Maharashtra government. The four posts covered under this advertisement are closely related in nature and responsibility, all involving public communication and information management at the state and district levels.

  • Senior Assistant Director (Information) - Responsible for coordinating information and media activities at the directorate level.
  • District Information Officer - Handles government communication and public relations at the district level.
  • Senior Sub-Editor - Involved in editing and managing content for government publications.
  • Public Relations Officer (Group-A Junior) - Manages public outreach and media coordination for government departments.

The selection process consisted of two stages: a Screening Test and a Personal Interview. The final total marks are the sum of marks scored in both stages.

How to Check the MPSC Provisional Merit List 2026 Online 

Candidates can access the official MPSC Provisional General Merit List for Advertisement No. 130/2022 by following these simple steps. The document is available on the MPSC official website in PDF format.

  1. Visit the official MPSC website at mpsc.gov.in.
  2. Navigate to the "Results" or "Notices" section on the homepage.
  3. Search for Advertisement No. 130/2022 or the post name "Senior Assistant Director (Information)".
  4. Click on the link for the Provisional General Merit List.
  5. The PDF will open; use Ctrl+F to search your Roll Number or Name.
  6. Note down your Merit Number, Total Marks, and category details for future reference.

Understanding the Marks and Qualification Codes in the Merit List

The MPSC merit list uses specific codes to indicate candidates' highest educational qualifications. Understanding these codes is important for correctly reading the list and verifying your entry.

  • A - Ph.D. (Doctorate Degree)
  • B - M.Phil. (Master of Philosophy)
  • C - P.G. Degree (Post Graduate Degree such as MA, MSc, MCom, etc.)

The Total Marks for each candidate are calculated as: Screening Test Marks + Interview Marks = Total Marks. The merit list is arranged in descending order of total marks. In case of a tie in total marks, candidates are ranked based on age (older candidate ranked higher) as per MPSC norms.

What is "Provisional" Merit List? What Happens Next?

The term "provisional" indicates that this merit list is not yet final and is subject to revision. Candidates who find discrepancies or have objections regarding their placement or any factual errors in the list can raise them with MPSC within the specified period. After addressing all valid objections, MPSC will publish the Final Merit List, which will be used for the actual appointment process.

Key points to keep in mind about the provisional merit list:

  • It is based on marks scored in the Screening Test and Personal Interview.
  • Candidates included by MAT court orders are listed separately but are part of the overall selection pool.
  • Candidates should verify their name, roll number, category, and marks carefully.
  • Any discrepancy must be reported to MPSC through the official objection process before the deadline.

GPSC Assistant Inspector Final Result 2026 - Key Highlights

Particulars Details
Organization Gujarat Public Service Commission (GPSC)

Exam Date 04 May 2025

Total Marks 250 (Part A: 125, Part B: 75, Part C: 50)

Official Websites gpsc.gujarat.gov.in, gpsc-ojas.gujarat.gov.in

How Was the GPSC Assistant Inspector Merit List Prepared?

This section explains the rules and criteria GPSC applied while preparing the merit list, including marking scheme, reservation policy, and tie-breaking rules, so candidates understand how their final ranking was determined.

  • Merit has been determined based on marks obtained by candidates in the examination, out of a total of 250 marks (Part A – 125, Part B – 75, Part C – 50), as per Rule 10 of the Assistant Inspector of Motor Vehicles, Class-III Competitive Examination Rules, 2012 (as amended).
  • As per Rule 9, a waiting list equal to 20% of the total advertised posts has been prepared.
  • Reserved category candidates (EWS/SC/ST/SEBC) who met or exceeded the general category qualifying standard without availing any age or marks relaxation have been classified as Meritorious Reserved Category (MRC) candidates and recommended against unreserved posts, as per applicable G.A.D. circulars.
  • Candidates with sports qualifications received bonus marks equal to 5% of their obtained marks, as per Government Resolution No. CRR-1077-2660-G.2, dated 25 February 1980.
  • In case of a tie in marks, preference in merit is given to the older candidate (based on date of birth).
  • The result has also taken into account Supreme Court judgments in Rajesh Kumar Daria vs. Rajasthan Public Service Commission (2007) and Public Service Commission, Uttaranchal vs. Mamta Bist & Others (2010).

  • Supplementary List: 41 candidates distributed across categories including Ezhava/Thiyya/Billava, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Muslim, Latin Catholics/Anglo-Indian, OBC, Viswakarma, SIUC Nadar, Scheduled Caste Converts to Christianity, Dheevara, and Economically Weaker Section (EWS). What Happens After the Shortlist?

Candidates listed should know what the shortlist means and what document verification process follows before the interview stage.

Being included in this list is provisional and does not guarantee a place in the final Ranked List. Shortlisted candidates must:

Candidates who appeared for the Pre-Teacher Education Test held on 14 June 2026 can now download their scorecards from the official website ptetvmoukota2026.in or vmou.ac.in using their roll number and date of birth. This guide covers everything from the direct download link and qualifying marks to the documents you'll need for counselling.

Exam Date 14 June 2026 (Sunday)

Result Declared On 25 June 2026, 11:30 AM
Official Websites ptetvmoukota2026.in / vmou.ac.in

How to Check Rajasthan PTET Result 2026 Online

Downloading your PTET scorecard is a simple login-based process that takes only a few minutes. Below is a step-by-step breakdown so you don't miss any field while entering your details.

  • Go to the official website ptetvmoukota2026.in (or the university portal vmou.ac.in).
  • Select your applicable course 2-Year B.Ed or 4-Year Integrated B.A. B.Ed/B.Sc. B.Ed.
  • Click on the link labelled "PTET Result 2026" or "Download PTET Scorecard 2026."
  • Enter your Roll Number/Application Number along with your Date of Birth (or password, as prompted).
  • Enter the security pin/captcha shown on screen and click Submit.
  • Your scorecard will appear on screen download and save it as a PDF, and keep multiple printouts for the counselling stage.

What Details Are Mentioned on the PTET 2026 Scorecard?

Once your scorecard is downloaded, it's important to verify every detail printed on it, since errors can cause problems later during document verification. The scorecard typically includes the following information.

  • Candidate's full name, roll number, and category
  • Subject-wise and total marks obtained, out of the maximum marks
  • Percentage/percentile score
  • Qualifying status (Qualified/Not Qualified)
  • Merit rank and category-wise rank

If you notice any discrepancy in your scorecard, report it to the university authorities immediately rather than waiting until counselling.

Rajasthan PTET 2026 Minimum Qualifying Marks

Every candidate must clear a minimum cutoff to be eligible for the merit list and subsequent counselling. The qualifying percentage varies by category, as shown in the table below (out of a total of 600 marks).

Category Qualifying Percentage Qualifying Marks (out of 600)
General/Unreserved 50% 300
OBC/MBC (Creamy & Non-Creamy) 45% 270
SC 45% 270

PwD 45% 270
EWS/Widows/Divorcees 45% 270

Rajasthan PTET Merit List 2026

Alongside the result, VMOU Kota will also release a separate PTET Merit List for each course stream. This section explains how the merit list works and why it matters for admission.

The merit list will be prepared individually for the 2-Year B.Ed programme and the 4-Year Integrated B.A. B.Ed / B.Sc. B.Ed programmes. Only candidates whose names appear in the relevant merit list and who meet the category-wise qualifying marks will be eligible to participate in online counselling, choice filling, and seat allotment.

Documents Required for PTET Counselling Verification

Before counselling begins, candidates should organize all required documents to avoid last-minute issues during verification. Keep both originals and photocopies ready.

  • Rajasthan PTET Scorecard 2026 and PTET Admit Card/Hall Ticket
  • Class 10th and Class 12th marksheets and certificates
  • Graduation/Post-Graduation marksheets (for 2-year B.Ed candidates)
  • Valid category/caste certificate (if applicable) and domicile certificate of Rajasthan
  • Income certificate (for applicable categories) and counselling registration fee receipt
  • Passport-size photographs and a government-issued photo ID (Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, or PAN Card)

What Happens After the Rajasthan PTET Result 2026?

Clearing the PTET exam is only the first step admission to a B.Ed college depends on successfully completing the counselling process conducted by VMOU Kota. Here's what to expect next.

  • Step 1 Online Counselling Registration: Qualified candidates must register on the official counselling portal and pay the counselling registration fee (commonly around ₹5,000), which is later adjusted against the college admission fee.
  • Step 2 College Choice Filling: Candidates select their preferred B.Ed colleges from over 935 participating institutions, arranging choices in order of preference to maximize admission chances.
  • Step 3 Seat Allotment: VMOU Kota prepares the seat allotment list based on PTET merit rank, category reservation, and the college preferences submitted.
  • Step 4 Document Verification & Admission Confirmation: Candidates allotted a seat must report to the assigned college with all required documents and pay the remaining admission fee to confirm their seat.
  • Step 5 Upward Movement: Candidates not satisfied with their allotted college can opt for the "Upward Movement" facility, which allows reconsideration for higher-preference colleges if seats fall vacant.

RPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Main List vs Reserve List: What's the Difference?

Candidates often get confused between the Main List and Reserve List released by RPSC for the same exam. This section explains what each list represents so candidates understand exactly which document applies to them.

  • Main List: Contains the roll numbers and cutoff marks of candidates who have been provisionally selected against the originally notified vacancies for the Assistant Statistical Officer post.
  • Reserve List: Contains an additional set of candidates kept on standby. If any candidate from the Main List does not join, gets disqualified during document verification, or is found ineligible, candidates from the Reserve List are considered for selection against the resulting vacancy.

Both lists have been released together by RPSC on 24 June 2026, along with the respective category-wise cutoff marks.

  5. Use Ctrl + F to search your roll number within the PDF.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference, especially for the document verification stage.

The official Main List and Reserve List PDFs contain the category-wise cutoff marks (such as UR, EWS, SC, ST, OBC, and MBC, including Non-TSP and TSP area distinctions where applicable) for the Assistant Statistical Officer exam. Since exact cutoff figures vary by category and are detailed directly inside the official PDF, candidates should refer to the result document on rpsc.rajasthan.gov.in to check the precise qualifying marks for their category.

  • Final Selection Based on successful document verification, RPSC will proceed toward final appointment for the Assistant Statistical Officer post.

Candidates are advised to keep all original and self-attested documents ready in advance to avoid last-minute issues during verification.

  2. Look for the press release or result notification for Advertisement No. 06/2026.
  3. Open the result PDF titled "Jharkhand Combined Civil Services (Backlog) P.T. Examination-2023 Result."
  4. Search for your roll number in the list of selected candidates.
  5. If your roll number appears, you are eligible to apply for the Mains examination.

JPSC CCS Backlog Mains Exam 2026 - Schedule and Paper Structure

The JPSC Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Backlog Main (Written) Examination 2023 will be conducted across three consecutive days in two sessions per day. Each session is three hours long. The full schedule is as follows.

Date First Session (10:00 AM - 1:00 PM) Second Session (2:00 PM - 5:00 PM)
25 July 2026 Paper I Paper II
26 July 2026 Paper III Paper IV
27 July 2026 Paper V Paper VI

A total of six papers will be held over three days, with two papers conducted each day in morning and afternoon sessions respectively.

Online Application Process for JPSC Mains Exam 2026

Candidates who have cleared the JPSC CCS Backlog PT Exam 2023 must fill out the online application form for the Mains examination. The application portal will be available from 27 June 2026. Here is everything you need to know about the application process.

  • Online applications must be submitted at https://jpscotr.com.
  • The application window is open from 27 June 2026 to 2 July 2026 (5:00 PM).
  • Candidates must log in using their registered Email ID / Phone Number / Candidate ID and Password.
  • After logging in, click Start/View Application in Step 1 to view previously entered details.
  • In Step 2, enter the required information for the Mains examination and upload all necessary documents as scanned PDF files.
  • For Paper II (Language & Literature), candidates must select one language subject as per clause 16(a) of the advertisement.
  • Candidates must choose either Hindi or English as the medium for answering Mains papers (except Language & Literature paper) and for the interview.

Required Documents for JPSC Mains Online Application

Candidates must upload self-attested scanned copies of the following documents during the online application process. All original documents must be produced at the time of document verification.

  • Educational Qualification Certificate: Mandatory for all candidates to substantiate their claimed educational eligibility.
  • Category Certificate (BC-II / SC): Candidates claiming reservation benefits under Backward Class-II or Scheduled Caste categories must upload a valid local/domicile certificate as specified in the original advertisement (Clause 6).
  • Caste Certificate: As per the Government of Jharkhand guidance issued vide Memo No. 4258 dated 30 May 2019, a valid caste certificate is also applicable.
  • NOC from Controlling Officer / Head of Department: Candidates who are regular government employees of Jharkhand must upload a No Objection Certificate (NOC) issued by their Controlling Officer or Head of Department.
  • Ex-Serviceman Certificate: Candidates seeking age relaxation on the basis of Ex-Serviceman status must upload the relevant certificate.

Submission of Hard Copy to JPSC Office

In addition to the online application, candidates are required to send a physical (hard copy) of their application and documents to the JPSC office. Missing this step may lead to cancellation of candidature.

  • The hard copy must include a downloaded printout of the online application and self-attested copies of all uploaded certificates.
  • It must be sent via Speed Post / Registered Post or by hand to:
    Pariksha Niyantrak, Jharkhand Lok Seva Aayog, Circular Road, Ranchi - 834001
  • Deadline for receipt of hard copy at the JPSC office: 10 July 2026 (up to 5:00 PM).
  • The envelope must clearly mention in bold: Advertisement No. 06/2026, Registration Number, and Exam Name - "Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Mains (Written) Backlog Competitive Examination-2023."
  • Hard copies received after the deadline will not be accepted, and the candidature will be cancelled. The candidate will be solely responsible for this.

Important Instructions for JPSC CCS Backlog Mains Applicants

Candidates must carefully read all guidelines available on the official JPSC portal before submitting the application. Key instructions issued by JPSC are summarized below.

  • Read the detailed advertisement and application instructions available at https://jpscotr.com before starting the application process.
  • Any discrepancy between the information in the online application and the uploaded documents may result in cancellation of candidature.
  • If any candidate is found to have concealed or misrepresented facts at any stage, their candidature will be cancelled.
  • JPSC will not be responsible for any internet-related disruptions. Candidates are advised not to wait until the last moment and complete all formalities well in advance.
  • The right to correct any typographical or data entry error in the result rests with JPSC.

What Is the RRC ER Liluah Apprentice Merit List 2026?

This section explains the basic nature and purpose of the released panel before candidates dive into checking their names.

The RRC ER Liluah Apprentice Merit List 2026 is a provisional empanelment list published by the Workshop Personnel Officer, Eastern Railway, Liluah. It names candidates found suitable after verification of their original testimonials, shortlisted trade-wise and community-wise as per merit, against the Act Apprentice notification for 2025-26. The panel applies jointly to two units Liluah Workshop and Howrah Division.

Being named on this list is not a confirmation of final selection. The notification clearly states that the panel is purely provisional, and merely being called for further process does not confer any right to engagement as an Act Apprentice.

GSSSB Royalty Inspector Result 2026 - Key Highlights

UPSC Combined Stenographers' (Grade 'B'/Grade-I) LDCE 2019 Final Result

This result covers departmental candidates from the Central Stenographers' cadre seeking promotion to higher stenographic grades across various central services. 

Basis of Recommendations

The recommendations have been made on the basis of candidates' performance in the written examination conducted in December 2025 and the subsequent evaluation of service records completed in May 2026. The final selection combines both components written exam marks out of 500 and service record evaluation to arrive at the merit list for each participating service.

The Armed Forces Headquarters Stenographers' Service recorded the highest number of recommendations, with 16 candidates selected against 24 vacancies. For the Central Secretariat Stenographers' Service, four candidates have been recommended against 287 notified vacancies. In the Indian Foreign Service (Branch 'B') category, five candidates have secured recommendations against 19 vacancies. 

The significant gap between notified vacancies and candidates finally recommended particularly in the Central Secretariat Stenographers' Service reflects the competitive nature and strict eligibility norms of the LDCE process.

UPSC Combined Section Officers' (Grade 'B') LDCE 2025 Final Result

The Final Result for the Combined Section Officers' (Grade 'B') LDCE-2025 has been published on the official UPSC website. This is one of the most sought-after departmental promotion examinations for Assistant Section Officers and eligible central government employees aspiring to be promoted to the Section Officer (Grade 'B') level in key central services.

Exam and Evaluation Details

The Combined Section Officers' (Grade 'B') Limited Departmental Competitive Examination for the year 2025 was held on 13th and 14th December 2025 at exam centres including Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Nagpur, Noida, Ghaziabad, Faridabad, and Gurugram. 

The evaluation process comprises two parts: Part 1 is a written examination worth 500 marks conducted by UPSC, and Part 2 is an evaluation of the record of service carrying a maximum of 100 marks, making the total evaluation based on 600 marks.

Important Notes on Final Selection and Reservation Policy

Understanding the conditions attached to the final select list is essential for all recommended candidates.

UPSC has clarified that the final selection and category-wise allocation of candidates will be determined in accordance with reservation guidelines issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). The outcome will remain subject to decisions in ongoing court proceedings, including matters related to the Jarnail Singh case pending before the Supreme Court. 

Final selection of candidates under different categories shall be decided and results declared inter-alia based on the guidelines issued by the Department of Personnel and Training vide O.M. No. 36012/2016/2019-Estt (Res.) dated 12.04.2022, subject to the final outcome of the Civil Appeal No. 629/2022 arising out of SLP (C). 

Candidates whose results have been withheld will be notified separately by the Commission.

Marks and Cut-Off Publication

Detailed marks, cut-off scores, and related information will be uploaded on UPSC's official website within fifteen days after the declaration of final results for all select list years covered under the examination. Candidates are advised to check upsc.gov.in regularly for their individual mark sheets and category-wise cut-off data.

  • It includes candidates whose application form, category claim, age, and eligibility documents (such as ex-servicemen rank certificate and Marathi language proficiency proof) matched MPSC's prescribed criteria.
  • Being on this list does not guarantee final selection it only confirms eligibility to continue in the recruitment process.
  • Candidates must verify their name/roll number directly from the official PDF linked by MPSC, as no third-party source can confirm individual status.

What Is the MPSC Not Eligible Candidate List?

The not eligible candidate list contains applicants whose forms were rejected during scrutiny, along with the post-wise and category-wise reason for rejection. This section helps such candidates understand why they were excluded and whether they have any recourse.

  • Common reasons for rejection in this category of recruitment typically include incomplete documents, rank/service certificate not matching the required Major-and-above criterion, missing Marathi language proof, or age/category mismatch.
  • MPSC generally provides a specific remark against each rejected application explaining the exact reason.
  • Candidates who believe their rejection is incorrect should check the official notification for any objection or grievance window provided by MPSC, since timelines for raising objections are usually short.

How to Download the MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Candidate List PDF

This section explains the simplest way to access and check your name in the official lists without confusion.

  1. Visit the official MPSC website: mpsc.gov.in
  2. Go to the "Recruitment" or "Advertisement" section and locate Advt No. 004/2026.
  3. Click on the relevant link for Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director result updates.
  4. Open the Eligible Candidate List or Not Eligible Candidate List PDF.
  5. Use Ctrl+F (Find) to search your roll number, application ID, or name.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

About the MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director Post

Before checking the result, it helps to understand the post itself its eligibility, age limit, and pay scale since this context explains why MPSC's scrutiny stage is particularly strict for this role.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Candidates must have ceased to be a serving member of the Armed Forces of the Union and must have held the rank of Major and above in the Army, or an equivalent rank in the Navy or Air Force.
  • Candidates must possess adequate knowledge of Marathi, sufficient to speak, read, and write the language with facility.
  • If officers of the requisite rank are unavailable, those holding the rank of Lieutenant and above (or equivalent) may also be considered.

Age Limit

The maximum age limit for the Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer / Deputy Director post is 55 years for all categories, as specified in the official advertisement.

Salary / Pay Scale

Selected candidates for this Group-A post will receive a pay scale of approximately ₹67,700 to ₹2,08,700, along with applicable government allowances, as per Maharashtra Government service rules.

MPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer Selection Process 2026

Understanding the stages ahead helps eligible candidates prepare for what comes next after this scrutiny result.

Stage Description
Application Scrutiny Verification of documents, rank certificate, and category claims (current stage)
Screening/Written Test Conducted if the number of eligible applicants is large
Interview Personal interview to assess suitability for the post
Final Merit List Prepared based on interview marks (or combined screening + interview marks)

What Should Candidates in the Not Eligible List Do Next?

Candidates appearing in the not eligible list should not assume the process is over without first checking the specific remark mentioned against their name in the PDF. If the rejection appears to be a documentation error, candidates can refer to the official notification on mpsc.gov.in for any objection window and the prescribed procedure to raise a grievance, since MPSC may allow limited corrections in certain cases.

Candidates who do not find a call letter or admit card in their email inbox can still appear for the Trade Test. They simply need to verify that their own name and father's name appear in the official shortlisted candidates' list, and then report on the scheduled date by following the standard reporting instructions.

Important: If a candidate's name appears on the list but they remain absent because they did not receive the email, Ordnance Factory Itarsi will not be held responsible. Every shortlisted candidate is strongly advised to personally check their name in the list rather than waiting for an email confirmation.

This section lists the mandatory documents candidates must carry, since incomplete documentation can affect participation in the test.

Candidates must carry both identity proof and the original documents submitted earlier with their application. The following checklist applies to every shortlisted candidate:

  • Appearing for the test does not guarantee a job offer. Participation in the Trade Test/Practical Test does not automatically make a candidate eligible for engagement. Final appointment depends on the merit list, available vacancies, fulfilment of all eligibility criteria, character verification, medical examination, and document verification.
  • Call letters were issued based on the NAC cut-off. For each feeder trade, a cut-off percentage based on National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) marks was applied. Only candidates meeting or exceeding this cut-off received the email call letter.
  • No requests for change of date or venue will be entertained. Candidates who fail to report at the specified venue on their allotted date risk having their candidature cancelled without further notice.
  • Check the official websites before travelling. Candidates should verify the latest Trade Test date and time on the MIL website (munitionsindia.in) and the DDPDOO website (ddpdoo.gov.in) before starting their journey, in case of any last-minute change.

This section gives quick context on the recruitment drive this shortlist belongs to, useful for candidates who are new to this notification.

Ordnance Factory Itarsi had earlier released its Tenure Based CPW recruitment notification for 265 vacancies under the primary trade of AOCP (Attendant Operator Chemical Plant) and other specified feeder trades such as Fitter, Electrician, Machinist, and Turner. As per the official selection process, candidates are first shortlisted on the basis of their NAC marks against a trade-specific cut-off, then called for the Trade Test/Practical Test, after which a final merit list is prepared by combining both sets of marks before document verification and engagement.

APPSC Junior Assistant Hall Ticket 2026 - How to Download Your Admit Card

The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission (APPSC) releases hall tickets for the Junior Assistant cum Computer Operator exam through its dedicated hall ticket portal at portal-psc.ap.gov.in/Download_HallTickets/LOGINFORM_OTHERS. Candidates need their OTPR (One Time Profile Registration) ID and password to log in and download the admit card, which is mandatory for entry into the exam hall. What Is the APPSC Junior Assistant Hall Ticket?

This section explains what the hall ticket is and why it matters for exam-day entry.

The hall ticket (admit card) is an official document issued by APPSC that confirms a candidate's registration for the Junior Assistant cum Computer Operator written examination. It carries identity and exam-logistics details and acts as the primary entry pass at the test centre no candidate is permitted inside the exam hall without it.

How to Download the APPSC Junior Assistant Hall Ticket 2026

This section covers the exact step-by-step login process used on the official APPSC hall ticket portal.

  1. Go to the official hall ticket portal: portal-psc.ap.gov.in/Download_HallTickets/LOGINFORM_OTHERS (or the main site psc.ap.gov.in).
  2. Locate and click the link related to "Junior Assistant cum Computer Operator" hall ticket download under the Download Hall Tickets section.
  3. Enter your OTPR ID and Password, then complete the captcha.
  4. Select your applied post/notification if prompted, and click Submit.
  5. Your hall ticket will display on screen download it as a PDF and take a clear printout.

Information Printed on the Hall Ticket

This section lists the candidate and exam details that typically appear on an APPSC admit card.

  • Candidate name, photograph, and signature
  • Father's/Mother's name
  • Roll number and exam centre code
  • Exam centre name and address
  • Exam date, reporting time, and duration
  • Category (SC/ST/BC/Other) and gender
  • Important exam-day instructions

Documents to Carry Along With the Hall Ticket

This section outlines the proof-of-identity documents APPSC requires alongside the printed admit card.

Candidates must carry the printed hall ticket plus one valid original photo ID, such as:

  • Aadhaar Card
  • PAN Card
  • Voter ID
  • Passport
  • Driving Licence
  • College/Employee ID (where applicable)

What If You Can't Download the Hall Ticket?

This section gives quick fixes for common login or access issues on the portal.

If the hall ticket doesn't load or login fails, try these steps before contacting support:

  • Clear your browser cache and cookies, or try a different browser/device
  • Double-check your OTPR ID and password for typing errors
  • Wait and retry, since the portal can be slow during peak download periods

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. How to Download RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026

RBI Grade B Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Section Questions Marks Duration
Reasoning Ability 60 60 45 Minutes
English Language 30 30 25 Minutes

Total 200 200 120 Minutes

Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Pattern - Objective + Descriptive

Phase 2 is the main scoring round with 300 marks spread across 3 papers. Both objective and descriptive components are tested. Marks from this stage directly determine the final merit list.

Paper Subject Question Type Marks Duration
Paper I Economic & Social Issues (ESI) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes
Paper III Finance & Management (FM) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Total     300 330 Minutes

RBI Grade B Exam Day Instructions 2026

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. Electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and books are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. The exam centre and date allotted on the call letter are final no requests for change of centre, date, or session will be entertained.

The selection process for all HPRCA Teacher posts, including Public Administration, follows these stages:

  2. Qualifying Marks Minimum 45% for General category and 40% for SC/ST/OBC/WFB categories (subject to relaxation if insufficient candidates qualify).

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces before/after)
  • Check date of birth format if using DOB: DD/MM/YYYY
  • Ensure CAPS LOCK is off while entering details
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies (Ctrl+Shift+Del)
  • Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
  • Use “Forgot Password” link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation details

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your slot
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning or late night)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately via regional offices
  • Email or call with screenshot and registration details
  • Keep your registration number ready
  • Explain the exact discrepancy in detail
  • Request for correction before exam date

Issue #4: PDF Download Not Working

Solutions:

  • Take a screenshot of the city slip as backup
  • Try “Print to PDF” option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)
  • Use a different PDF reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader)
  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Refresh the page (F5 key)
  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card - Key Differences

Aspect City Intimation Slip Admit Card / Hall Ticket
Purpose Advance information only for travel planning Mandatory entry document for examination
Release Time Around 5-10 days before exam (30 Jan 2026) From 1 Feb 2026 onwards (2-4 days before exam)
Information Provided Exam city, date, shift timing only Complete center address, roll number, photo, signature
Can you enter exam hall? NO - Not permitted YES - Mandatory requirement
Contains Photo No Yes
Contains Roll Number No (or limited) Yes
Exam Center Address Only city name Complete address with venue details
Use for Travel Booking Yes - Use for advance planning Can use after release
Barcode/QR Code Usually not present Present for verification
Exam Instructions General instructions Detailed exam day instructions

Critical Warning: You CANNOT enter the examination hall with only the city intimation slip. You MUST download and carry the admit card (from 1 February 2026 onwards) along with a valid photo ID proof to appear for the exam.

UPTET Online Form 2026 : Educational Qualification 

Class  Eligibility 
Primary Level Teachers (Class 1 to 5)
  • Candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree from an NCTE-recognized institution along with a valid teacher training qualification such as BTC, B.El.Ed, or equivalent. Final-year candidates are also eligible. In general, a minimum of 50% marks in graduation or the relevant training program is required.
Upper Primary Teacher (Class 6 to 8)
  • Candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree with at least 50% marks (45% in some cases as per rules) from an NCTE-recognized institution along with a valid teacher training qualification such as B.Ed, BTC, B.El.Ed, or equivalent. Final-year candidates of these courses are also eligible. Additionally, candidates with specialized education qualifications (like Special Education) from RCI-recognized institutes are eligible. In some cases, candidates with 50% marks in intermediate and a 4-year integrated teaching program can also apply.

Who Can Apply? - NIACL Apprentice 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Understanding the eligibility criteria is the first and most critical step before applying. Here is a detailed breakdown of all conditions you must satisfy.

Nationality

All applicants must be citizens of India.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government.

Crucially, the final year mark sheet date must fall between January 1, 2022 and June 1, 2026 (both dates inclusive). Graduates who passed before January 1, 2022, or after June 1, 2026, are not eligible.

Prior Apprenticeship Condition

  • Candidates must not have previously undergone apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act 1961 - either with NIACL or any other organization.
  • Candidates currently pursuing an apprenticeship anywhere are also ineligible.
  • Candidates with one or more years of job experience after graduation are not eligible.

NIACL Apprentices Recruitment 2026 Apply Online Link - Activated

Online Applications Are Now Open (June 23 – July 6, 2026)

The application process is a two-step procedure. Both steps must be completed for your application to be valid.

Step 1 - Register on the NATS Portal: Apply via the official NATS (National Apprenticeship Training Scheme) portal run by the Government of India: https://nats.education.gov.in (Complete 100% of your profile and click "APPLY" against The New India Assurance Company Limited.)

Step 2 - Complete Application & Pay Fee on BFSI Portal: After NATS registration, proceed to: https://beep.bfsissc.com/candidate_login (Update your personal information, NATS enrolment number, documents, state preference, and pay the examination fee.)

Important: Your application is only considered complete after the examination fee is successfully paid online. Incomplete applications will be automatically rejected.

Application & Examination Fee Structure

All fees must be paid online. No offline payment mode is accepted. GST at 18% is charged over the base fee.

Once paid, the fee is non-refundable under all circumstances, including application rejection or withdrawal.

Step-by-Step Application Process for NIACL Apprentice 2026

Here is a clear walkthrough of exactly what you need to do to successfully submit your application.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Begin

Gather these before starting the registration to avoid interruptions:

  • Aadhaar Card
  • Valid personal email ID (for account activation and login)
  • Active mobile number
  • Passport-size photograph (JPEG format, under 1 MB)
  • Qualifying degree or provisional certificate (PDF format, under 1 MB)

Step-by-Step Process

1. Register on NATS Portal Visit https://nats.education.gov.in, create your account, and ensure your profile is 100% complete. Then apply specifically for The New India Assurance Company Limited's apprenticeship listing.

2. Note Your NATS Enrolment Number After applying on NATS, you will receive a unique NATS enrolment number. This is mandatory for the next step.

3. Apply on BFSI SSC Portal Go to https://beep.bfsissc.com/candidate_login. Fill in personal details, upload documents, enter your NATS enrolment number, choose your preferred state, and pay the examination fee.

4. Select Only One State Candidates can apply for only one state. Your training, if selected, will be at a Regional Office within that state based on the company's requirements.

5. Confirm Payment & Save Application After successful payment, take a printout of your completed online application form. No changes are permitted after final submission.

Selection Process - How NIACL Apprentices Are Chosen

Selection happens in two main stages after fee payment. Here is what to expect at each stage.

Stage 1 - Online Written Test (Objective Type)

The online exam is held from home (proctored), using your own camera-enabled device - desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone.

Section No. of Questions Maximum Marks Language
General / Financial Awareness 25 25 English / Hindi
General English 25 25 English only
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 25 25 English / Hindi
Computer Knowledge 25 25 English / Hindi
Total 100 100 -
  • Duration: 60 minutes
  • Tie-breaking rule: If two candidates score equally, the older candidate is ranked higher (descending age order).

Stage 2 - Regional Language Test & Document Verification

Candidates who clear the online written test are shortlisted in 3× the number of available seats per state per category for this stage.

  • Candidates who studied the regional language of their chosen state in Class 10 or 12 are exempt from the language test.
  • All others must demonstrate proficiency (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified local language of the state.
  • Candidates failing the language test cannot be engaged as apprentices.

Document Verification Checklist

Carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of:

  1. Photo ID proof (Aadhaar / PAN / Voter ID / Driving License / Passport)
  2. Class 10 certificate (as proof of date of birth)
  3. Class 12 marksheets and graduation marksheets (semester/year-wise) with degree
  4. CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate (if applicable)
  5. SC / ST / OBC / EWS / PwBD certificates with required declarations

Stipend, Training Conditions & What to Expect

This section covers what apprentices receive during training and the rules governing their engagement.

Stipend & Payment

  • Monthly stipend: ₹12,300
  • Payment is made by the 10th day of the following month
  • No additional benefits, allowances, or statutory contributions (PF, Mediclaim, etc.) are provided
  • Pro-rata deduction applies for unauthorized absences

Leave Policy

  • 1 day of leave per month, credited at the beginning of the next month
  • Leave can be carried forward but not more than 2 days at a time
  • All accumulated leave lapses at the end of the contract
  • Apprentices are entitled to all company-observed public holidays

Training Duration & Certification

  • Training period: 12 months
  • On completion, apprentices undergo an assessment (theory by BFSI SSC + practical by NIACL)
  • Successful candidates receive an Apprenticeship Certificate from BFSI SSC

Employment Disclaimer

It is important to note clearly: this is not a job offer. NIACL is under no obligation to offer employment after training, and apprentices have no right to claim a job. This is a training engagement, not a contract or regular employment.

Special Guidelines for Reserved Category Candidates

Certain candidate groups have specific rules they must be aware of before applying.

OBC Candidates

  • Only Non-Creamy Layer OBC candidates are entitled to OBC reservation benefits.
  • Creamy layer OBC candidates must apply under the General (Unreserved) category and meet General category age criteria.
  • An undertaking regarding non-creamy layer status must be submitted at the time of fee payment.

EWS Candidates

  • Candidates must produce an Income and Asset Certificate for financial year 2025–26, issued by a competent authority after March 31, 2026.
  • Gross annual family income must be below ₹8 lakh, and the family must not own 5+ acres of agricultural land, 1000+ sq. ft. residential flat, or qualifying residential plots.

PwBD Candidates (Persons with Benchmark Disabilities)

  • Minimum disability of 40% is required for reservation benefits.
  • Eligible disability types: Visual Impairment (VI), Hearing Impairment (HI), Locomotor/Orthopedic (OH), Intellectual/Autism (ID), Multiple Disabilities (MD).
  • PwBD candidates using a scribe get 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour.
  • The scribe must not be a co-applicant for the same exam and cannot serve as scribe for more than one candidate.

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

RCF Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria – Qualification and Age Limit

The eligibility criteria for RCF Officer Recruitment 2026 vary significantly by post and grade. All qualifications must be from UGC/AICTE-recognized universities or institutions, and experience is calculated as of 01 March 2026.

Officer (Finance) – E1 Grade

Candidates must hold either a CA/CMA qualification or a full-time graduation degree in Commerce/Accounting/Finance (B.Com, BMS, BAF, BBA) along with a 2-year full-time MBA/MMS/PGDM/PGDBM with specialization in Finance. M.Com alone is not accepted. Minimum 60% in the final year of the qualifying post-graduation degree is required (55% for SC/ST). No percentage criterion applies for CA/CMA holders. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification executive-level experience in accounting, auditing, budgeting, or taxation is required. Training, internship, and articleship periods do not count toward experience. Age limit: SC/ST – 39 years; OBC (NCL) – 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (HR) – E1 Grade

A full-time graduation degree in any discipline plus a 2-year full-time post-graduation degree/diploma/equivalent master's degree with specialization in HR/Personnel/Social Work/Welfare/Industrial Relations/Labour Studies from a UGC/AICTE institution is required. Minimum 55% for SC category candidates in the final year of the post-graduation. Additional qualification in law and proficiency in Marathi are preferred. Minimum 2 years of experience in HR departments covering labour administration, industrial relations, and grievance handling is required. Age limit: SC – 39 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Medical) – E1 Grade

MBBS with completed internship and registration with the Medical Council of India or State Medical Council is mandatory. Preference is given to candidates with a Certificate Course in Industrial Health (3 months) or AFIH recognized by DGFASLI, or a 2-year recognized Diploma in Anaesthesiology. Minimum 2 years of experience (excluding internship) in a hospital of 25 beds or more is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) – 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Senior Manager (CC Lab) – E5 Grade

Candidates must hold either a Ph.D. in Chemistry from a UGC/AICTE-approved institution or a 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Chemical Engineering/Petrochemical Engineering/Chemical Technology (minimum 60% aggregate). Preference is given to Ph.D. holders. Minimum 17 years of relevant experience in academics or research is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) – 52 years as on 01.03.2026.

Officer (Legal) – E1 Grade

A regular full-time LLB degree or a 5-year integrated Law degree from a recognized Indian university is required, with a minimum of 60% in the final year of LLB. At least 2 years of relevant experience in PSU/Government/Autonomous Bodies/MNC/Private Organization/Law firms or practicing as an Advocate is required. Age limit: OBC (NCL) – 37 years as on 01.03.2026.

Assistant Engineer (Electrical) – E0 Grade

A 3-year full-time Diploma in Electrical/Allied Electrical Engineering/Technology from a UGC/AICTE institution is required, with a minimum of 60% in the final year. Sandwich-pattern diploma holders (3½ or 4 years) are also eligible. Minimum 16 years of post-diploma relevant working experience is required. Age limit: UR – 42 years; OBC (NCL) – 45 years as on 01.03.2026.

Engineer (Electrical) – E1 Grade

A 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Electrical/Electrical and Power/Electrical Power Engineering, or a 3-year B.E./B.Tech acquired after a 3-year full-time Diploma, or a Dual/Integrated Degree in Electrical Engineering - all from UGC/AICTE institutions with minimum 60% aggregate - is required. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance in fertilizer, chemical, refinery, petrochemical, cement, or power plant industries is required. Age limit: UR – 34 years; OBC (NCL) – 37 years; PwBD (UR) – 44 years; PwBD OBC (NCL) – 47 years as on 01.03.2026. One PwBD (OH – one lower limb affected) vacancy is available.

Senior Engineer (Electrical) – E2 Grade

Same educational qualification as Engineer (Electrical) - minimum 60% B.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering from UGC/AICTE institutions. Minimum 4 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance is required. Age limit: UR – 36 years; OBC (NCL) – 39 years as on 01.03.2026.

Deputy Manager (Electrical) – E3 Grade

Same educational qualification as above (B.E./B.Tech Electrical, minimum 60%) from UGC/AICTE institutions. Minimum 8 years of post-qualification field experience in HT/LT electrical equipment maintenance is required. Age limit: UR – 38 years; OBC (NCL) – 41 years as on 01.03.2026.

Engineer (Civil) – E1 Grade

A 4-year full-time B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering or allied Civil specializations (Construction Engineering, Civil Technology, etc.) with minimum 60% from UGC/AICTE institutions is required. Lateral entry B.E./B.Tech after a 3-year Diploma is also eligible. Minimum 2 years of post-qualification experience in process industries such as fertilizers, chemicals, or refineries is required. Age limit: UR – 34 years as on 01.03.2026.

Senior Engineer (Civil) – E2 Grade

Same qualification as Engineer (Civil) - B.E./B.Tech Civil Engineering (60% minimum). Minimum 4 years of post-qualification experience in process industries preferably in fertilizers, chemicals, or petrochemicals is required. Age limit: UR – 36 years as on 01.03.2026.

Selection Process – RCF Recruitment 2026

The selection process for RCF Ltd 2026 differs by grade. Understanding the process in advance helps candidates prepare effectively for each stage.

For the E0 Grade (Assistant Engineer – Electrical), selection is through a Skill Test consisting of three components: Practical Job Knowledge and Handling of Technical Equipment (70 marks), Safety Awareness and Computer Knowledge (20 marks), and Communication Skills (10 marks) - totalling 100 marks. Candidates must score a minimum of 60 marks (55 marks for SC/ST) to qualify. The Skill Test is of a qualifying nature.

For E1 Grade and above (all Officer, Engineer, Senior Engineer, Deputy Manager, and Senior Manager posts), selection is through a Personal Interview. The interview carries 100 marks distributed as: Subject Knowledge (50 marks), Nature of Experience (20 marks), Personality and Communication Skills (15 marks), and General Awareness/Computer Knowledge/Additional Qualification (15 marks). Candidates must secure a minimum average of 50% marks to qualify the interview.

A waiting list is also maintained - in the ratio of 1:2 for up to 5 vacancies and 1:1 for more than 5 vacancies - valid for one year from the date of empanelment.

All outstation candidates called for Skill Test or Personal Interview are reimbursed to-and-fro III-tier AC train/bus fare from their correspondence address to the interview/test venue.

  11. For any queries related to the online form, email: [email protected]

Common Mistakes to Avoid – RCF Bharti 2026

Many candidates lose their eligibility due to avoidable errors in the application process. The following original guidance is based on common pitfalls in PSU recruitment applications.

Uploading documents in wrong formats is one of the most common rejection reasons - ensure photographs are in JPG/JPEG at 165×125 pixels and all supporting documents are in PDF format. Candidates often assume M.Com qualifies for the Finance Officer post - the notification explicitly states M.Com is not accepted; an MBA/MMS/PGDM with Finance specialization is mandatory. Failing to convert CGPA to percentage before submission causes frequent rejections; contact your university for the official conversion formula and attach a copy at interview. OBC candidates whose most recent Non-Creamy Layer certificate was issued before 1 April 2025 will not be accepted - the notification specifically requires a certificate issued on or after 1 April 2025.

Counting internship, articleship, or training periods as work experience is not permitted - only post-qualification executive experience counts. Name mismatches between the application and photo identity proof result in disqualification from the Skill Test or Interview - use your name exactly as it appears on your Matriculation certificate. Government-employed candidates must carry a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their present employer at the time of interview or their candidature will be rejected.

Eligibility Criteria - Qualification & Age Limit

The CCRUM Ayush Job 2026 eligibility varies significantly by post group. Candidates should verify their qualification carefully against the specific post before applying, as merely meeting one criterion is not sufficient.

Group A - Research Officers

Research Officer (Unani): PG Degree (MD or MS) in Unani System of Medicine from a university/institution recognized by NCISM (formerly CCIM), plus enrolment on the Central Registrar of NCISM/CCIM or State Register of Unani/ISM. Age: up to 40 years (Government servants get 5 years' relaxation).

Research Officer (Pathology): MD in Pathology from an MCI-recognized university. Enrolment on Central Register of MCI or State Register of Medical Council. Age: up to 40 years.

Research Officer (Physiology): Master's Degree in Molecular Biology / Biotechnology / Human Genetics / Genetics Engineering from a recognized institution, plus 3 years' post-Master's research experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant subject. Age: up to 40 years.

Group B - Key Posts

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacology): M.Sc. in Pharmacology or M.V.Sc from a recognized university. Age: up to 30 years.

Asst. Research Officer (Pharmacognosy/Botany): Master's Degree in the concerned discipline plus 3 years' research/teaching experience OR a Ph.D. in the relevant discipline. Age: up to 35 years.

Staff Nurse: B.Sc. (Hons) Nursing / Regular B.Sc. Nursing / Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing OR Diploma in General Nursing & Midwifery from a recognized institution, registered as Nurse/Nurse & Midwife with State Nursing Council, plus 1 year's experience in a minimum 50-bed hospital. Age: up to 35 years.

Accounts Officer (HQ): Degree from a recognized university plus 3 years' experience in Cash, Accounts, and Budget work in a Government Office / PSU / Autonomous Body. Age: up to 30 years (5-year relaxation for CCRUM employees).

MLT: Bachelor's Degree in Medical Laboratory Science with 2 years' relevant experience. Age: up to 35 years.

Library & Information Assistant: Degree from a recognized university plus Degree in Library Science. Age: up to 28 years.

Group C - Key Posts

UDC: Degree from a recognized university. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

LDC: 12th class pass with typing speed of 35 wpm in English or 30 wpm in Hindi on computer. Age: between 18 and 27 years.

Stenographer Grade-III: Matric/equivalent plus shorthand speed of 80 wpm and typewriting speed of 40 wpm. Age: up to 28 years.

Staff Car Driver: Matriculation pass, valid driving license for Motor Cars/LMV, 3 years' motor car driving experience, knowledge of vehicle maintenance. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

MTS: Matriculation/equivalent pass OR ITI pass in relevant subject. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Compounder: Matric or equivalent plus Certificate of Training as Compounder in Unani System of Medicine (minimum 1 year), plus 2 years' experience preferably in a Unani Dispensary/Hospital. Age: 28 years and below.

Pharmacist: 10+2 with Science plus 2-year Diploma in Pharmacy plus registration with State/Central Pharmacy Council. Age: between 18 and 25 years.

Age Relaxation Summary

Candidates wondering about age relaxation can note the following: SC/ST candidates get 5 years' relaxation, OBC-NCL candidates get 3 years, PwBD (UR) candidates get 10 years, PwBD (OBC-NCL) candidates get 13 years, and PwBD (SC/ST) candidates get 15 years. The maximum age after all cumulative relaxations shall not exceed 56 years. Candidates domiciled in Jammu & Kashmir between 1 January 1980 and 31 December 1989 are also eligible for 5 years' relaxation.

Application Fee - CCRUM Recruitment 2026

The CCRUM 2026 application fee structure is divided into a non-refundable Processing Fee (applicable to all candidates) and an Examination Fee (waived for exempted categories). SC/ST, PwBD, EWS, Women candidates, and Ex-Servicemen are exempt from the Examination Fee but must still pay the Processing Fee.

Payment is accepted only through the online payment gateway via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. Cash, Demand Draft, and Postal Orders are not accepted. The fee is inclusive of GST; bank charges will be levied additionally depending on the payment mode.

Selection Process - CCRUM Ayush Vacancy 2026

The CCRUM 2026 selection process differs by post group. Group A candidates face both a written test and an interview, while Group B and C candidates are selected primarily through the Computer Based Test.

Group A Posts (Research Officers):

  • Online CBT - 70 marks (subject knowledge + research methodology + general awareness)
  • Interview - 30 marks
  • Shortlisting ratio: 1:5 for 1 vacancy, 1:4 for 2 vacancies, 1:3 for 3 or more vacancies
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Group B & C Posts:

  • Online CBT - 100 marks
  • Skill Test (mandatory and qualifying) for LDC, Stenographer Grade-III, Staff Car Driver, and wherever applicable
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 25% for SC/ST/PwBD; 30% for all others

Negative Marking: There is a 0.25 mark deduction per wrong answer in the CBT for all posts except MTS, where there is no negative marking.

Exam Duration: 100 minutes for all candidates (Group A, B & C). PwBD candidates eligible for a scribe receive 130 minutes (100 + 30 compensatory minutes).

Exam Centers: New Delhi/Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Guwahati.

Tie-Breaking Rules: In case of equal marks, tie-breaking follows this order: older age ranked higher → higher subject marks → higher marks in second part of syllabus → earlier degree/diploma completion → higher final aggregate percentage.

Exam Syllabus at a Glance

The CCRUM CBT syllabus is post-specific. Every paper follows a common structure: subject knowledge (70 marks) + research methodology/relevant technical knowledge (20 marks) + general awareness/IT & computing (10 marks) for Group B and C posts. Group A post papers total 70 marks (subject: 40 + research methodology: 20 + general awareness/IT: 10), followed by an interview of 30 marks. MTS and Staff Car Driver follow SSC's MTS/Matric-level examination syllabus.

How to Apply - CCRUM Recruitment 2026 Online Application

All applications for CCRUM Bharti 2026 must be submitted online only through the official CCRUM website. No documents or application forms need to be sent to CCRUM by post or mail.

  1. Visit www.ccrum.res.in or www.ccrum.ayush.gov.in and go to the "Advertisement/Vacancy" tab.
  2. Create a new account (Step I): Enter your full name (as per Matriculation Certificate), father's name, mother's name, gender, date of birth, mobile number, valid email ID, and Government ID proof. Verify via OTP.
  3. Complete your profile (Step II): Log in with your Reference Number and Password. Upload photograph, signature, caste certificate, disability certificate (if applicable), basic qualification certificates, and other relevant documents.
  4. Apply for the post (Step III): Select the post(s) you wish to apply for, fill in post-specific information, and upload post-specific documents.
  5. Pay the fee: You will be redirected to the payment gateway. Pay via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI. Download the payment acknowledgement slip.
  6. Download your application form in PDF format from the Dashboard for future reference.

Important: Details entered during account creation (Step I) cannot be modified at any later stage. Candidates applying for multiple posts must use the same login reference number and pay the fee separately for each post.

Modification Window

After the application window closes, CCRUM provides a Modification Window from 3 August 2026 (10:00 AM) to 5 August 2026 (23:59 hrs). A modification fee of ₹300 per attempt per post is charged. Note that account creation details from Step I cannot be changed through this window. If a modification makes a candidate ineligible for the post, the change will not be permitted.

Salary / Pay Scale

The CCRUM Recruitment 2026 offers 7th CPC pay structure with NPA (Non-Practising Allowance) for Group A medical posts as per Government of India rules. Selected candidates are placed on probation for two years, extendable at the discretion of the competent authority, and will be governed by the New Pension Scheme (NPS). All posts carry All India transfer liability; candidates must be willing to serve at any of CCRUM's 24 Institutes/Centers across India.
