Documents Required

Candidates should keep the following documents ready before starting the CCRUM online application 2026. All documents must be scanned and uploaded in JPEG/JPG or PDF format as specified.

  • Latest passport-size colour photograph (50–100 KB, JPEG/JPG), taken in 2026
  • Signature on white paper with black ink pen (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG)
  • Caste/Category Certificate in Central Government format (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD/EWS)
  • Disability Certificate issued by Competent Authority (for PwBD candidates)
  • Discharge Certificate (for Ex-Servicemen)
  • Educational qualification certificates with mark sheets
  • Valid Government photo ID proof (Voter ID, Passport, PAN Card, or Driving License)
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates already in Government service)
  • Each document file: between 100 KB and 1000 KB in PDF/JPG/JPEG format

Common Mistakes to Avoid

These are avoidable errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification in CCRUM recruitment:

  • Entering wrong details at account creation: Name, date of birth, and gender entered at Step I cannot be changed under any circumstances. Cross-check with your Matriculation Certificate before submitting.
  • Not checking the OBC certificate date: Your OBC (NCL) certificate must have been obtained within 3 years before the closing date of application. An outdated certificate will result in disqualification.
  • Applying through offline modes: Applications submitted by post, email, or courier are rejected outright without any communication.
  • Uploading blurry or cut documents: All uploaded documents must be clear, complete, and within the specified file size limits.
  • Missing the payment confirmation step: Your application is only considered submitted after successful payment. Always ensure the payment status reads "Payment Received."
  • Not downloading your application form: After Step III, download and preserve your application form PDF and payment receipt from the Dashboard for future reference.
  • Using electronic devices in the exam hall: Mobiles, smart watches, calculators, earphones, and Bluetooth devices are strictly prohibited. Violation leads to a ban of at least 5 years from CCRUM exams.
  • Applying for multiple posts with different logins: Candidates must use the same reference number for all posts. Creating multiple accounts is not permitted.

Indian Navy SSC Selection Process 2026

The Indian Navy SSC selection process 2026 is a multi-stage procedure that begins with shortlisting based on normalised marks and culminates in a merit list after SSB interview and medical examination. Understanding each stage will help candidates prepare strategically for this defence government job.

Stage 1 – Shortlisting for SSB Interview

Shortlisting will be done using formulae mentioned on the Indian Navy website (https://www.joinindiannavy.gov.in/files/normalisation.pdf). Marks obtained by candidates in the qualifying degree will be considered for SSB shortlisting.

  • BE/B.Tech candidates: Marks obtained up to the fifth semester will be considered. For candidates in the final year, shortlisting will be based on final-year performance.
  • Post-Graduate Degree Programme candidates: For those who have completed MSc, MCA, MBA, M.Tech, marks obtained in all semesters will be considered.

Stage 2 – SSB Interview

Shortlisted candidates will be informed about their selection for SSB interview through e-mail or SMS. Candidates are advised not to change their e-mail/mobile number till selection process is over and to check their inbox and spam folder periodically. Change of SSB Centre for interview is not permissible under any circumstances.

Stage 3 – Medical Examination

SSB-recommended candidates will be required to inform their final result of their respective degree to the Indian Navy at [email protected] prior to 20 June 2027. Candidates declared fit in the medical examination would be appointed as per availability of vacancies in the entry.

Stage 4 – Merit List

A merit list will be prepared based on SSB marks for all entries, after medical clearance for the respective entry. Mere inclusion in the select list does not confer a vested right to appointment. All vacancies are to be filled as per service requirement and as per statutory guidelines issued from time to time.

Indian Navy Officer Salary 2026

  • The initial gross salary of a Sub Lieutenant starts from Rs 1,20,000/- (approximately) per month, along with other allowances as applicable.
  • Pilot/NAOO and Submarine allowance of Rs 31,250/- will be admissible to candidates post successful completion of training.

Selected candidates will be granted Short Service Commission initially for 12 years, extendable by a maximum of 02 years, subject to service requirement, performance, medical eligibility, and willingness of candidates.

Indian Navy SSC Probation Period

Probation period for all branches/cadres is two years. The probation period will commence from the date of grant of the rank of Sub Lieutenant and will terminate after two years or on completion of initial training (whichever is later). During probation, officers are liable to be discharged in case of unsatisfactory performance at any stage.

Indian Navy Physical and Medical Standards 2026

Candidates are strongly advised to ascertain their eligibility for branches with respect to applicable medical standards, prior to indicating their preference. This is especially relevant for SSC (Pilot) entry where specified numbers of candidates based on service requirement will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination.

  • A specified number of candidates for SSC (Pilot) entry will be considered for SSB/CPSS/Aviation Medical Examination and are advised to check physical/medical standards (Height, leg length etc.) before selecting this option.
  • Remaining candidates will be considered for other preferences opted by them.
  • Candidates declared medically fit for DG Jul 27 course will be considered fit for all SSC branches of IN (except for Pilot/NAOO).
  • Please visit www.joinindiannavy.gov.in for information. SSB-recommended candidates must undergo medical examination applicable to their entry. Change of medical hospital/centre is not permissible under any circumstances.

Training Details – Indian Naval Academy

Candidates selected for the Indian Navy SSC Jun 2027 (AT 27) Course will undergo training at the Indian Naval Academy (INA), Ezhimala, Kerala. Key training-related points are as follows:

  • Candidates will be inducted in the rank of Sub Lieutenant, subject to clearing induction medical examination at INA, Ezhimala upon posting.
  • Only unmarried candidates are eligible for training. Any candidate found to be married or who marries during training will be discharged from service.
  • Candidates must fulfil the educational qualification stipulated above before joining INA, Ezhimala by June 2027. The candidate failing to meet stipulated educational criteria will not be permitted to join INA, Ezhimala.
  • Male candidates shortlisted for GS(X) are also eligible to volunteer for submarine arm subject to medical fitness, vacancies, and service requirements.

Apply Online – Indian Navy SSC Officer 2026

Candidates who meet the Indian Navy SSC eligibility criteria 2026 can apply online through the official Indian Navy recruitment portal. The online application process is active from 25 June 2026 and the final deadline is 27 July 2026. No applications will be accepted after the last date.

Important instructions before applying:

  • Candidates must register and fill the application on the Indian Navy website at www.joinindiannavy.gov.in. To save time, candidates can fill in their details and upload documents in advance.
  • Whilst filling the e-application, keep the following documents readily available:
    • Correct personal particulars (as given in Matriculation Certificate)
    • Valid e-mail address and mobile number (mandatory fields)
    • CGPA covering up to 5th & 7th semester for regular and integrated BE/B.Tech courses respectively and all semesters for other degree programmes
    • All relevant documents (preferably mark sheets up to 10th & 12th certificate)
    • Date of birth proof (as proof of 10th or 12th certificate)
    • NCC 'C' certificate issued by National Cadet Corps (if applicable)
    • Recent passport-size colour photograph in original JPG/TIFF format
  • If any scanned document is not legible/readable, the application will be rejected. Candidates must take a printout of the application and carry it while appearing for SSB interview.
  • The application once submitted will be final and no request for amendments/change will be entertained.
  • Multiple applications for this course by any candidate will lead to cancellation of his/her candidature.

Common Application Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates make avoidable errors while applying for defence jobs in India 2026. Based on general guidance for government online application processes, here are common mistakes to be careful about:

  • Uploading blurred, low-resolution, or incorrectly formatted photographs and documents - these lead to rejection.
  • Entering incorrect personal details that do not match your Matriculation Certificate.
  • Selecting a branch for which you do not meet the educational qualification or stream requirement.
  • Failing to include CGPA/marks for all required semesters as specified for your course type.
  • Changing your registered mobile number or e-mail address after submission - you may miss SSB shortlisting communications.
  • Submitting multiple application forms - this will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Not taking a printout of the submitted application - candidates must carry it to the SSB interview.

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected Young Professionals work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement enriches both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience within India's financial policy ecosystem.

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

RBI Young Professional Recruitment 2026 Apply Link & Process

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 - Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 - Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 - Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 - Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application - [Post Code] - [Your Full Name]"
Example: YP Application - YP0626FIN01 - Ramesh Kumar

Step 5 - Send the Application:
Email your complete application to [email protected] before the deadline.

Step 6 - Applying for Multiple Posts:
If you wish to apply for more than one position, send a separate email for each post. Each email must include a complete, independent set of all required documents.

  • [Apply Online] - Send your application email to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] - Download the official notification and Annexure-VI application proforma from www.rbi.org.in

Selection Process for RBI YP 2026

Submitting a complete and eligible application is only the first step. The selection process for RBI Young Professionals involves multiple stages, and meeting the minimum eligibility is not a guarantee of progression.

Stage 1 - Preliminary Screening: A screening committee reviews all received applications against the eligibility criteria and the quality of supporting documents. The Bank reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview.

Stage 2 - Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit and verify original documents related to age, educational qualifications, and experience.

Stage 3 - Interview: Shortlisted candidates will receive an interview call letter via email only. No physical call letters will be sent by post. Candidates must make their own travel and accommodation arrangements for the interview.

Reserve List: RBI maintains a reserve list of suitable candidates, valid for one year from the date of publication of the selection list.

RBI's decision regarding shortlisting, interview, and all aspects of engagement is final. No correspondence will be entertained in this regard.

SBI BMO Selection Process 2026

The selection process for the SBI Bank Medical Officer post involves three stages - an Online Written Test, an Interview, and a Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) - with the final merit list based on 70% weightage to the written test and 30% to the interview. Candidates wondering how marks are normalized can note that the Bank combines scores from both stages using this 70:30 ratio before preparing the final merit list, circle-wise and category-wise.

  1. Online Written Test – Tentatively scheduled for August 2026 across multiple centres nationwide; call letters will be issued via the Bank's website, SMS, and email.
  2. Shortlisting – Based on Professional Knowledge cut-off marks, plus minimum qualifying marks in General Aptitude sections.
  3. Interview – Carries 100 marks; conducted for a category-wise adequate number of shortlisted candidates.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) – Conducted for provisionally selected candidates before joining; candidates with 10th/12th mark sheets showing the relevant local language as a subject are exempted.
  5. Final Result & Wait List – A circle-wise and category-wise wait list valid for one year (or until a fresh advertisement, whichever is earlier) is maintained for non-joining or termination cases.

  • If the university provides a conversion formula: Use the university's own conversion and obtain a certificate from the university confirming the equivalent percentage. Submit this certificate at the time of interview.
  • If the university does not provide a conversion formula: A minimum CGPA of 6 on a 10-point scale will be treated as equivalent to 60%. For scales other than 10-point, the score will be prorated accordingly.

Eligibility Criteria for ESIC Professor 2026

Understanding who qualifies is essential before applying. The eligibility conditions differ slightly for medical and non-medical candidates, and both must meet specific experience thresholds recognized by the National Medical Commission (NMC).

Age Limit

  • Maximum age: 50 years as on the closing date (27 July 2026)
  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years relaxation (upper limit: 55 years)
  • OBC candidates: 3 years relaxation (upper limit: 53 years)
  • PwBD candidates: 10 years relaxation (upper limit: 60 years; SC/ST PwBD: 15 years, OBC PwBD: 13 years) - subject to a maximum of 56 years
  • ESIC/Government employees: 5 years relaxation
  • Ex-Servicemen: 5 years relaxation, subject to minimum 6 months service after attestation

Educational Qualifications

For Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A recognized medical qualification included in the First or Second Schedule or Part-II of the Third Schedule to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
  2. A postgraduate qualification - MD (Doctor of Medicine) or MS (Master of Surgery) or a recognized equivalent in the respective subject or allied discipline.

For Non-Medical Candidates (Essential):

  1. A Master's Degree in the concerned subject or allied discipline.
  2. A Doctorate degree from a recognized university in the respective subject or allied discipline.

Teaching Experience

Candidates must fulfill one of the following:

Option A: Four years of teaching experience as a Reader or Associate Professor in a recognized medical college in the concerned specialty.

Option B: Three years of teaching experience as an Associate Professor in a recognized medical college, plus a minimum of four research publications in indexed or national journals - published as the First Author in journals of National Associations or Societies of the respective specialties. Of these, at least two publications must have been during the tenure as Associate Professor.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Pay Scale and Benefits

The Professor post carries Pay Level-13 in the Central Government Pay Matrix, with a pay range of ₹1,23,100 to ₹2,15,900 per month. In addition to basic pay, selected candidates are entitled to:

Promotional avenues are available under the Dynamic Assured Career Progression (DACP) guidelines of the Government of India.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The selection for ESIC Professor 2026 is based entirely on an interview conducted by a Selection Board. There is no written examination. Candidates who have applied will be assessed on experience and merit before being called.

Step-by-Step Selection Process

  1. Application Submission - Send the completed application form by Speed Post to reach ESIC Regional Office, Delhi by 27 July 2026.
  2. Shortlisting - If the number of applications is large, ESIC will shortlist candidates based on teaching experience at Associate Professor/Reader level or higher, beyond the minimum eligibility. Shortlisting is based solely on information and certificates submitted with the application - no subsequent documents will be accepted.
  3. Interview - Shortlisted candidates appear before the Selection Board at a venue decided by ESIC.
  4. Minimum Qualifying Marks in Interview (out of 100):
    • UR / EWS: 50 marks
    • OBC: 45 marks
    • SC / ST / PwBD: 40 marks
  5. Tie-Breaking (if scores are equal):
    • First: Elder candidate preferred.
    • Second: Candidate who passed the essential postgraduate degree earlier.
    • Third: Candidate who completed internship earlier.
  6. Reserve List - ESIC may draw a Reserve List as per UPSC guidelines.
  7. Probation - Selected candidates will be appointed on probation as per rules.

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply Step-by-Step

Candidates cannot apply online for this recruitment. The application is purely offline via Speed Post.

  1. Download the application form from the official ESIC notification (available at www.esic.gov.in).
  2. Fill in the application form completely in block letters. Ensure at least 10 state preferences for posting are listed.
  3. Attach a recent self-attested passport-size photograph firmly (not stapled) on the application form.
  4. Prepare a Demand Draft/Banker's Cheque of ₹500 (where applicable) in favour of 'ESI Fund Account No. 2', payable at Delhi. Write your name and address on the reverse side.
  5. Attach self-attested copies of all required documents (see Documents Required section below).
  6. Place the DD/BC pinned or clipped (not stapled or tagged) at the top of the application.
  7. Superscribe the envelope: "Application for the post of Professor for Medical Institutions"
  8. Send by Speed Post to: Regional Office Delhi, ESI Corporation DDA Complex Cum Office, 3rd & 4th Floor,, Rajendra Bhawan, Rajendra Place,, New Delhi - 110008
  9. Ensure delivery by 27 July 2026. ESIC will not be responsible for postal delays.

Documents Required with Application

Every applicant must submit self-attested copies of the following documents. Incomplete applications are liable to be summarily rejected without communication.

  • Demand Draft / Banker's Cheque (original, pinned at top)
  • Passport-size photograph (recent, firmly pasted)
  • Date of Birth proof - Matriculation/10th certificate or mark sheet (School Leaving Certificate accepted for Tamil Nadu and Kerala candidates only)
  • Degree certificates and mark sheets for all academic years (or provisional certificate with mark sheets)
  • Experience certificates from each employer, clearly stating duration, nature of work, and basic/consolidated pay
  • Research publication certificates/testimonials
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in the prescribed central government format
  • OBC Non-Creamy Layer declaration (Annexure-II)
  • Certificate of Disability (PwBD candidates) in the prescribed format - minimum 40% disability
  • Ex-Servicemen certificate in prescribed proforma (if applicable)
  • Declaration that current employer has been informed (for serving government/ESIC employees)
  • Name-change supporting documents (if applicable - marriage certificate, divorce decree, or Deed Poll/Affidavit as appropriate)

ESIC Professor Recruitment 2026 - Posting Locations

Selected candidates are liable to be posted anywhere in India. ESIC operates medical colleges and PGIMSRs across the following states, and applicants must indicate at least 10 state preferences in the application form:

Rajasthan, Bihar, Karnataka, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Haryana, Telangana, Delhi, Maharashtra, Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Jharkhand, and Gujarat.

Preference will be considered subject to administrative requirements and cannot be claimed as a matter of right.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

These pitfalls are frequently responsible for application rejections - check each before dispatch:

  1. Not attaching the DD/BC - Applications without the prescribed fee from paying categories are summarily rejected with no appeal.
  2. Submitting multiple applications under different categories - All such applications will be rejected outright.
  3. Requesting to add experience after submission - Only experience with certificates submitted with the original application is considered for shortlisting.
  4. Using the wrong DD format - Online transfers, UPI, or cheques other than DD/Banker's Cheque are not accepted.
  5. Not superscribing the envelope - Failure to write the prescribed text on the cover may result in the application being overlooked.
  6. Unsigned application form - Unsigned or incomplete forms are liable to rejection without notice.
  7. Sending experience certificates without duration/pay details - Certificates must clearly state start date, end date, nature of duties, and pay. Vague letters will not be counted.
  8. Listing fewer than 10 state preferences - The notification specifically advises candidates to fill at least 10 options.
  9. Tampered or altered documents - Any forgery or alteration will lead to cancellation and potential legal action.
  10. Relying on postal speed alone - Send applications well in advance; postal delays are the applicant's responsibility.

How to Apply for Sarkari Job Online 2026

  1. Find the right Sarkari Job: Use the vacancy table or sector links above on OnlyJobs. Filter by your qualification — 10th, 12th, Graduate, or Engineering. Check the last date and eligibility carefully.

  2. Read the official notification: Click on the job listing to open the official notification PDF. Read all eligibility conditions — age limit, educational qualification, experience, category relaxations.

  3. Visit the official recruitment website: Never apply through third-party sites. Use the direct official link provided on OnlyJobs. Look for "Apply Online" or "Register" on the official portal.

  4. Register / Create account: Sign up using your valid email ID and active mobile number. Keep your Aadhaar, bank account details, and email accessible.

  5. Fill the application form: Enter personal details, educational qualifications, category (General/OBC/SC/ST/EWS), address, and other required information accurately.

  6. Upload documents: Scan and upload recent passport-size photograph, signature, 10th certificate (for DOB proof), educational certificates, caste certificate (if applicable). Check file size and format (JPG/PDF as specified).

  7. Pay application fee: Pay via Net Banking, UPI, Debit/Credit Card as applicable. Some categories (SC/ST/PwD/Women) may be exempted from fee. Keep the payment receipt.

  8. Submit and save confirmation: Review all details before final submission. After submitting, download the application printout / PDF confirmation with your registration number. Store it safely for admit card, exam, and future reference.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs

Eligibility for forest department jobs depends on the post, state and recruitment authority. Below is a general idea of qualification and age for popular posts like Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer. Candidates should always check the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Forest Guard / Field Guard / Forest Watcher / Beat Guard: Usually 10th pass or 12th pass from a recognized board, knowledge of local language, and basic physical standards as per state rules.
  • Forester / Section Forest Officer / Deputy Forest Ranger: Generally 12th pass or graduate in any stream or science-related subjects, with physical standards and sometimes driving or technical skills depending on the post.
  • Forest Range Officer (RFO) / Forest Ranger / ACF: Normally graduate degree in Science, Agriculture, Forestry, Environmental Science, Engineering or related disciplines, with higher physical standards and sometimes a competitive exam similar to state PCS level.
  • IFS / Indian Forest Service and senior posts (DCF, CF, CCF, PCCF): Filled through UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination and promotions, requiring a graduate degree and all-India competitive selection.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • Forest Guard / Forester / Field Guard: Minimum age is usually 18 years and maximum age is around 27–30 years, with age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, Ex-servicemen and other categories as per government rules.
  • Forest Range Officer / ACF and higher competitive posts: Age limit often ranges from 21 to 32 years (varies by recruitment), with relaxations for reserved categories.
  • Exact age limit, cut-off date and relaxation details always depend on the particular notification, so candidates should verify from the official advertisement before applying.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The selection process for Forest Department Jobs 2026 typically includes written examinations, physical tests and document verification. Some posts also conduct medical examination and walking tests due to the demanding nature of field duties.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  • Written Exam: Most Forest Guard, Forester and Forest Range Officer recruitments start with a written exam based on objective-type questions (MCQs).
  • PET / PST (Physical Efficiency Test / Physical Standard Test): Candidates who qualify written exam are called for running, walking test, height, chest measurement and other physical parameters as per post and gender.
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates of age, qualification, caste, residence, sports/NCC and other documents mentioned in the notification.
  • Medical Examination: Many forest posts require medical fitness to ensure candidates can perform field duties in forests, wildlife areas and difficult terrain.

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

Typical syllabus for written exam may include:

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs (national, state-level, environment and forest-related topics)
  • General Hindi / English or regional language (grammar, comprehension, vocabulary)
  • General Mathematics / Quantitative Aptitude (up to 10th or 12th level)
  • General Science and Environmental Studies (forest, wildlife, biodiversity, conservation, climate, basic biology)
  • Reasoning Ability (logical and analytical reasoning)

Exact subject-wise marks, number of questions, negative marking and exam duration will be given in the respective forest department notification.

How to Apply for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Most Forest Department Jobs 2026 applications are accepted either online through official websites or offline via prescribed application forms. Candidates should carefully read the official notification before filling the form.

Online Application Process

  1. Visit the official website of the recruiting body (State Forest Department, State PSC, Staff Selection Board or other government portal).
  2. Find the latest link for Forest Guard / Forester / Forest Range Officer / other forest posts and open the detailed advertisement.
  3. Complete the registration process with basic details like name, mobile number, email ID and verify using OTP if required.
  4. Fill the online application form with personal, educational, address and category information exactly as per documents.
  5. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature and other certificates in the prescribed format and size.
  6. Pay the application fee online through Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card or UPI as per your convenience.
  7. Finally, submit the form and take a printout or PDF of the submitted application and payment receipt for future reference.

Documents Required & Application Fee

  • Recent passport size photograph and signature (scanned)
  • Class 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates
  • Degree / Diploma certificates for graduate-level posts
  • Caste / Category certificate (SC, ST, OBC, EWS, etc.)
  • Domicile / Residence certificate if required by the state
  • NCC, Sports, Ex-serviceman and other quota certificates if applicable
  • Valid ID proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, Passport, etc.)

Why Choose Forest Department Jobs?

Forest department jobs are popular among candidates who love nature, wildlife and field work. These jobs offer job security, government benefits and a chance to work in forest conservation, wildlife protection, eco-tourism and community development.

  • Stable government job with regular salary, pension/NPS and allowances
  • Opportunity to work in forests, wildlife sanctuaries, national parks and protected areas
  • Contribution to environment protection, afforestation and biodiversity conservation
  • Good promotion avenues from Forest Guard to Forester, Forest Range Officer and higher posts in many states.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

What is OnlyJobs?

OnlyJobs is the common Hindi-English term for the outcome of any Indian government recruitment or board examination - the published result, merit list, or scorecard that tells a candidate whether they have qualified. Around this single moment sits an entire cycle: the recruitment notification, the online application form, the admit card (hall ticket), the exam, the answer key, the cut-off marks, and finally the result and document verification. When people search for a OnlyJobs, सरकारी रिजल्ट, or a OnlyJobs result, they are usually looking for one trusted place that tracks every one of these stages without sending them to dozens of separate official portals.

OnlyJobs has done exactly that since 2011. This page brings together the latest OnlyJobs results, admit cards, answer keys, and online-form notifications from national bodies such as SSC, UPSC, the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB), and banking recruiters like IBPS and SBI, alongside every State Public Service Commission across India's 28 states and 8 union territories. Each listing links to a detailed page with the official source, important dates, and a direct download link - so you can move from "is my result out?" to "result downloaded" in a couple of clicks.

How to Check Your OnlyJobs 2026 Online (Step-by-Step)

Checking a OnlyJobs result takes only a few minutes once you know the steps:

  • Find your exam in the Latest Results section below, or use the search bar to type the exam name (e.g., "SSC CGL" or "RRB NTPC").
  • Read the result summary to confirm the post, organisation, and result date.
  • Open the official portal link provided in the article (e.g., ssc.nic.in, upsc.gov.in).
  • Enter your Roll Number or Registration ID along with your date of birth, as required by that exam body.
  • Download or screenshot your result/scorecard for future reference - most government portals remove results after a few weeks.
  • Check the next stage (cut-off, document verification, interview call letter) - OnlyJobs lists this under the same exam tag so you can track the full recruitment cycle.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 has been officially announced by the ISRO Telemetry Tracking & Command Network (ISTRAC), Bengaluru under the Department of Space, Government of India. A total of 95  apprentice positions - across Graduate, Diploma, and ITI (Trade) categories - are open for one-year training under Advt. No. ISTRAC:01:2026 dated 22 June 2026. The last date to apply via email is 31 July 2026. Only candidates who passed their qualifying course in 2024, 2025, or 2026 are eligible.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Notification Out

ISTRAC has released the official apprenticeship notification under the Apprentices Act 1961 and Amendment Act 1963. The advertisement covers three training locations - Bengaluru (headquarters), Lucknow, and Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) - with positions distributed across engineering and commercial disciplines. Candidates must apply separately via dedicated email IDs for each location they wish to be considered at.

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentices Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

The ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice 2026 eligibility rules are strict and candidates should verify each condition carefully before applying. Only those who passed their qualifying examination as regular candidates are eligible - correspondence, private, or sandwich course degrees are not accepted. Candidates currently pursuing higher studies (e.g., B.E./B.Tech for diploma holders) are also not eligible.

Educational Qualification

  • Graduate Apprentice (GA01-GA06): B.E./B.Tech in the relevant engineering discipline from any recognised University. For GA07 (Library Science): MLISc. (Library and Information Science).
  • Diploma Apprentice (DA01-DA06): Diploma in Engineering awarded by a recognised State Board in the respective discipline. DA06 requires Diploma in Commercial Practice.
  • ITI Trade Apprentice (TA01-TA05): ITI certificate in the concerned trade from any recognised University.

Year of Passing Condition

Candidates must have passed their qualifying course in 2024, 2025, or 2026 only. Candidates are also required to join within 3 years of acquiring the degree/diploma/ITI (calculated from the month and year of passing as stated in the certificate). If this three-year window lapses before the date of joining, the candidature will be cancelled.

NATS Registration (Mandatory)

Every candidate must register on the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) portal at nats.education.gov.in before applying. The NATS Enrolment Number must be included in the email application. Applications without a valid NATS Enrolment Number are liable to be rejected. Candidates must upload their Degree/Diploma/ITI certificate and a valid government-issued ID on the NATS portal during registration.

Other Eligibility Conditions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • Ex-apprentices, candidates currently undergoing apprenticeship elsewhere, or candidates with one year or more of work experience in Government/Public/Private Sector as on the date of joining are not eligible.
  • Combining this apprenticeship with any other institution's apprenticeship is not permitted.
  • Courses must be recognised by any University in India or State Boards.

Also read: SBI PO 2026 Notification PDF Out - Apply Online for 1,500 Probationary Officer Posts

Application Fee

ISRO ISTRAC has not prescribed any application fee for this apprenticeship recruitment. The application process is free of cost for all candidates across all categories.

How to Apply - Email Only

Applications for ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice 2026 are accepted exclusively via email - no online portal, no postal applications. Candidates must send their application to the dedicated email ID of the location they are applying for. If applying to multiple locations, separate emails must be sent to each location's dedicated email address.

Step-by-Step Application Process

  1. Register on the NATS portal at nats.education.gov.in and obtain your NATS Enrolment Number.
  2. Prepare scanned copies of: Final Degree/Diploma/ITI Certificate (or final year/semester mark sheet if certificate is awaited), Class X and Pre-University marks card/certificate, and NATS Enrolment Number.
  3. Compose an email to the correct location-specific email ID (see table below).
  4. In the Subject Line, mention the Post Code - e.g., "Application for Post Code: GA02".
  5. In the body of the email, clearly state: Name, Contact Number, Degree/Diploma/ITI Details, Year of Passing, and NATS Enrolment ID.
  6. Attach all required documents and send before 31 July 2026.

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentices Recruitment 2026- Selection Process

The ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice selection process consists of document scrutiny followed by an in-person interview. There is no written examination. Candidates shortlisted after screening will be called to the respective location for document verification and interview, and a merit panel will be drawn based on academic scores and interview performance.

  1. Application Scrutiny: Submitted emails are screened for eligibility and completeness.
  2. Shortlisting: Eligible candidates are shortlisted based on academic percentage and other criteria.
  3. Document Verification / Interview: Shortlisted candidates are called to the respective centre. Interviews are held at Lucknow (27-28 August 2026), Sri Vijaya Puram (03-04 September 2026), and Bengaluru (09-11 September 2026). Reporting time at all centres is 8:30 AM.
  4. Panel Formation: A merit panel is prepared based on Degree/Diploma/ITI academic scores and interview performance.
  5. Final Induction: Apprentices are inducted against vacant positions strictly based on their rank in the panel. Selected candidates are informed only via email.

Important: Candidates shortlisted for document verification/interview are not eligible for Travelling Allowance (TA). No request to change the place of interview or place of posting will be entertained.

ISRO ISTRAC Apprentices Recruitment 2026 - Stipend / Monthly Salary

Candidates selected under ISRO ISTRAC Apprentice Recruitment 2026 will receive a monthly stipend as fixed under the Apprentices Act. The stipend varies by apprentice category as follows:

Category Monthly Stipend
Graduate Apprentice Trainee ₹12,300/-
Diploma Apprentice Trainee ₹10,900/-
ITI Trade Apprentice ₹9,600/-

Apprentices should note that there is no claim for regular employment in ISRO or any other Centre/Unit under the Department of Space after completion of the one-year training period.

Documents Required at Interview

Candidates called for document verification must carry all original documents to the venue. Failure to produce any of the required originals will result in disqualification from the apprenticeship training.

  • Proof of date of birth
  • Class X and Pre-University marks card/certificate
  • Final Degree/Diploma/ITI Certificate or final year mark sheet (if certificate is awaited)
  • Mark sheets of all years/semesters of qualifying course
  • NATS Enrolment ID
  • Caste/Tribe/Disability certificate in prescribed format (if applicable)
  • Medical Fitness Certificate (to be submitted at the time of joining)

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many eligible candidates get rejected due to avoidable errors in the email application. Review these common pitfalls carefully before sending your application to ISRO ISTRAC.

  • Wrong email ID for location: Each training location has a separate email ID. Sending your Bengaluru application to the Lucknow email ID will result in rejection. Double-check the email address against the location you are targeting.
  • Missing Post Code in subject line: The subject line must clearly mention the Post Code (e.g., "Application for Post Code: GA02"). Emails without the Post Code may not be processed.
  • No NATS Enrolment Number: Registration on nats.education.gov.in is mandatory before applying. Not including the NATS Enrolment Number in the email body is grounds for rejection.
  • Passing year outside 2024-2026: If you passed your qualifying course before 2024, you are not eligible regardless of your marks or experience.
  • Applying with a private or sandwich course degree: Degrees obtained via private mode, correspondence, or sandwich courses are explicitly not accepted. Only regular candidates qualify.
  • Currently pursuing higher studies: Diploma holders currently doing B.E./B.Tech, or graduates currently doing M.E./M.Tech, are not eligible.
  • One year or more of work experience: Candidates with one year or more of work experience in Government, Public, or Private Sector as on the joining date are not eligible.
  • Applying to multiple locations in one email: Send separate emails to separate location-specific IDs. Do not combine locations in a single email.

State Bank of India has released the official notification for SBI PO Recruitment 2026, inviting online applications for 1500 Probationary Officer (PO) vacancies under Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09. SBI PO Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF Out

SBI's Central Recruitment & Promotion Department, Corporate Centre, Mumbai, has officially issued the SBI PO Recruitment 2026 notification, dated 18 June 2026, under Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09. The notification announces 1500 Probationary Officer vacancies and lays out the complete eligibility criteria, exam pattern, and application process for the post. Candidates can access the PDF Download Link of the detailed advertisement directly from SBI's official careers page before starting their online application, since the notification advises every applicant to read it carefully before applying.

  • Download SBI PO Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

Why Join SBI as a Probationary Officer?

This section answers why thousands of graduates target the SBI PO exam every year as one of India's most sought-after banking careers. Selected candidates step into leadership-track roles from day one, with the bank highlighting accelerated career progression, nationwide and international postings, structured leadership-development training, and exposure to modern digital banking operations. The role also comes with strong job security, an attractive compensation package, and a clear promotion path that can take meritorious officers up to Top Management Grade over time.

SBI PO Eligibility Criteria 2026

Eligibility for the SBI PO post is built on two pillars: an age limit checked as on a fixed cut-off date, and an academic qualification checked as on a separate, later cut-off date. Candidates must satisfy both conditions independently to be considered eligible for this recruitment.

SBI PO Age Limit 2026: 21 to 30 Years

Candidates applying for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 must be not below 21 years and not above 30 years as on 01 April 2026, meaning they must have been born between 02 April 1996 and 01 April 2005 (both dates inclusive). Age relaxation is available to specific categories, but the notification clarifies that cumulative age relaxation across multiple categories is not permitted.

SBI PO Educational Qualification 2026

Candidates need a Graduation degree in any discipline from a recognised university, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government, as on 30 September 2026. Final-year or final-semester students can also apply provisionally, but they must produce proof of having passed the graduation examination on or before 30 September 2026 if shortlisted for interview. Candidates holding professional qualifications such as Medical, Engineering, Chartered Accountancy, or Cost Accountancy, as well as those with an Integrated Dual Degree (IDD) passed by the cut-off date, are also eligible.

SBI PO Application Fee 2026

The application fee for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 is Rs 750 for Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates, while SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted from paying any fee. This fee is non-refundable once paid and cannot be carried forward or held in reserve for any other examination, so candidates should confirm their category and details before making the payment.

CIBIL Score Requirement for SBI PO Candidates

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment relates to credit history, since SBI PO is a banking role with financial responsibility. Candidates who have defaulted on repayment under any loan, NBFC, or financial institution arrangement, including credit card dues, and whose accounts reflect adverse credit history in CIBIL or another recognised credit agency, must regularise or repay all outstanding dues on or before the date of joining the Bank. If the adverse status has not been updated in CIBIL records by the joining date, candidates must either get the status updated or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender confirming there are no outstanding dues; failure to do so will render the candidate ineligible and the offer of appointment will be withdrawn. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying.

SBI PO Selection Process 2026: Prelims, Mains & Interview

Selection for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 follows a three-phase process: Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Main Examination, and Phase-III Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview. Candidates must clear each phase to be considered for the next, and only the marks from Phase-II and Phase-III are carried forward to prepare the final merit list.

Phase-I: SBI PO Prelims Exam Pattern 2026

The Preliminary Examination is an online objective test carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 1 hour, with separate timing for each of its three sections. There is no sectional cut-off in the Preliminary Exam, but a category-wise merit list is prepared based on the aggregate score, and candidates numbering approximately 10 times the vacancies in each category are shortlisted for the Main Exam.

Section No. of Questions Marks Duration
English Language 40 - 20 minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 - 20 minutes
Reasoning Ability 30 - 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 hour

Phase-II: SBI PO Mains Exam Pattern 2026

The Main Examination is conducted online and consists of an Objective Test of 200 marks and a Descriptive Test of 30 marks, taken together in 3 hours 30 minutes. The descriptive paper is administered immediately after the objective test, and candidates must type their answers directly on the computer.

Section No. of Questions Max Marks Duration
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 40 60 50 minutes
Data Analysis & Interpretation 30 60 45 minutes
General Awareness / Economy / Banking Knowledge 60 60 45 minutes
English Language 40 20 40 minutes
Objective Test Total 170 200 3 hours
Descriptive Test (Email / Situation Analysis / Report or Precis Writing) 3 30 30 minutes
Grand Total 230 3 hours 30 minutes  

Each candidate must score a minimum qualifying mark in every individual section, including the descriptive paper, with sectional cut-offs decided by the Bank based on vacancies. A category-wise merit list is then prepared from the aggregate Main Exam score, and candidates numbering approximately 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for Phase-III.

There is also a penalty for wrong answers in both the Preliminary and Main objective tests: for every wrong answer, 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question is deducted, while unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview

Shortlisted candidates undergo a Psychometric Test for personality profiling, followed by a Group Exercise (20 marks) and a Personal Interview (30 marks), totalling 50 marks. The Psychometric Test findings are shared with the interview panel to give a fuller perspective on each candidate, and all questions in this test are mandatory.

Final Merit List and Normalisation

The marks from Phase-II (Main Exam, both Objective and Descriptive) and Phase-III (Group Exercise & Interview) are normalised to 100 marks each before being combined into the final merit list; marks from the Preliminary Exam are not added at this stage.

Component Maximum Marks Normalised Marks
Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) 230 75
Group Exercise & Interview 50 25
Total 280 100

If two or more candidates score identical marks at the cut-off point in the final merit list, they are ranked according to age in descending order, meaning the older candidate is placed higher.

SBI PO Syllabus 2026: Check Exam Pattern and Syllabus Details Here

SBI PO Apply Online 2026: Step-by-Step Registration Guide

Candidates can apply for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 only in online mode, from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026; no other mode of application is accepted. Before starting, candidates must have a valid personal email ID and mobile number kept active until the declaration of the final result, since all call letters and result-related communication will be sent there.

  1. Visit SBI's official careers portal at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings (also accessible at https://bank.sbi/web/careers/current-openings) and locate Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09.
  2. Download and carefully read the detailed advertisement PDF before proceeding with registration.
  3. Click Apply Online and open the registration form under "Current Openings."
  4. Keep scanned images ready in advance: your photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB), signature (140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB), left-hand thumb impression (3cm x 3cm, 240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB), and a hand-written declaration (10cm x 5cm, 800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB), all in JPG/JPEG format.
  5. Fill in the application form carefully; you can save a partially completed form, which generates a provisional registration number and password that you must note down to resume later.
  6. Capture a live photograph through your webcam or mobile phone during registration, as this is mandatory in addition to the uploaded photograph.
  7. Recheck every field for accuracy, since no edits are allowed once the form is finally submitted.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI; SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt from the fee.
  9. On successful payment, download and print the e-receipt and application form for your records.
  10. Complete your application well before 8 July 2026 to avoid last-minute technical issues caused by heavy website traffic.

You can also apply directly through the dedicated SBI PO registration link at https://ibpsreg.ibps.in/sbipojun26/.

SBI PO Salary 2026: Pay Scale and CTC

Selected candidates for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 will draw a starting basic pay of Rs 48,480, plus 4 advance increments, in the Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I) pay scale of 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920. In addition to basic pay, officers are eligible for Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), City Compensatory Allowance (CCA), Provident Fund, the National Pension System (NPS), Leave Fare Concession (LFC), medical facilities, lease rental facility, and other allowances as per the Bank's prevailing rules. The approximate CTC at the initial pay scale for the Mumbai Centre works out to Rs 21.97 Lacs.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Joining, Bond and Probation Period

Selected candidates must complete a basic banking knowledge online course before joining and will be designated as Probationary Officers, placed on probation for two years with continuous performance assessment. At the time of joining, candidates must execute a bond of Rs 2.00 Lacs, committing to serve the Bank for a minimum period of three years; this bond is invoked if the candidate resigns before completing three years of service. Officers who clear the probation assessment standards are confirmed in JMGS-I, and SBI's promotion policy offers a path for high-performing officers to reach senior and top management grades, including opportunities for international postings.

SBI PO Exam Preparation 2026: Strategy, Exam Pattern, Selection Process & Study Plan

Documents and Identity Proof Required at Examination

Candidates must carry specific documents at each stage of the selection process, and missing or mismatched documents can lead to disqualification. At the time of the Preliminary and Main Examinations, candidates must bring a valid photo identity proof such as a Passport, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Driving Licence, Voter's ID Card, or Bank Passbook with an attested photograph, along with a self-attested photocopy. The notification also specifies that candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card, as SBI conducts online Aadhaar verification at different stages of the selection process, and biometric verification (photo and thumb impression/IRIS scan) may also be carried out.

For the Main Exam specifically, candidates must bring the duly authenticated Original Preliminary Exam Call Letter along with the authenticated ID proof copy, the Main Exam Call Letter, and two additional photographs identical to the one used during registration; candidates without these will not be allowed to appear. Use of mobile phones or any electronic devices inside the examination or interview premises is strictly banned and can lead to disqualification.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for SBI PO 2026

Many otherwise eligible candidates lose out due to small, avoidable errors during the application process, so it helps to be deliberate at each step. Keep your photograph, signature, thumb impression, and hand-written declaration within the exact pixel dimensions and file-size ranges specified, since uploads outside these limits will trigger an error and block submission; also remember that signatures and the hand-written declaration in capital letters are not accepted.

Avoid waiting until the closing date of 8 July 2026 to register, as heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions, and SBI does not take responsibility for applications that fail to go through for this reason. Double-check your category selection before final submission, since no change of category is permitted at any stage after registration, and incorrectly chosen reserved or unreserved status cannot be corrected later. If an online payment fails or appears incomplete, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the transaction went through, since the fee is strictly non-refundable. Finally, save your provisional registration number and password immediately after saving your form, and keep multiple copies of your registration photograph ready, as these are needed at every subsequent stage of the selection process.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 - Age Relaxation

The standard age relaxations applicable to these posts are as follows. SC candidates receive 5 additional years, OBC candidates receive 3 additional years, and all PwBD candidates receive 10 additional years over and above their category relaxation. For certain posts with a base upper limit of 50 years, the PwBD maximum is capped at 56 years - this applies to the Regional Director (NCONF), Professor Sugar Engineering (NSI), Principal (A&N), and Consultant Ophthalmologist (UT Ladakh). UPSC may relax qualifications and experience at its discretion in writing for candidates otherwise well qualified.

Special Condition - UT Ladakh Posts (Posts 60-70)

All posts under the Administration of the Union Territory of Ladakh are exclusively open to Domiciles of UT Ladakh. A valid Domicile Certificate issued by the Tehsildar under the Ladakh Civil Services Decentralization and Recruitment Rules, 2025 (published in the Gazette of India on 03.06.2025) is mandatory. Two eligible categories exist: Category A (holders of or eligible for Ladakh Resident Certificate) and Category B (children of LRC holders or those eligible). Reservation is governed by the Jammu and Kashmir Reservation Act, 2004, as extended to UT Ladakh and amended by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Regulation, 2025 (No. 1 of 2025), and further by the Ladakh Reservation (Amendment) Rules, 2025 notified vide S.O. 77 dated 27.06.2025.

UPSC Recruitment 2026- How to Apply

The following steps reflect the application process described in the notification for UPSC's ORA portal.

  1. Visit the UPSC Online Recruitment Application portal at https://upsconline.nic.in/ora/.
  2. Register as a new user if you do not already have an account, or log in with your existing credentials.
  3. Select Advertisement No. 06/2026 from the list and choose the relevant post.
  4. Fill in all required personal, educational, and experience details accurately.
  5. Upload your photograph, signature, and required supporting documents.
  6. Submit the application and save the system-generated confirmation receipt with your registration number.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes

Candidates applying through the UPSC ORA portal can avoid common problems by following these general practices. Photograph and signature files must meet the portal's specified size and dimension requirements; uploading files that are too large or in an unsupported format is among the most frequent causes of incomplete applications. If a payment transaction fails, wait for the system to confirm the failure before attempting to pay again - making duplicate payments can cause complications that require manual resolution. Use an updated, stable browser on a desktop or laptop for the best experience; mobile browsers sometimes fail to render form fields correctly. Save your registration number and password immediately after registering, as the portal requires them for every subsequent login. Do not attempt to submit your application on the final day of the application window, as heavy traffic on the server is common and can cause timeouts or session errors.

SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 - Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The examination consists of two parts: Part-I (Computer Based & Written Examination, 300 marks) and Part-II (Evaluation of Record of Service/APARs, 100 marks). Total marks = 400. Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance in all parts. This is a competitive and not a qualifying examination.

Part-I: Computer Based & Written Examination (300 Marks)

Subject Paper No. No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time Duration Mode
General Awareness Paper-I 100 200 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Computer Based Examination (Objective Type Multiple Choice)
English Language and Comprehension 100
Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Paper-II -- 100 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Written Examination (Descriptive / Conventional type)

Note: There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in Computer Based Examination (Paper-I). Candidates have to attempt the examination in the language (English/Hindi) as opted in the online Application Form. There will be no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates.

Marks 100 marks earmarked for evaluation of record of service (APARs - Annual Performance Assessment Reports)
