Syllabus of the Examination

Paper Subject Syllabus / Topics
Paper-I (CBE) General Awareness Questions aimed at testing General Awareness of the environment around and its application to society. Current events; matters of everyday observations and experience in their scientific aspect; History, Culture, Geography, Economics, Science, General Politics and Scientific research relating to India and neighboring countries.
Paper-I (CBE) English Language and Comprehension Understanding and knowledge of English language: Vocabulary, spelling, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, sentence completion, phrases and idiomatic use of words, comprehension of a passage. Questions will be of matriculation level.
Paper-II (Written/Descriptive) Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Knowledge of office procedure in the Secretariat and Attached Offices; ability to write and understand notes and drafts. Candidates are required to study the Manual of Office Procedure (including Ministry of Railways version), the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Hand Book of orders issued by Ministry of Home Affairs regarding use of Hindi for official purpose of the Union, and Reservation Policy for SC/STs in services and orders issued by Government thereon from time to time.

Mode of Selection

Step 1 Based on performance in Paper-I (CBE) of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of Paper-II (Descriptive Paper) of Part-I. Candidates not qualifying Paper-I will not be evaluated for Paper-II and will not be considered for further selection.
Step 2 Based on aggregate performance in Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of record of service (Part-II). Candidates not qualifying Part-I aggregate will not be eligible for Part-II evaluation.
Step 3 Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance of candidates in Paper-I (CBE) + Paper-II (Descriptive) of Part-I and Part-II (APAR Evaluation). The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I.

Tie-Breaking Rules

1st Tie-Break Marks obtained in Paper-II (Descriptive)
2nd Tie-Break Marks obtained in part (b) of Paper-I (English Language and Comprehension)
3rd Tie-Break Date of birth - older candidates placed higher
4th Tie-Break Alphabetical order in which the names of the candidates appear

How to Apply for SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025

The Application Form must be submitted only in online mode on the SSC website https://ssc.gov.in. The process consists of two parts: (i) One Time Registration (OTR) and (ii) Filling of online Application Form for the Examination. Candidates who have not generated their OTR on the new website (https://ssc.gov.in) will be required to do so; the earlier OTR generated on the old website (https://ssc.nic.in) will not be functional for the new website.

After completion of online Application Form, the printed copy accompanied with necessary documents must be duly forwarded by the respective Service/Cadre Controlling Authority to "The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi-110003" so as to reach by 03.07.2026 (1800 hrs). Only those candidates whose application is forwarded by their Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission to this Examination.

Documents to be Uploaded with Online Application:

  • Certified true copy of the first page of the Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office (showing Name, Father's Name, Husband's Name, Nationality, SC/ST Name if applicable, Date of Birth)
  • Certified true copy of particulars of service attested by Head of Department/Head of Office (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment - substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Copy of certificate of essential educational qualification, if applicable
  • Form of certificate for disabled Defence Personnel while in service, wherever applicable
  • Certificate of disability in case of PwBD candidates
  • Live photograph captured through the application module (plain background, no cap/mask/glasses, full frontal view)
  • Scanned signature in JPEG format (10 to 20 KB; image dimension about 6.0 cm width x 2.0 cm height)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in

Important Instructions for SSC SSA/UDC Departmental Examination 2025 Candidates

  • This is a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination - only eligible serving JSA/LDC employees of the specified 10 participating cadres can apply.
  • Only one application form should be submitted; submission of multiple applications may lead to rejection of candidature.
  • After completion of online application, the printed copy must be forwarded by the Head of Department/Office through proper channel to reach SSC (NR) by 03.07.2026 (1800 hrs); applications not forwarded through proper channel will not be considered.
  • A candidate who resigns, quits service, or whose services are terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.
  • No change in entries made in the online application form shall be allowed at any stage under any circumstances.
  • The examination shall be conducted in Delhi NCR only; no centre will be at any Indian mission abroad. Candidates serving abroad will have to appear in India at their own expense.
  • Admission Certificate for CBE will be issued online by uploading on the website of the Northern Regional Office; it will not be issued by post. Candidates are advised to regularly visit https://sscnr.nic.in.
  • Candidates must carry their Departmental Identity Card (Original) along with hard copy of Admission Certificate for appearing in the examination.
  • Candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar Based Authentication must carry at least two passport size recent colour photographs and Original valid Photo-ID proof with Date of Birth at the examination centre.
  • There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores of any stage/paper(s) of the Examination; no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained.
  • Tentative Answer Keys of CBE will be placed on the SSC website after the examination; candidates can submit online representations within the time limit on payment of Rs. 50/- per question (non-refundable).
  • Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during the OTR process.
  • The appearance of a candidate at the examination must match the photograph in the application form - no change in appearance is permitted.
  • All communications should be addressed to "The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi-110003" with subject line "Senior Secretariat Assistant/Upper Division Clerk Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025".
  • For Helpdesk: SSC-HQ toll-free 1800 309 3063; SSC (NR) New Delhi: 011-24363343.
  • Legal disputes, if any, shall be subject to courts/tribunals having jurisdiction over the place of the Regional Office of SSC where the candidate appeared in the examination.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has released the notification for the Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) / Lower Division Clerk (LDC) Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination (LDCE), 2025 vide Notice No. 4/4/2026-CONF-5, to fill 149 vacancies across 12 Central Government departments and cadres. The online application window is open from 05th June 2026 to 26th June 2026 (up to 11:00 PM). Please note this is a limited departmental examination - only existing regular Group 'C' / Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) employees of the participating cadres are eligible, and every application must be forwarded through proper channel by the Head of Department/Office. The Computer Based Examination is tentatively scheduled for July–August 2026 and will be held in Delhi-NCR only. Check the complete eligibility, vacancy break-up, exam pattern, and step-by-step process below.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

Important: Who Can Apply (and Who Cannot)

Because this is an LDCE (Limited Departmental Competitive Examination), eligibility is far narrower than an open recruitment. Read this before anything else - it is the most common point of confusion.

You CAN apply only if all of the following are true:

  • You are a regularly appointed Group 'C' employee or Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) in Level-1 / Grade Pay ₹1,800 of one of the 12 participating cadres listed below.
  • You have completed at least 3 years of regular service in that grade as on your cadre's crucial date.
  • You have passed Class 12th (Higher Secondary) or equivalent from a recognised Board.
  • Your application is forwarded by your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (Northern Region).

You CANNOT apply if:

  • You are a fresh candidate / general public with no qualifying government service - this exam is not open to private-sector or unemployed applicants.
  • You work in a department that is not among the 12 participating cadres.
  • Your application is not forwarded through proper channel - direct/self-submitted hard copies will be summarily rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Candidates must have passed the 12th standard (Higher Secondary) examination from a recognised Board or equivalent. For the Railway Board Secretariat Clerical Service, candidates are additionally required to pass a typing test (35 w.p.m. in English or 30 w.p.m. in Hindi on computer) within one year of appointment.

Length of Service

A minimum of three years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee / MTS in Level-1 (Grade Pay ₹1,800) in the respective cadre, counted as on the crucial date applicable to that cadre.

Crucial Date (Varies by Cadre)

The crucial date for counting approved service and age is not the same for every department. Check yours carefully:

Age Limit & Relaxation

For most participating cadres, the maximum age is 45 years (50 years for SC/ST) as on the crucial date. Candidates should confirm the exact age condition for their own cadre from the notification. Permissible relaxation beyond the upper age limit:

Category Age Relaxation

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Application Fee

For this Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, the notice does not prescribe an application fee for submitting the form. (A separate, non-refundable charge of ₹50 per question applies only if a candidate later chooses to challenge the tentative answer key - this is unrelated to the application itself.)

How to Apply for SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025

The process has two parts - One Time Registration (OTR) followed by the application - plus a mandatory offline forwarding step. Follow these steps:

  1. Generate OTR on the new website. Visit ssc.gov.in and click "Register Now." Any OTR created on the old site (ssc.nic.in) will not work on the new portal.
  2. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during OTR (recommended). Candidates who skip Aadhaar must upload the prescribed proof documents.
  3. Log in with your Registration Number and password, then open the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 link under the "Live Exam" tab and click Apply.
  4. Fill the application - service details, cadre, crucial date, length of service, and age-relaxation code (if any). Information auto-filled from OTR is non-editable; use "Modify Registration" if a correction is needed.
  5. Capture your live photograph and upload your signature as per the specifications (see below).
  6. Upload the required documents (listed below) and Submit. Take a printout of the submitted application.
  7. Forward the hard copy through proper channel. Your Head of Department / Head of Office must forward the printed application along with service documents to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 03-07-2026 (6:00 PM) - or 10-07-2026 for candidates abroad/A&N/Lakshadweep.

Critical: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Office will be admitted. A correctly submitted online form alone is not enough.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Start

  • Certified true copy of the first page of your Service Book (attested by HoD/HoO)
  • Certified particulars of service (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment)
  • Class 12th certificate / educational qualification proof (if applicable)
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST), if claiming reservation
  • Disability certificate (Annexure-VII / VIII) for PwBD candidates
  • A recent passport-size photo for the live capture reference, and a scanned signature

Photograph & Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: Captured live via webcam/phone, in a well-lit area with a plain background. No cap, mask, or spectacles. Face must fill the on-screen red rectangle. Pre-existing/scanned photos are rejected.
  • Signature: JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, dimensions about 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm. Sign so the signature fills at least 80% of the box. Blurred or miniature signatures are rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Exam Pattern & Scheme

The examination carries 260 marks in total - 200 for Part-I (the exams) and 60 for Part-II (service record). Note that Paper-I is descriptive (written) and Paper-II is the objective Computer Based Test (CBT).

Part-I: Written + Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Paper Type Section Questions Max Marks Duration
Paper-I Descriptive (Written) Short Essay – 100 1 hr 30 min*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (a) Language - General English or Samanya Hindi 50 50 2 hrs*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (b) General Knowledge 50 50 (combined)

*Scribe-eligible candidates get 2 hours for Paper-I and 2 hours 40 minutes for Paper-II, plus 20 minutes compensatory time per hour.

  • Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applies to Paper-II (CBT) only. There is no negative marking in the descriptive Paper-I.
  • Candidates must attempt the exam in the language (English/Hindi) chosen in the application form.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (60 Marks)

60 marks are reserved for evaluation of the APARs (Annual Performance Appraisal Reports). These marks are added to determine the final rank. Once evaluated, no request to change APAR grading is entertained.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Selection Process

This is a competitive, not qualifying examination. Selection proceeds stage by stage:

  1. Paper-II (CBT) qualifying: Candidates must clear the minimum marks fixed for Paper-II to have their Paper-I evaluated.
  2. Paper-I (Descriptive) evaluation: Only those qualifying in Paper-II have their descriptive paper assessed.
  3. APAR evaluation (Part-II): Based on the aggregate of Paper-I + Paper-II, shortlisted candidates move to service-record evaluation.
  4. Final merit: Prepared on the combined total of Paper-I + Paper-II + Part-II (APAR) = 260 marks, cadre-wise, subject to reservation. Ties are resolved by Paper-I marks, then Paper-II part (a), then Paper-II total, then date of birth (older ranked higher), then alphabetical order.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Syllabus

  • Paper-I (Short Essay): One essay of 400–500 words on any of the specified subjects.
  • Paper-II (a) Language: Simple composition and applied grammar (in the chosen English/Hindi medium).
  • Paper-II (b) General Knowledge: Current events, matters of everyday observation and experience, and general information about India.

SSC JSA / LDC Salary 2026

Selected candidates are appointed in Pay Level-2 (₹19,900 – ₹63,200 per month) under the 7th CPC, as Group 'C' Non-Gazetted staff. In addition to basic pay, employees are entitled to Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and other benefits as admissible under Central Government rules for the respective department.

Common Reasons SSC Applications Get Rejected

A large share of LDCE applications fail on avoidable mistakes. Double-check all of these before submitting:

  • Application not forwarded by the Head of Department/Office (the single biggest cause of rejection).
  • Multiple applications submitted for the same exam.
  • Photograph with a cap/spectacles, dark background, blurred, or a pre-existing (scanned) photo instead of a live capture.
  • Signature that is blurred, miniature, or below the size norm.
  • Wrong OTR details - name, father's/mother's name, or date of birth not matching the matriculation certificate (OTR data is non-editable).
  • Hard copy reaching SSC-NR after the deadline, or incomplete documents.

What to Do If the SSC Website Is Slow

Traffic on the SSC portal spikes near the closing date. If you face issues:

  • Apply during off-peak hours - late at night or early morning - rather than on the last day.
  • Clear your browser cache/cookies, or use an incognito/private tab.
  • Try a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
  • Keep all documents pre-scanned and ready in the correct format so a session timeout doesn't cost you the whole form.
  • Save a draft frequently and take a printout immediately after final submission.

Exam Day Guidelines

  • The exam is conducted in Delhi-NCR only; there is no centre abroad. A candidate posted abroad must appear in India at their own expense.
  • The Admission Certificate is issued online via sscnr.nic.in (3–4 days before the exam); it is never sent by post.
  • Carry your original Departmental Identity Card along with a hard copy of the Admission Certificate.
  • Candidates not Aadhaar-authenticated during OTR must report early with two passport-size photographs and an original photo ID showing date of birth.
  • No Travelling Allowance is paid by SSC.
  • Mobile phones, Bluetooth/wireless devices, smartwatches, and electronic gadgets are strictly prohibited. SSC conducts post-exam log, biometric, and CCTV analysis, and malpractice attracts debarment of 1 to 7 years depending on the offence.

  • SSC (Northern Region): 011-24363343
  • Official Websites: ssc.gov.in (HQ) · sscnr.nic.in (Northern Region)

Selection Process - How Candidates Are Chosen

The IAF MTS recruitment follows a clearly defined selection process. Knowing each stage in advance helps candidates prepare effectively and avoid being eliminated at any step.

Stage 1 - Application Scrutiny

All applications received will be examined for age limit compliance, minimum educational qualification, required documents, and certificates. Only eligible candidates will be shortlisted for the written test.

Stage 2 - Written Test

Eligible shortlisted candidates will be called for a written test. The selection of candidates will be based purely on performance in the written test — no interview is conducted.

Written Test Syllabus covers four areas:

  • General Intelligence and Reasoning
  • Numerical Aptitude
  • General English
  • General Awareness

The question-cum-answer paper will be available in both English and Hindi.

Stage 3 - Document Verification

Shortlisted candidates after the written test must bring original certificates and copies of the annexure attached with the application at the time of document verification.

Important: Candidates are required to bring original certificates of SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM, educational qualifications, technical qualifications, and experience at every stage of recruitment. The crucial date for determining validity of documents is on or before the last date of receipt of application.

Where to Send the Application

The fee is non-refundable and must be paid online. GST at 18% is charged additionally on the base fee.

Payment is accepted through online mode only. No other payment method is accepted. Fee once paid is not refunded under any circumstances.

How to Apply for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The application process involves two portals. Here is a step-by-step guide:

Step 1 - Register on NATS Portal Visit https://nats.education.gov.in and navigate to the "Student Register/Login" section. Complete your registration and note your Enrolment ID, which is required for all future correspondence.

Step 2 - Find CBI Apprenticeship on NATS After logging in, visit https://nats.education.gov.in/student_type.php to find and apply to the Central Bank of India apprenticeship advertisement.

Step 3 - Complete Application on BEEP Portal After applying on NATS, you will receive an email from BFSI SSC ([email protected]) with a link to register on https://beep.bfsissc.com. Complete your final application here by entering caste category, district preferences, and other details.

Step 4 - Pay the Application Fee Pay the applicable fee online through the BEEP portal. The application is complete only after successful payment.

Step 5 - Save Your Application Take a printout of the system-generated online application form after submitting. Do not make multiple submissions; only the last valid completed application will be retained.

Selection Process for Central Bank of India Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Selection involves multiple stages. Candidates must clear all stages to be engaged as apprentices.

Stage 1 - Online Written Examination

The exam is objective type, conducted by BFSI SSC. It will be taken from the candidate's own home on their own device - no admit card or examination centre is required.

Subject Questions Marks Duration
General / Financial Awareness 20 20 -
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 20 20 -
Computer Knowledge 20 20 -
General English 20 20 -
Central Bank of India Products & Services 20 20 -
Total 100 100 60 minutes
  • Medium: English/Hindi (General English section in English only)
  • No negative marking for wrong answers
  • Tie-breaking rule: if two candidates score equally, the older candidate ranks higher (descending order of age)
  • Details on CBI Products & Services will be shared on the bank's official website in due course

Stage 2 - Test of Local Language

Candidates must be proficient (reading, writing, speaking, and understanding) in the specified official language of the state they apply for. This test is conducted after qualifying the online exam at a centre decided by the bank, at the candidate's own expense.

Candidates who have studied the specified local language at the 10th or 12th standard level (as evidenced by mark sheets) are exempt from the language test.

Stage 3 - Document Verification

Qualified candidates are called to the relevant CBI Regional/Zonal Office for verification of all original documents, including date of birth proof, graduation certificates, category certificates, and any other relevant documents.

Stage 4 - Medical Fitness Verification

Final engagement is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit by a qualified medical practitioner or MBBS doctor, as per the bank's requirements.

Stipend, Training Conditions, and Benefits

Understanding what to expect during the apprenticeship helps candidates plan ahead.

  • Monthly Stipend: ₹15,000 per month for the 12-month training period
  • No other allowances or employee benefits are provided
  • Leave: One casual leave per month; public/bank holidays as applicable; no other leave types
  • Working hours: Same as clerical staff of the bank; no overtime is permitted
  • No hostel, transport, or residential accommodation is provided by the bank
  • An assessment test may be conducted after completion, followed by certification as per prevailing guidelines
  • Apprentices are trainees, not employees - no labour laws or employee benefits apply
  • Apprentices cannot form or join any union

Contract of Apprenticeship

Candidates selected after document verification will receive a digital apprenticeship contract through the NATS government portal (https://nats.education.gov.in). They must accept the contract within the stipulated timeframe. No candidate can begin training without an approved apprenticeship contract.

Termination Conditions

The contract may be terminated in the following situations:

  • Non-reporting on the date of commencement of On-Job Training
  • Automatic termination on expiry of the 12-month training period
  • Mutual application to the Apprenticeship Advisor (BFSI SSC) before completion, with stated reasons
  • Misconduct by the apprentice, with written notice from the bank
  • If the Apprenticeship Advisor finds either party has failed to fulfil the contract terms

Documents Required at the Time of Document Verification

Candidates must carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of all the following:

  • System-generated printout of online application/NATS enrolment form
  • Date of Birth proof (Birth Certificate or Class X certificate with DOB)
  • Photo identity proof
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and final degree certificate
  • Caste certificate (for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates) in the Government of India prescribed format
  • OBC certificate must explicitly contain the non-creamy layer clause and be valid as on the date of the Language Test (issued within one year)
  • Disability certificate from District Medical Board (for PwBD candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates) issued by competent authority

Reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Under Section 34 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, reservation for PwBD is on a horizontal basis within the overall vacancies for each state. The qualifying disability categories include:

  • Visual Impairment (Blindness and Low Vision)
  • Hearing Impairment (Deaf and Hard of Hearing)
  • Orthopedic/Locomotor Disability (OA, OL, BL, OAL)
  • Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism, Acid Attack Victims, Muscular Dystrophy
  • Intellectual Disability (Autism Spectrum Disorder, Specific Learning Disability, Mental Illness)
  • Multiple Disabilities

A total of 45 seats each are reserved for VI, HI, OH, and ID categories, amounting to 180 PwBD seats across the country.

Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) Eligibility

Candidates not covered under SC/ST/OBC reservation and whose family gross annual income is below ₹8 lakh from all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession) qualify for EWS reservation. Additionally, the family must not own:

  • 5 acres or more of agricultural land
  • A residential flat of 1,000 sq. ft. or more
  • A residential plot of 100 sq. yards or more in notified municipalities
  • A residential plot of 200 sq. yards or more outside notified municipalities

The EWS benefit requires an Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed Government of India format, issued by a competent authority.

Where to Find Updates and Announcements

All announcements, addendums, and corrigenda will be published exclusively on:

  • Central Bank of India official website: Click here (Career section → Current Opportunities)
  • BFSI SSC portal: https://bfsissc.com
  • BEEP portal: https://beep.bfsissc.com (under "My Applied Opportunities")

DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is ₹100 (One Hundred only). Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Serviceman categories are fully exempted from paying the fee. Ex-Servicemen who have already secured regular civil employment under the Central Government or Government of NCT of Delhi after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for fee exemption.

Payment must be made only through SBI ePay. No other payment mode will be accepted, and fees paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be made through a Computer Based Written Examination under one of three examination schemes depending on the post applied for.

One Tier General (I-T-G) — Post Codes 34/26, 39/26, 40/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Five sections of 40 marks each: General Awareness, General Intelligence & Reasoning Ability, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability, Hindi Language & Comprehension, and English Language & Comprehension. Final merit is based on written examination marks only.

One Tier Technical (I-T-T) — Post Codes 21/26 to 31/26, 32/26, 33/26, 35/26 to 38/26, 45/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks covering General Awareness, Reasoning, Arithmetic, Hindi, and English (20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks on the domain subject for the post concerned. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine the final merit list.

One Tier Technical/Teaching (I-T-T) — Post Codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26, 44/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks (same five general subjects, 20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks from subject-specific content including teaching methodology/B.Ed. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine final merit.

Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks will be deducted for each wrong MCQ answer. Skill Test, Aptitude Test, Trade Test, or Physical Endurance Test may be conducted additionally as per job requirements. Marks will be normalized (if required) using the Score Normalisation Based on Deviation Method formula published by DSSSB vide Notice No. 10(271)/Sec.Cell/DSSSB/18/989 dated 11.07.2018.

How to Apply

The application process for DSSSB Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. No applications sent by post, by hand, or by email will be accepted.

  1. Visit the official DSSSB registration and application portal at https://dsssbonline.nic.in.
  2. If you are a new user, complete the one-time registration process. Note down your User ID and password — the same credentials are to be used for all future DSSSB examinations; do not register multiple times.
  3. Log in using your registered credentials and select the relevant post code from Advertisement No. 03/2026.
  4. Fill in all fields of the online application form accurately. Once submitted, no change or correction — including change of category — will be permitted under any circumstances.
  5. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white or off-white background, full face, front view, eyes open) and your signature. Blurred or illegible photographs/signatures will result in rejection.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹100 through SBI ePay (exempted categories need not pay).
  7. Submit the form and take a printout for your own records. Keep the registration number and application number safely.

The application portal will be live from 16 June 2026 (12:00 Noon) until 15 July 2026 (11:59 PM), after which the link will be disabled.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Candidates applying for DSSSB 2026 should be careful about a few common pitfalls in the online application process.

Photo and signature uploads are a frequent reason for rejection — ensure the image files are clear, correctly sized, and within the file-size limit specified on the portal. Blurred or illegible uploads will cause outright rejection of candidature. If the payment gateway shows an error after fee deduction, do not immediately retry; wait for a few hours to check whether the payment was credited before attempting again through the portal's payment history section. Use an updated browser (Chrome or Firefox preferred) and avoid mobile browsers for form submission, as they may not render all fields correctly. Save your User ID and password immediately after registration and store your application number carefully — all future communications from DSSSB will reference these. Avoid applying on the last day; DSSSB expressly states it will not be responsible for inability to submit due to heavy server load near the closing date.

BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

All candidates will undergo the recruitment process in the following sequence: (i) Written Examination, (ii) Physical Efficiency Test (PET) including physical measurements and Trade Test (TT) where applicable, (iii) Primary Medical Examination (PME) and Document Verification (DV), and (iv) Induction/Joining. The PET and TT are qualifying in nature - final merit is based solely on written exam marks, subject to qualifying PET, TT, and clearing PME. Minimum passing marks in written exam: 50% for UR/EWS/OBC; 40% for SC/ST. Trade test requires minimum 40% marks to qualify.

Physical Efficiency Test (PET): Candidate must complete 1.6 km (1 mile) run in 10 minutes. PwBD, ESM, Ex-Agniveers, and departmental re-appointment candidates are exempt from PET.

Competition Level Analysis for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

The competition level for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026 is expected to be moderate to high. The recruitment is restricted to Male candidates only, which reduces the applicant pool compared to open-gender recruitments. However, 899 vacancies across technical/trade posts will attract a large number of ITI-qualified and Matriculation-level candidates, especially for high-vacancy posts like Store Keeper Technical (300) and Operator Communication (261). The written exam followed by PET and Trade Test provides multiple elimination stages, but candidates with relevant ITI trade certificates and physical fitness will have a clear advantage. Ex-Servicemen and Ex-Agniveers get significant age relaxation and weightage, which makes certain trades more competitive in that segment.

The key differentiator here is the offline application process - many eligible candidates may miss out due to postal delays or incorrect application format, effectively reducing actual competition at the written exam stage. Candidates who submit complete and correct applications well before the deadline and prepare trade-specific written exam syllabi will have a significant edge.

Who should NOT apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Female candidates - this recruitment is strictly for Indian National Males only.
  • Candidates who do not possess the requisite educational/technical qualification as on the closing date of application; those awaiting final exam results are not eligible.
  • Candidates outside the age band 18-27 years as on 01 Jun 2026 (except those eligible for applicable category-based relaxation).
  • OBC candidates from the Creamy Layer - they are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply as UR/General category.
  • Candidates who cannot meet the region-wise physical standards (height, chest, weight) as physical fitness is mandatory for induction.
  • Candidates with permanent medical conditions listed as grounds for permanent rejection (colour blindness for Drivers/Operators, cardiac conditions, gross myopia, etc.) who cannot pass the Primary Medical Examination at GREF Centre.
  • Candidates unwilling or unable to be posted anywhere in India, especially in remote, high-altitude, or difficult terrain areas in Northern and Eastern regions.
  • Candidates who cannot arrange and send a physical application form with photograph, thumb impression, signature, fee e-receipt, and attested copies by post to Pune - there is no online application mode.
  • Candidates with tattoos on any body part other than the inner forearm (inside elbow to wrist) or reverse palm - tattoos on other parts lead to disqualification at PME.
  • Ex-servicemen who have already joined Govt civil service using ESM benefits and are claiming ESM status again - such candidates are treated as civilian employees.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying BRO GREF Recruitment 2026?

  • Not printing the application form on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card on both sides of a single paper as mandated - non-standard paper leads to rejection.
  • Applying without attaching the e-receipt copy of the application fee paid via SBI Collect; no other payment mode is accepted and missing receipt causes rejection.
  • Sending the application from a wrong/old address instead of present postal address - applications posted from wrong address are rejected to prevent fraudulent claims of 60-day receipt benefit.
  • Not superscribing the envelope with "APPLICATION FOR (NAME OF TRADE/POST) Under Category (UR/SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM/CPL)" as required - unlabelled envelopes may be misdirected.
  • Mismatch between name in application and name in Matriculation certificate - even a dropped or added part of the name requires a Gazette Notification; otherwise candidature is summarily cancelled.
  • Submitting multiple applications for the same post with different details or photographs - this results in lifetime debarment from all GREF examinations.
  • OBC/EWS certificate dated older than one year from the closing date - OBC and EWS certificates must be fresh (not older than one year as on closing date) and in the prescribed Central Govt format.
  • Candidates applying for more than one post/trade using the same envelope - each post requires a separate application with separate fee in a separate envelope.
  • Not carrying the minimum 12 passport-size photographs (same as pasted on application and admit card) to all subsequent recruitment stages - shortage of photos causes disruption at PET/TT/PME stages.
  • Ignoring the trade-specific syllabus and treating the written exam as a general knowledge test - each post has a distinct subject-wise syllabus and candidates must prepare trade-specific topics.

How to Apply for BRO GREF Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply offline only; no online application mode is available. Application form and admit card must be downloaded from the official BRO website (www.bro.gov.in) and filled in English or Hindi only, in capital letters. The application form must be printed on A4 size 75 GSM bond paper (one side only) and admit card printed on both sides of a single paper. Candidates must first pay the application fee online via SBI Collect portal and attach the e-receipt copy. Candidates applying for more than one post must send separate applications with separate fee in separate envelopes. Candidates are strongly advised to send applications well before the closing date and not wait for the last day - GREF Centre will not be responsible for postal delays.

Candidates should read the detailed instructions and guidelines available at https://bfsissc.com before applying.

  • Left hand thumb impression at the prescribed place on application form and admit card
  • Signature of candidate at the prescribed place

  • NCC certificate copies (B or C grade), sports certificate, or relationship certificate for Sons of Serving/Ex-GREF personnel - for claiming weightage marks
  • Proof of residence/domicile (for correct physical standards region)
  • Any certificate in language other than Hindi or English must be enclosed with an attested Hindi/English translation by a Group A Gazetted Officer

Send Application (by Postal Service) to: Commandant, GREF Centre, Dighi Camp, Pune - 411015

  • Only Male Indian Nationals can apply; Female candidates are not eligible.

  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, and all electronic/communication devices are strictly NOT ALLOWED inside GREF Centre, Pune campus during any recruitment process.
  • A candidate who absents himself during any recruitment activity for which he has been called will have his candidature cancelled automatically - he will not be allowed to appear for further stages.
  • There shall be no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores in examination; no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this Advertisement shall fall within the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
  • Impersonation or submission of forged documents leads to debarment from all GREF examinations for life/2 years and legal action. GREF has not appointed any agent or coaching centre for action on its behalf - SELECTION WILL BE DONE PURELY ON MERIT IN A TRANSPARENT MANNER.
  • Vacancies are liable to increase/decrease/cancel at any stage without notice due to unforeseen situations.
  • All revisions/corrigendum will be hosted on the BRO website only - candidates should visit www.bro.gov.in regularly.

About CRE-5: What Is It and Who Is It For?

CRE-5 is a unified, single-window recruitment platform that allows eligible candidates to apply once and be considered for similar posts across multiple participating institutes. The Examination Section, AIIMS New Delhi acts solely as the examination-conducting body; recruitment rules, service conditions, and final appointment decisions rest entirely with each participating institute independently.

Participating organizations are autonomous bodies or subordinate offices under the Government of India, functioning independently from AIIMS New Delhi. Candidates are advised to check each institute's individual recruitment rules and eligibility criteria before applying, as conditions may differ for the same post name across different institutes.

Payment can be made via Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking. The examination fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, even if the application is rejected for ineligibility. However, application fees paid by SC/ST candidates who appear in the examination will be refunded to the source account after declaration of results.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern and Syllabus

The CRE-5 Computer Based Test is a structured, time-bound examination designed to assess both domain knowledge and general aptitude.

CBT Structure

Parameter Detail
Duration 90 minutes
Total Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 400 marks (4 marks per question)
Negative Marking –1 mark per wrong answer (1/4th deduction)
General Knowledge & Aptitude / Computer 20 MCQs
Domain-Specific Questions 80 MCQs
Sections 5 sections × 20 questions × 18 minutes each

Each section is sequential and time-locked - once a section closes, candidates cannot return to it. Candidates must attempt all possible questions within the active section's time window.

Medium of Examination

Posts where the essential qualification is 10th/12th will be examined in bilingual (English and Hindi) medium. Posts requiring bachelor's or higher qualifications, or posts involving specific technical domain knowledge, will be examined in English only.

Qualifying Marks

Category Qualifying Percentage
UR / EWS 40%
OBC 35%
SC / ST 30%
PwBD (all categories) 30%
Ex-Servicemen As per their category

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal marks, ties are resolved in this order: (i) higher marks in the domain-specific section; (ii) fewer wrong answers/negative marks; (iii) older date of birth; (iv) alphabetical order of name, then father's name, then mother's name.

Syllabus (Domain Part - Selected Groups)

Group Domain Syllabus
1 Food & Nutrition, Diets
2 General Administration, CCS Rules, FR/SR, Basic Computer
3 General Maths & English
4 Civil Engineering
5 Electrical Engineering
12 Pharmacy
17 Medical Laboratory Technology
34 Nursing
41 Computer Applications and Programming
53 General Maths, English, Fire Safety and Security

Full syllabus details for all 57 groups are in Section IX of the official DRA.

Skill Test

For selected post groups, a Skill Test is conducted as Stage II for candidates who qualify the CBT. The skill test is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared based on CBT performance, but only among those who pass the skill test for the relevant post.

Posts requiring skill tests include groups such as Junior Administrative Assistant (typing test), Stenographer (stenography test), Programmer (computer skill test), Hindi Translator (translation test), Assistant Security Officer (PST), and Fire Technician (PET & PST). See Annexure-V of the DRA for complete scheme details.

If a candidate qualifies the CBT but fails the skill test, they remain eligible only for posts within the same group that do not require a skill test.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

CRE-5 follows a multi-stage recruitment process. Each stage is mandatory for progression to the next.

Stage 1 - Online Application: Candidates register on www.aiimsexams.ac.in and submit applications by 30 June 2026.

Stage 2 - Application Acceptance: Application status published on 9 July 2026.

Stage 3 - Computer Based Test (CBT): Tentatively 25–27 July 2026 at examination centres across major states/UTs of India.

Stage 4 - Skill Test (where applicable): Conducted after CBT for qualifying candidates in applicable groups. Venue: preferably Delhi/NCR. Date to be notified.

Stage 5 - Choice & Preference: Qualified candidates are invited to exercise institute choices and indicate order of preference. Candidates who fail to exercise choices within the given period will not be considered for any institute.

Stage 6 - Seat Allocation: Allocation is made in order of merit based on choices exercised and eligibility at each participating institute.

Stage 7 - Document Verification: Original certificates verified by the respective AIIMS/Institute on the date notified by them.

Stage 8 - Joining: Selected candidates must report on the date specified in the result/allocation notice. Failure to report will lead to mandatory cancellation of candidature for CRE.

AIIMS CRE-5 Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply for AIIMS CRE-5 2026

National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) has released vacancy notices for 175 posts across two grades - Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller (34 posts, Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026) and Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager (175 posts, Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026) - on absorption basis from Regular/Contractual employees of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, and RRTS. NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Quick Summary

This recruitment covers two distinct pay grades under IDA scales. The Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller grade carries the NE-6 IDA pay scale of ₹46,000–1,45,000, while the Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager grade carries the NE-4 IDA pay scale of ₹40,000–1,25,000. Both grades are open exclusively to serving employees of Indian Railways/Government Railways/Metro Railways/RRTS - this is not an open-market recruitment.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is assessed differently depending on whether the candidate is employed under IDA or CDA pay scales. All experience and eligibility conditions are reckoned as on 31 May 2026. Experience gained through teaching, faculty, apprenticeship, internship, proprietorship, partnership, or freelancing will not count toward the required years of experience.

Work Experience – Deputy Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026)

For IDA pay scale employees (Metro Railways/RRTS):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field (Civil/Track maintenance, Electrical Power Distribution, Railway Signalling, Rolling Stock maintenance, or OCC Operations as applicable); AND
  • Currently working in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹46,000, OR
  • 2 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹40,000 and above, OR
  • 5 years' experience in pay scales with minimum bottom pay of ₹37,000 and above.

For CDA pay scale employees (Ministry of Railways / other Govt. Railways):

  • Minimum 5 years' supervisory work experience in the relevant field; AND
  • Working in PB-2 + GP ₹4,200 (Level 6 of 7th CPC); AND
  • Minimum 4 years of Group C service.

For the Deputy Chief Controller (Operations) post specifically, candidates under CDA scales must have 5 years' supervisory experience in maintenance of Rolling Stock and Depot Machinery (not OCC operations) to be eligible. Under IDA scales, the requirement is 5 years' post-qualification supervisory experience in OCC/Station/Train operations with minimum 2 years as Traffic Controller in an OCC equipped with modern OCC systems.

Note on MACP: For CDA-scale employees, higher grade pays granted under MACP by the department will not be considered for eligibility. Only the substantive grade is taken into account for determining the grade of absorption.

Work Experience – Junior Engineer Grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026)

All posts require a minimum of 3 years of post-qualification experience in the relevant field within Operations & Maintenance departments of Indian Railways, Government-owned or operated Railways, Metro Railways, or RRTS systems.

Age Limit

The maximum age limit is 45 years for all posts in both groups. Age is reckoned as on 31 May 2026.

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee structure is identical for both vacancy notice groups. Female candidates and candidates from Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe backgrounds are fully exempt from paying the fee. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable under any circumstances - candidates are advised to confirm their eligibility before making payment.

Salary / Pay Scale

NHSRCL offers IDA (Industrial Dearness Allowance) pay scales. The pay and emoluments include Perks, HRA, Medical Benefits, other allowances, EPF, and Gratuity as per extant rules of the corporation.

Grade Pay Scale (IDA)
Deputy Engineer / Deputy Chief Controller (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026) ₹46,000–1,45,000 (NE-6)
Junior Engineer / Controller / Train Manager / Station Manager (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026) ₹40,000–1,25,000 (NE-4)

NHSRCL DE & JE Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

For the Deputy Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 21–25/2026), selection consists of four stages in this order: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, Interview, and Medical Examination.

For the Junior Engineer grade (Vacancy Nos. 26–32/2026), selection consists of three stages: Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification, and Medical Examination. Note that the Interview stage is not part of the JE-grade selection process.

In both cases, management reserves the right to include or dispense with any stage of the selection methodology. Shortlisted candidates will be informed through their registered email addresses. Out-station candidates called for interview (DE grade) will be paid Travelling Allowance as per company rules.

Medical fitness is a mandatory condition of appointment. Candidates will be examined as per the Indian Railway Medical Manual (IRMM). Additional medical tests such as Audiometry and Perimetry may also be conducted as required for safe operation of High Speed Trains.

Surety Bond and Service Commitment

Candidates selected for absorption must be aware of the following binding commitments before joining NHSRCL.

Surety Bond on Joining: Selected candidates must execute a surety bond of ₹3,00,000/- committing to serve NHSRCL for a minimum period of 4 years (excluding any period on Leave Without Pay or Extra-Ordinary Leave). A prior notice of 90 days is required before resigning from the corporation.

Surety Bond on Training: If training is provided, candidates must execute a separate surety bond for the cost of training plus applicable service tax, committing to serve for a minimum of 6 years after training completion. A three-month prior notice is required before resignation in such cases.

Candidates appointed on absorption basis will be on probation for one year. They may be posted anywhere across NHSRCL offices and the MAHSR Project.

Important Note on Controller and Safety Assignment

Candidates applying for posts that include a Controller or Safety assignment (such as Vacancy Nos. 21–29, 31/2026) must indicate their willingness for such assignments in the online application form. They must also furnish their order of preference between the available designations at the time of application. However, the final allocation of post or assignment rests entirely at NHSRCL's discretion, regardless of the candidate's stated preference.

Document Requirements

Along with the application, candidates must submit a Competency Certificate or Experience Certificate issued by their employer. This certificate must clearly indicate the required work experience with year-wise details of the nature and type of work performed. Incomplete applications or applications submitted without supporting documents will be rejected outright.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Applying for NHSRCL absorption posts is a specialized process. Keep the following in mind to avoid rejection:

  • Do not apply for more than one post within the same vacancy notice group (21–25 or 26–32). Only one application is permitted per group, and both CBT sessions may be held simultaneously.
  • Save your registration credentials immediately after creating your portal account. NHSRCL communicates exclusively through registered email IDs - check your spam folder regularly.
  • Verify eligibility before paying the fee. The ₹400 fee is non-refundable under all circumstances, including ineligibility or withdrawal.
  • If your internet connection drops during payment, do not immediately retry - check your bank statement first to avoid a double payment. Contact your bank if the amount is debited but confirmation is not received.
  • Use an updated browser on a stable connection for the application portal. Avoid submitting on the final day to prevent server congestion issues.
  • Ensure your experience certificate is on your employer's letterhead with year-wise work details - general appointment letters or offer letters alone are not acceptable.

Eligibility Criteria for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Eligibility for this CET cycle is built around two simple pillars - educational qualification and age - but each carries specific conditions that can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate if overlooked.

Educational Qualification

For all Group-D posts except Sweeper, Chowkidar, and Sweeper-cum-Chowkidar, a candidate must hold:

  • Matriculation from a recognized Board, and
  • Hindi or Sanskrit up to Matriculation as one of the subjects studied.

The notification clarifies that the detailed, post-wise educational qualification (for the specific Group-D posts) will be published separately along with the vacancy details.

Age Limit and Relaxation

A candidate must be not less than 18 years and not more than 42 years of age as on the closing date of registration (3 July 2026). Age relaxation is governed by Haryana Government instructions dated 25 March 2022, and the upper age limit can extend up to 52 years for candidates entitled to combined relaxation benefits.

How to Apply Online for HSSC CET Group D 2026

  3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details accurately, since no corrections are allowed after final submission except during the 7–9 July 2026 edit window.
  4. Upload all category-specific scanned documents (see the documents section below).
  5. Pay the applicable fee online through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
  6. Submit the form, then download and retain a printed copy along with the uploaded documents for future reference.

DSC / OSC Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + DSC or OSC caste certificate
BC-A / BC-B (Non-Creamy Layer) Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + BC-A/BC-B certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026
EWS Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + EWS certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026

Dependent of Freedom Fighter Certificate for children/grandchildren of the Freedom Fighter
PwBD Scanned copy of the disability certificate

Only documents uploaded at the time of filling the form are considered for scrutiny - anything submitted later, in any form, will not be entertained.

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Exam Pattern

The CET for Group D is designed as a single-stage, OMR-based screening test rather than a multi-stage exam, making the marking scheme one of the most important things to understand before attempting it.

Feature Detail
Number of Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 100
Duration 1 hour 45 minutes
Question Paper Level Secondary Education (Matriculation level)
Language Bilingual - English and Hindi
Mode Offline, OMR-based
Negative Marking for Wrong Answer None
Penalty for Skipped Question -1 mark, but only if the candidate fails to darken the fifth "not attempting" bubble

This last rule is unusual and trips up many candidates: marking a wrong answer carries no penalty at all, but leaving a question blank without filling in the designated fifth circle results in a one-mark deduction. The exam centre, once allotted on the admit card, will not ordinarily be changed.

Also read: SBI PO 2026 Notification PDF Out - Apply Online for 1,500 Probationary Officer Posts

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Syllabus

The CET syllabus is split into two weighted parts - a larger general-skills component and a smaller Haryana-specific component - and the question paper stays at Matriculation difficulty throughout.

Part A: 75% Weightage

  • General Awareness: India and neighbouring countries, especially History, Indian Polity & Constitution, Art & Culture, Geography; General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
  • Reasoning: Alphabetical order, series, coding-decoding, direction and distance, order and ranking, blood relations, analogy, classification, clock and calendar, mirror/water image, syllogism, sitting arrangement, statement and assumption/conclusion, counting figures, non-verbal series
  • Quantitative Ability: Number system, simplification, decimals, fractions, LCM/HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, roots, average, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest, mensuration, partnership, mixtures and alligation, time and work, time and distance, basic trigonometry, algebra, and geometry
  • English Language: Grammar, spotting errors, fill in the blanks, synonyms and antonyms, spellings, idioms and phrases, sentence improvement, active/passive voice, direct/indirect narration, and tenses
  • Hindi Language: Varna, swar-vyanjan, sangya, sarvanam, visheshan, kriya, kaal, sandhi, samas, paryayvachi-vilom shabd, muhavare-lokoktiyan, and vakya shodhan

Part B: 25% Weightage - Haryana-Specific General Knowledge

This portion covers History, Current Affairs, Literature, Geography, Environment, and Culture of Haryana, along with the state's economy, civics, polity, art, customs, and society.

Minimum Qualifying Marks and Validity of Earlier CET Scores

A general-category candidate needs to score at least 50% in the CET to be eligible, while reserved-category candidates (both vertical and horizontal) get a 10% concession, bringing their qualifying mark to 40%.

For candidates who already cleared the Group D CET held on 12 January 2024 - a score that remains valid until 11 January 2027 - their marks (originally scored out of a maximum of 95) will be mathematically converted into a percentage so they can be merged into the same combined merit list as candidates appearing under the new 100-mark pattern.

It's also worth noting that selection for Group-D posts has changed structurally: under a Government notification dated 12 February 2026, the earlier selection formula (which included up to 10 marks for socio-economic factors such as orphan or widow status alongside the written exam) has been replaced. Selection is now based entirely on CET marks, with no interview at any stage.

HSSC CET (Group D) Syllabus 2026

Reservation Benefits and Certificate Rules

Reservation benefits under this notification are available only to bonafide residents of Haryana State; reserved-category candidates from other states or Union Territories are treated purely as general-category candidates for this recruitment.

BCA and BCB (Non-Creamy Layer)

Certificates must follow the format in Annexure-II and be issued on or after 1 April 2026. Certificates issued for contesting Panchayati Raj elections, or OBC certificates issued for Central Government jobs, are not accepted.

EWS (Economically Weaker Section)

The family's gross annual income must be below Rs. 8 lakh (revised upward from Rs. 6 lakh per the 14 January 2026 instructions), and the family must not own specified assets such as 5+ acres of agricultural land, a 1,000+ sq. ft. residential flat, or immovable property valued at Rs. 1 crore or more. The certificate must be issued on or after 1 April 2026 and is valid only for the financial year it specifies.

DSC and OSC (Deprived and Other Scheduled Castes)

Under instructions dated 13 November 2024, Haryana's existing 20% Scheduled Caste reservation quota is now split equally between Deprived Scheduled Castes (DSC) and Other Scheduled Castes (OSC). If suitable DSC candidates aren't available, the balance posts can go to OSC candidates, and vice versa.

Ex-Servicemen and Freedom Fighter Dependents

Ex-servicemen benefits follow Government Instructions dated 25 May 2026, while reservation for children or grandchildren of Freedom Fighters (paternal or maternal lineage) follows instructions dated 27 October 2021 and 26 April 2022, applicable only when reserved Backward Class or Ex-servicemen posts remain unfilled.

Provisions for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Candidates registering under the PwBD category must select the correct disability code at the time of registration: VH (Visual Impairment), HH (Hard of Hearing), OH (Orthopedic, including locomotor disability and cerebral palsy), or MD (Multiple Disability, including autism and intellectual disability).

Scribe and compensatory time facilities are available as follows:

  • Candidates with blindness, locomotor disability (both arms affected), or cerebral palsy can use a scribe without needing a physical-limitation certificate.
  • Candidates in other PwBD categories need a certificate from a Chief Medical Officer, Civil Surgeon, or Medical Superintendent confirming the need for a scribe.
  • The scribe's own qualification must be up to Matriculation only, and the scribe cannot be a candidate in the same examination.
  • All eligible PwBD candidates referred above receive 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour, bringing the total exam duration to 140 minutes instead of 105.

Selection Process for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Since Group-D recruitment has no separate written exam beyond the CET, the process works differently from Group-C recruitment. The Commission shortlists candidates purely on CET marks, then publishes a category-wise merit and waiting list. When actual posts are advertised later, eligible candidates apply electronically to express willingness for that specific post using their existing Registration Number - only the candidate's consent is sought before the Commission recommends names to the appointing department; there is no fresh written test at this stage.

In case of a tie in CET marks, the older candidate gets precedence; if birth dates also match, the candidate whose first name comes earlier alphabetically (in English) ranks higher.

Exam Day Rules and Malpractice Penalties

HSSC enforces strict frisking and conduct rules at every CET centre, and violations carry debarment periods ranging from two to five years depending on severity.

Items strictly barred inside the exam hall include textual material, calculators, pens, geometry boxes, pen drives, mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, smartwatches, wallets, belts, caps, jewellery, and food or water containers. Candidates wearing articles of religious or cultural faith are advised to report at least two hours before the last reporting time to allow for proper frisking.

Type of Malpractice Debarment Period
Leaving the venue uninformed, or removing exam material from the hall 2 years
Misbehaving with staff, obstructing the exam, or submitting fabricated documents 3 years
Forged admit card/ID, copying, possessing electronic gadgets, impersonation, or hacking exam systems 5 years

OMR sheets must be marked only with a ballpoint pen (not a pencil), and any erasing, scratching, or use of whitener detected by the scanning machine leads to outright cancellation of the OMR sheet and candidature.

Who Should Apply for HSSC CET Group D 2026?

This recruitment cycle is suited to candidates who meet the matriculation-plus-language qualification and fall within the eligible age bracket, with a clear path for reserved-category candidates as well.

You should apply if you:

  • Have passed Matriculation from a recognized board with Hindi or Sanskrit as a subject
  • Are between 18 and 42 years of age as on 3 July 2026, or qualify for a relaxation category
  • Are a bonafide resident of Haryana seeking reservation benefits, or are applying as a general-category candidate from anywhere in India, Nepal, or Bhutan

You should reconsider applying if you:

  • Do not hold Matriculation, or did not study Hindi/Sanskrit up to that level
  • Fall outside the 18–42 age band without an applicable relaxation
  • Are a reserved-category candidate from outside Haryana expecting reservation benefits - you will only be considered under the general category

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Several avoidable errors lead to rejection at the scrutiny stage or loss of marks during the exam itself, based directly on the causes of rejection listed in the notification.

  • Uploading a BCA, BCB, EWS, or DSC/OSC certificate dated outside its required validity window
  • Submitting an incomplete document set for your claimed category
  • Registering more than once instead of using an existing CET 2022 or 2025 Registration Number
  • Leaving a question blank without filling the fifth "not attempted" bubble, resulting in an avoidable -1 mark
  • Darkening more than one circle for a single question, which voids that answer entirely
  • Assuming corrections can be made after final submission - they are only possible during the 7–9 July 2026 window
  • Carrying barred items such as mobile phones, watches, or wallets into the exam hall

Eligibility Criteria - Qualification and Age Limit

Candidates checking their eligibility for BEML Operator Recruitment 2026 should know that both educational qualification and age are fixed as on 10 July 2026. This section explains the mandatory ITI qualification and the trade-independent age limit applicable across all five posts.

Educational Qualification (Applicable to All Trades)

  • First-class (60%) marks in the respective ITI trade, along with a National Trade Certificate (NTC) issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT)
  • Completion of Apprenticeship with a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) in the respective trade issued by the Directorate General of Training (DGT)
  • Candidates must have completed the ITI course under the Conventional Training Pattern of the Craftsmen Training Scheme as a regular candidate

Candidates from SC/ST/PwD categories get a 5% relaxation in the minimum qualifying percentage, meaning they need only 55% instead of 60% in their respective trade.

BEML Operator Selection Process 2026 - Step-by-Step

Candidates wondering how BEML will select Operators for these 362 posts can note that the process involves a Computer Based Written Test, document verification, and a pre-employment medical examination, conducted broadly in the sequence below.

  1. Computer Based Written Test: Conducted over 2 hours, with three parts — Part-I: 20 questions on General Awareness, Part-II: 20 questions on English & Reasoning, Part-III: 60 questions on the concerned Discipline. Each question carries 1 mark, and there is no negative marking.
  2. Result and Shortlisting: The qualifying mark is fixed at 45%, relaxed to 40% (5% relaxation) for SC/ST/PwD candidates. Shortlisting is done purely on written test performance.
  3. Document Verification: Candidates are called in order of merit, limited to the number of positions notified per trade/category, where original certificates and one set of self-attested photocopies must be produced.
  4. Travelling Allowance: Candidates who qualify document verification are reimbursed Sleeper Class/II Class train or bus fare by the shortest route, on production of proof of travel.
  5. Provisional Offer and Medical Examination: Candidates clearing document verification receive a Provisional Offer and must undergo a pre-employment medical examination, with no relaxation in health standards.
  6. Final Offer of Engagement: Issued only after a satisfactory medical report is received from the Company's doctor.

Candidates should note that mere fulfilment of eligibility conditions does not guarantee selection, and BEML Management reserves the right to restrict the number of candidates or increase the qualifying percentage based on the volume of applications received.

Candidates can use the Apply Online link only until 18:00 Hrs on 10 July 2026, after which the registration site will close. No request for change in category, address, e-mail, mobile number, or test centre location will be entertained once submitted.

Provident Fund is calculated on Basic Pay plus DA, and selected candidates are also entitled to Gratuity (as per the Gratuity Scheme) and Bonus (as per the Bonus Act). The engagement itself is on a tenure basis for a maximum of four years and does not confer regular employee status.

Documents Required While Applying Online

Candidates often ask what documents are needed beforehand to avoid application rejection — this section lists every mandatory upload required to complete the BEML Operator online application successfully.

  • Recent photograph and signature (on clear white background, signature in black ink)
  • 10th Standard (X-th) marks card
  • ITI - National Trade Certificate (NTC); provisional certificate accepted if final certificate is not yet issued
  • All ITI marks cards as a single PDF (CGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate required, if applicable)

Applications submitted without uploading these documents will be treated as incomplete and summarily rejected, so candidates should keep scanned copies ready before starting the online form.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many candidates lose out on otherwise eligible applications due to small, avoidable errors. This section highlights frequent mistakes applicants should watch out for while applying for this BEML recruitment.

  • Uploading provisional instead of required documents: NTC provisional certificates are accepted, but candidates should still keep the final certificate ready for the joining stage.
  • Entering an inactive e-mail or mobile number: Since all communication, including offer letters, is sent only via the registered e-mail, candidates should use an ID and number valid for at least one year.
  • Ignoring the OBC-NCL certificate validity: The OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate must not be older than six months as on the last date of online application submission, so candidates should get an updated certificate if their existing one is outdated.
  • Missing the CGPA conversion certificate: Candidates with CGPA/credit-based ITI marksheets must attach the official conversion formula/certificate, or their application may be treated as incomplete.
  • Requesting changes after submission: Category, address, e-mail, mobile number, or test centre preference cannot be modified after submission, so candidates should double-check all entries before the final submit.
  • Applying without verifying eligibility: Only candidates who fully meet the qualification, age, and category criteria as on 10 July 2026 should apply, since candidature found ineligible at any stage will be cancelled, even after appointment.
