Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

Applications for this recruitment can be submitted only through the online mode on Bank of Baroda's official website - no offline or postal applications are accepted. The application window is open from 16 June 2026 to 06 July 2026, and registration is complete only once the application fee is successfully paid through the online payment gateway. Candidates can access the application form directly at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm, under the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page on www.bankofbaroda.bank.in.

  • Direct Link to apply Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026

Key Roles and Responsibilities

A few common themes run across most of these positions. The Vice President and Deputy Vice President-level Relationship Head and Senior Relationship Manager roles centre on growing and managing the bank's existing corporate relationships in their specialised segment - real estate, MNCs, credit-lite clients, or conglomerates - sourcing new-to-bank corporate clients, cross-selling fee-based products such as forex and cash management services, and building account plans with opportunity-income analysis while keeping risk exposure within the bank's Exposure Risk Framework. The Transaction Banking roles (Head-Product Sales, Senior Product Sales Manager, and Product Sales Manager) focus on selling trade, forex, and cash management products, managing transaction banking client relationships, and driving fee income and CASA balances. The AVP-level Conglomerate/Real Estate and Credit Lite roles concentrate on credit appraisal, risk evaluation, and timely account monitoring, while the DVP-Head Market Intelligence Unit role is centred on gathering and summarising market and industry intelligence to provide competitive insights to management. Across all positions, the bank has reserved the right to modify or add to these responsibilities at any time.

Application Fee

Bank of Baroda has set a two-tier, non-refundable application fee for this recruitment. Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates must pay Rs 850 (inclusive of GST), plus applicable payment gateway charges, while SC, ST, PWD, Ex-servicemen/DESM, and Women candidates pay Rs 175 (inclusive of GST), plus payment gateway charges. The fee can be paid online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. It is payable irrespective of whether an online test is eventually conducted and irrespective of whether the candidate is shortlisted for an interview, and once paid, it will not be refunded under any circumstances.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Contract Tenure, Remuneration and Credit Score Requirement

These are fixed-term contractual roles, and the tenure depends on the grade. For AVP I and AVP II, the initial contract runs for 5 years from the date of joining and can be renewed at the bank's discretion, subject to satisfactory performance, for one additional period of up to 5 years. For VP and DVP, the initial contract is for 3 years and can be extended in increments of 1 year each, provided the total engagement does not exceed 5 years. In every case, the engagement automatically ends at contract expiry unless renewed, and it cannot continue beyond the candidate reaching 60 years of age.

Remuneration is not fixed in the notification - the bank states it will be decided based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and the prevailing market benchmark for the position, and the place of posting will depend on the bank's requirement at any of its offices or branches in India.

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment is credit history: candidates must have a CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining, and the bank has explicitly stated that candidates who have defaulted on loan or credit card repayments, or against whom adverse reports exist with CIBIL or other credit-rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment - a check the bank can apply at any stage, including after joining.

Selection Process

Selection proceeds through Application Scrutiny, followed by an Online Test, Psychometric Test, or any other test the bank considers suitable, and then a Personal Interview along with compensation negotiation for those selected. The Psychometric Test and/or Interview assess a candidate's personality, communication, clarity, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country. To qualify in the Personal Interview, a candidate must score at least 60% for the Unreserved category and 55% for Reserved category candidates, though the bank reserves the right to revise this cut-off. If multiple candidates tie at the cut-off mark, they are ranked in descending order of age, meaning the older candidate ranks higher.

Call letters will be sent only to the email ID registered in the online application - no hard copies will be sent by post or courier - so candidates must keep that email account active and check it regularly. At the interview, candidates must carry a valid photo ID such as a PAN card, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar card with photograph; a Ration Card will not be accepted as identity proof for this recruitment, and candidates who have legally changed their name must produce the original Gazette notification or affidavit reflecting the new name.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Visit the Bank of Baroda website www.bankofbaroda.bank.in (or directly www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm) and go to the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active throughout the recruitment process, since all call letters and updates will be sent there.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully - no field can be edited once you click Submit - and ensure your name is spelt exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets.
  4. Upload your bio-data, scanned photograph (200×230 pixels, 20-50 KB), and signature (140×60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, along with PDF copies of your eligibility documents.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI through the integrated payment gateway.
  6. After successful payment, download and print the system-generated e-receipt and application form for your records; if a transaction fails, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the first attempt succeeded.
  7. Complete the process well before 06 July 2026, since the bank has advised against waiting until the last date to avoid login failures caused by heavy website traffic.

Documents Required (Upload and Interview)

Two separate sets of documents matter here - what must be uploaded with the online application, and what must be physically produced at the interview.

Documents to upload (PDF format, A4 page size, file size not exceeding 500 KB each):

  • Resume
  • Date of Birth proof (10th mark sheet/certificate)
  • Educational certificates (all relevant mark sheets and certificates scanned into a single PDF)
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable
  • Caste/Category certificate, if applicable
  • PWD certificate, if applicable

Documents to carry to the interview (originals plus a self-attested photocopy):

  • Printout of the valid interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Class X mark sheet showing DOB)
  • Photo ID proof (PAN, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar with photograph - a Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Semester/year-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate in the prescribed Government of India format for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates (the OBC certificate must include the non-creamy-layer clause and be issued within one year of the date of advertisement)
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board for PWD candidates, along with scribe details if a scribe was used
  • Discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof for Ex-servicemen candidates
  • A No Objection Certificate from the current employer for candidates serving in Government, Quasi-Government, or Public Sector roles, including nationalised banks
  • Certificate of eligibility from the Government of India for candidates from Nepal, Bhutan, the Tibetan-refugee category, or the specified person-of-Indian-origin categories
  • Proof of work experience such as appointment letters, salary slips, relieving letters, and CTC break-up documents

Bank of Baroda has also appended ready-to-use certificate formats for SC/ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Persons with Disabilities (single and multiple disability), and EWS candidates as annexures to the notification; candidates applying under these categories should get their certificates issued in this prescribed format from the competent authority.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Keep your scanned photograph between 20-50 KB and your signature between 10-20 KB, both in JPG/JPEG format - files outside this range, or in the wrong format, will trigger an error and block submission. Sign only in your normal handwriting and never in capital letters, since the bank has specified that signatures in capital letters will not be accepted, and any mismatch between your call-letter signature and your interview-day signature can lead to disqualification.

If an online payment fails or you are unsure whether it went through, do not assume it succeeded - register again and complete the payment, since the fee is non-refundable. Use an updated browser and a stable internet connection while filling the form, and avoid waiting until the last day or last few hours before 06 July 2026, since heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions. Always download and save your acknowledgement number, e-receipt, and printed application form immediately after payment, as these are needed for future reference and at the interview. Finally, double-check every field - especially your name, category, and date of birth - before clicking Submit, since no corrections are allowed after the online application has been submitted.

Age Relaxation Rules for Reserved Categories

The age limits mentioned above apply to General category candidates as on 1 June 2026. Candidates from reserved categories get additional years added to the upper age limit, but only for posts where reservation roster points actually exist.

Pay Scale and Salary Structure for Each Grade

Pay for Bank of Baroda C&IC officers follows the standard bipartite settlement scale used across the banking industry, with the figure increasing through fixed annual increments up to a ceiling for each grade. Selected candidates also receive allowances and perquisites as per the bank's policies, in addition to this basic pay.

Grade/Scale Pay Scale (₹) Maximum Basic Pay (₹)
MMG/S-II 64,820 - 2340/1 - 67,160 - 2680/10 - 93,960 93,960
MMG/S-III 85,920 - 2680/5 - 99,320 - 2980/2 - 1,05,280 1,05,280

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

CIBIL Score Requirement: A Credit History Check Unique to This Recruitment

Unlike most government recruitment notifications, this advertisement makes personal credit history a formal eligibility condition. Candidates need a minimum CIBIL score of 680 at the time of joining the bank, since this post involves handling corporate credit decisions.

Anyone who has defaulted on loan repayments or credit card dues, or who has adverse reports from CIBIL or other external credit assessment agencies, will be treated as ineligible for appointment. The bank has reserved the right to reject a candidate's selection at any stage, including after joining, if their credit profile turns out to be unsatisfactory.

Probation Period and Mandatory Service Bond

Selected candidates do not join in a permanent capacity immediately; they first complete a probation period, and they must also commit to a minimum service period backed by a financial bond.

  • Probation Period: 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • Service Bond: Candidates must serve the bank for a minimum of 3 years from the date of joining, or pay ₹5 lakh in lieu of completing the bond period.

The exact bond terms will be confirmed in each selected candidate's offer letter and are subject to revision as per the bank's prevailing policy.

Application Fee for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

The application fee for this recruitment is fixed by category and must be paid online; it is non-refundable even if the online test is not conducted or the candidate is not shortlisted for an interview.

Category Application Fee
General, EWS & OBC ₹850 (inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges
SC, ST, PWD, ESM/DESM & Women ₹175 (inclusive of GST) + Payment Gateway Charges

Selection Process: Online Test, Psychometric Assessment & Interview

Selection for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026 can include application scrutiny, an online test, a psychometric assessment, a group discussion, and a personal interview, though the bank retains the right to skip or modify any stage. Final selection depends on combined performance across whichever stages are actually conducted.

Online Test Pattern (Tentative)

If a written test is held, it will be a 150-mark, 150-minute online exam split into four sections, three of which only need to be passed rather than scored well in.

Section Test Questions Marks Duration
1 Reasoning 25 25 75 minutes (combined)
2 English Language 25 25
3 Quantitative Aptitude 25 25
4 Professional Knowledge 75 150 75 minutes
Total 150 225 150 minutes

Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge will be available bilingually in English and Hindi, while the English Language section will be in English only. Sections 1 to 3 are qualifying only and do not count toward the final score; candidates need at least 40% in General/EWS or 35% in Reserved categories to clear each of these sections, and there is no negative marking anywhere in the test.

Personal Interview & Final Merit

Candidates who clear the online test (or are otherwise shortlisted) move on to a psychometric assessment and/or personal interview, where the minimum qualifying score is 60% for General category and 55% for Reserved category candidates. If two or more candidates tie at the cut-off mark, the older candidate is ranked higher in the merit list.

The online test, if conducted, is tentatively planned across more than two dozen cities, including Mumbai, Delhi/NCR, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar, Jaipur, Lucknow, Baroda, Bhopal, Chandigarh-Mohali, and several other regional centres, with the final allotted centre confirmed in the call letter.

Documents Required During the Recruitment Process

Candidates do not need to upload every certificate while registering online, but they must be ready to produce the following documents in original, along with self-attested photocopies, at the interview stage or whenever the bank asks for them.

  • Printout of the interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate, SSLC/Std. X marksheet, or equivalent)
  • A valid photo identity proof such as PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, or Aadhaar card (Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Year-wise/semester-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate for SC/ST/OBC candidates, with the OBC certificate carrying a valid non-creamy-layer clause
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board, for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities
  • Income and Asset Certificate, for candidates applying under the EWS category
  • Service/discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof, for ex-servicemen candidates
  • No Objection Certificate from the current employer, for candidates already working in government, quasi-government, or public sector roles
  • Documentary proof of declared work experience, such as appointment letters, salary slips, or relieving letters

Step-by-Step Guide: How to Apply Online

Bank of Baroda accepts applications for this recruitment only through its official website; no offline or postal applications will be considered.

  1. Visit www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and navigate to the Careers section, then Current Opportunities.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active until the recruitment process is complete.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and work experience details carefully, since no changes are allowed once the form is submitted.
  4. Upload your photograph (200 x 230 pixels, 20-50 KB) and signature (140 x 60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, signed in your normal handwriting and not in capital letters.
  5. Upload your resume, Date of Birth proof, educational certificates (combined in one PDF), and category/PWD/experience certificates where applicable, each as a PDF on A4 size not exceeding 500 KB.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  7. Save and print the system-generated application form and fee receipt for your future reference.

Apply Online for Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026

Job Profile: What Will You Actually Do in This Role?

The two job families under this recruitment involve noticeably different day-to-day work, which is worth understanding before choosing which post to apply for.

Credit Analyst roles (Manager/Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are appraisal-focused: examining new and existing corporate credit proposals, conducting credit due-diligence on financial, industry, and business risk, coordinating with Relationship Managers, and ensuring compliance in corporate accounts.

C&IC Relationship roles (Senior Manager/Chief Manager) are client-facing: maintaining relationships with existing corporate clients, sourcing new-to-bank corporate borrowers, cross-selling ancillary business, and creating account plans with opportunity income analysis for corporate borrowers.

Mistakes That Could Cost You This Opportunity

Several avoidable errors can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate from Bank of Baroda C&IC Recruitment 2026, so it helps to check these before hitting submit.

  • Assuming any postgraduate degree qualifies - only a finance-specialised PG degree/diploma or a CA/CMA/CS/CFA qualification meets the educational criteria.
  • Not checking your CIBIL score in advance - a score below 680, or any default history, can lead to rejection even after selection.
  • Counting clerical-cadre banking experience toward the eligibility criteria, which is explicitly excluded.
  • Including work experience of less than 6 months from a previous organisation, which will not be counted unless it is part of your current employment.
  • Submitting more than one application - only the latest valid one is retained, and fees paid for earlier ones are forfeited.
  • Selecting a category casually, since no change of category is allowed after registration and an invalid OBC/EWS claim without supporting certificates can affect your candidature.
  • Overlooking the 3-year/₹5 lakh service bond commitment before deciding whether to accept the role if selected.
  • Waiting until the last date to register, risking last-minute website load issues for which the bank takes no responsibility.

MSC Bank Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility requirements differ by post for both educational qualifications and age limits. All candidates must have passed the Matriculation Examination with Marathi as one of the subjects and must be domiciled in Maharashtra State (Domicile Certificate is mandatory). Age is calculated as on 01 June 2026.

1. Trainee Junior Officer (49 Posts)

  • Education: Graduate in any discipline with at least 50% marks. Candidates with Bachelors/Masters in Law or JAIIB/CAIIB/MSCIT certifications, or work experience in Treasury/International Banking will be preferred.
  • Experience: Minimum 2 years' experience in Banking field, preferably in Urban/DCC Bank as an Officer (Officer Cadre — first level where Clerk level exists, or second level where it does not).
  • Age Limit: Minimum 23 years – Maximum 35 years (born not earlier than 01 June 1991).

2. Trainee Associate (81 Posts)

  • Education: Graduate in any discipline with at least 50% marks. Preference for Government Commercial Certificate in Marathi and English typing; proficiency in Computer Applications required.
  • Experience: Not mandatory; preference for candidates with Co-operative Intern experience in StCB/DCC Banks.
  • Age Limit: Minimum 21 years – Maximum 32 years (born not earlier than 01 June 1994).

3. Trainee Typist – Associate Grade (04 Posts)

  • Education: Graduate in any discipline with Marathi in Matriculation. Must possess Government Commercial Certificate Exam — 30 w.p.m. in Marathi typing and 40 w.p.m. in English typing. Proficiency in Word Processing and Spread Sheet required.
  • Experience: Not mandatory; preference for DTP Operator experience. Preference for Marathi/English stenography course holders.
  • Age Limit: Minimum 21 years – Maximum 28 years (born not earlier than 01 June 1998).

4. Trainee Driver (05 Posts)

  • Education: Matriculation (S.S.C.) Examination with Marathi as one of the subjects and a valid LMV licence.
  • Experience: Not mandatory.
  • Age Limit: Minimum 18 years – Maximum 30 years (born not earlier than 01 June 1996).
  • Special relaxation: Children of MSC Bank employees get 5 years relaxation on maximum age for Trainee Driver post.

MSC Bank Recruitment 2026 - Salary / Stipend & Pay Scale

All selected candidates will be engaged as Trainees for 12 months, during which a monthly stipend is paid. After successful training, candidates are placed in the Bank's regular grade with revised emoluments. Post-confirmation, a probation of 6 months follows before permanent absorption.

MSC Bank Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The selection methodology varies by post but all posts involve an online written examination conducted by IBPS, followed by an additional stage specific to the post. Candidates must score at least 50% (100 marks out of 200) in the written test for officer/associate posts and 50% (60 marks out of 120) for the Driver post to be shortlisted for the next round.

Service Bond / Consent Deposit

Candidates wondering about post-appointment obligations should note that selected candidates must execute an undertaking on Rs. 500/- stamp paper committing to serve MSC Bank for a minimum of 4 years from the date of joining. In case of default, voluntary resignation, or termination before the expiry of 4 years, the candidate is required to pay Rs. 10,00,000/- (Ten Lakh) as liquidated damages and execute a surety bond for Rs. 1,00,000/- from two income tax payees as sureties.

How to Apply for MSC Bank Recruitment 2026

The entire application process is online through the MSC Bank career portal. Physical applications will not be accepted under any circumstances. Candidates should keep their scanned documents ready before beginning registration.

Documents to scan before applying:

  • Photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm, passport style, colour, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB)
  • Signature (black ink on white paper, 140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB)
  • Left thumb impression (white paper, black/blue ink, 240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB)
  • Handwritten declaration in English on white paper with black ink (800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB)

Declaration text: "I, _______ (Name), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required."

Step-by-step application process:

  1. Visit https://msc.bank.in/career and click "APPLY ONLINE".
  2. Click "Click here for New Registration" and enter Name, Contact details, and Email ID. Note the Provisional Registration Number and Password sent via SMS and email.
  3. Log in and fill the application form. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to save progress at each step.
  4. Upload Photograph, Signature, Left Thumb Impression, and Handwritten Declaration as per specifications.
  5. Fill remaining application details and click "Validate Your Details" followed by "Save & Next".
  6. Preview the complete application using the "Preview Tab" and verify all entries.
  7. Click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" after final verification.
  8. Proceed to the Payment Tab and pay the application fee online.
  9. Click "Submit" and save/print the e-Receipt and application form for future reference.

Only one application per candidate is allowed. In case of multiple applications, only the latest will be retained and earlier fees will be forfeited.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Many applicants lose their candidature due to avoidable errors during or after the application process. Review the following checklist before submitting your form.

  • Applying for multiple posts: MSC Bank allows one application per candidate. Submit only one application for the post you are most qualified for.
  • Wrong photograph format: Passport-style colour photo against a light background is required. Selfies, group photos, or blurred images will lead to rejection.
  • Signature in CAPITAL LETTERS: Signatures in block/capital letters are strictly rejected. Sign in your normal cursive style with black ink.
  • Missing Domicile Certificate: Only Maharashtra residents can apply. Ensure your Domicile Certificate is valid and ready for document verification.
  • Not checking Marathi in SSC: All posts require Marathi as a subject in Matriculation. Check your mark sheet before applying.
  • Pressing Back/Refresh during payment: After submitting payment information, do not press Back or Refresh. Wait for the server confirmation to avoid double charges.
  • Incomplete scanning of thumb impression: The left thumb impression must be properly scanned and not smudged. A blurred or partial impression can invalidate your application.
  • Not saving the e-Receipt: If an e-Receipt is not generated, the transaction may have failed. Log in again and repeat the payment process.

Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for these IT leadership roles is assessed as on the cut-off date, and the Bank has linked position-specific qualification and experience details separately for each post rather than listing them within the main notification.

The detailed educational qualification and work experience criteria for each of the 5 posts - VP Head-AI, VP Head Platform Engineering, DVP Dy. Head Cloud CoE, DVP Dy. Head IT Infrastructure, and DVP Dy. Head Platform Engineering - are provided through separate position-specific links on the Bank's official notification, since each senior IT role has its own distinct skill and experience requirements.

General Eligibility Conditions

  • Eligibility is reckoned as on the cut-off date of 01-06-2026.
  • Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organization as on 01-06-2026 will not be counted toward eligibility, unless that experience is part of the candidate's current employment.
  • Candidates must be a Citizen of India, or fall under specific categories such as a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who settled in India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from select countries with the intention of permanently settling in India.
  • OBC candidates falling under the "creamy layer" are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply under the General category.

VP Head- AI B.E. or B.Tech. in Computer Science/ Information Technology/ any relevant field or MCA
VP Head Platform Engineering B.E./ B.Tech. in Computer Science or Information Technology/ Electronics & Tele Communication/ Electrical & Electronics OR MCA
DVP Dy. Head Cloud CoE (Centre of Excellence) B.E./ B.Tech. in Computer Science or Information Technology/ Electronics & Tele Communication/ Electrical & Electronics OR MCA

Application Fee

Candidates often want to know the cost of applying before starting their application. For this recruitment, Bank of Baroda has kept the process completely free.

The application fee is Nil for all categories of candidates applying for these 5 IT positions.

CIBIL Score and Credit History Requirement

Unlike most government job notifications, this Bank of Baroda recruitment includes a specific financial credibility check. This is an important and somewhat unique eligibility condition candidates must be aware of.

Candidates must maintain a satisfactory credit history, and a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above is required at the time of joining. Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or credit card dues, or against whom adverse reports exist from CIBIL or other external credit rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment. The Bank reserves the right to reject candidature at any stage, including after joining, if the credit profile is found unsatisfactory.

Remuneration and Location of Posting

Salary for these roles is not fixed on a standard pay scale, unlike typical government recruitment. This section explains how pay is determined and where selected candidates will be posted.

Remuneration will be offered based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and market benchmark - there is no fixed pay scale mentioned in the notification. The location of posting is Mumbai or Hyderabad, though selected candidates remain liable for transfer anywhere in India as per the Bank's requirement.

Selection Process

Selection for these IT leadership posts goes beyond a standard written exam, with the Bank assessing multiple professional parameters. No fixed exam date or selection timeline has been announced in the notification.

The selection process may include an online test, a psychometric test, or any other test the Bank deems suitable, followed by an Interview or multiple interviews. The Bank may shortlist applications based on criteria such as suitability for the role, depth of prior experience, leadership exposure, domain expertise, professional certifications, and exposure to regulatory or compliance frameworks. The minimum qualifying mark for the Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for UR category and 55% for Reserved category candidates.

How to Apply Online for Bank of Baroda IT Recruitment 2026

Applications for these posts can only be submitted online, with no other mode accepted. Here is the step-by-step process candidates need to follow.

  1. Visit the Bank's official website and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities page.
  2. Register online using the application format enabled for this recruitment.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking SUBMIT.
  4. Upload your Bio-data, scanned photograph, signature, and supporting eligibility documents as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Verify all entered details, including name, category, date of birth, and post applied for, before final submission.
  6. Submit the application well before 10-07-2026 to avoid last-minute website load issues.
  7. Save the acknowledgement number generated on the portal and check your registered email for confirmation - registration is complete only once this acknowledgement is received.

Documents and Upload Specifications

Bank of Baroda requires specific documents to be uploaded at the time of application, each with strict file format and size requirements. Getting these specifications wrong is a common reason applications get stuck.

Documents to Upload (Application Stage)

  • Resume (PDF)
  • DOB Proof: 10th marksheet/certificate (PDF)
  • Educational Certificates: relevant mark-sheets/certificates, scanned in a single PDF file
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable (PDF)
  • Caste/Category Certificate, if applicable (PDF)
  • PWD certificate, if applicable (PDF)

Photograph and Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: recent passport-style colour picture, dimensions 200 x 230 pixels, file size between 20kb–50kb.
  • Signature: signed in black ink on white paper, dimensions 140 x 60 pixels, file size between 10kb–20kb.
  • Document files: must be in PDF format, A4 page size, and not exceeding 500 KB each.

Documents Required at Interview Stage

At the time of interview, candidates must produce originals along with self-attested photocopies of documents including the call letter printout, system-generated application printout, date of birth proof, photo identity proof, mark sheets and degree certificates, and category certificates where applicable. Notably, a Ration Card will not be accepted as valid identity proof for this recruitment.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Given the strict, no-correction-after-submission policy of this recruitment, small errors can have a big impact. The following points can help candidates avoid losing their candidature.

  • Do not submit the application without double-checking every field - no changes are allowed once you click SUBMIT.
  • Do not upload a photograph or signature outside the specified pixel and file-size limits, as the system will reject non-compliant files.
  • Do not assume your credit history is irrelevant - a CIBIL score below 680 or any adverse credit report can make you ineligible.
  • Do not delay applying until the last day; server load near the 10-07-2026 deadline can prevent successful submission.
  • Do not carry a Ration Card as your only ID proof for the interview - it will not be accepted.
  • Do not forget to check the position-specific eligibility link for your chosen post, since detailed qualifications differ by role.

The maximum ages above apply to General category and EWS candidates. SC/ST candidates receive 5 years of relaxation in the upper age limit; OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates receive 3 years; Persons with Benchmark Disabilities receive 10 years; Ex-Servicemen (with at least 5 years' military service) receive 5 years; and persons affected by the 1984 riots receive 5 years. SC/ST/OBC candidates may combine their category relaxation with only one of the remaining relaxation categories.

Educational Qualification and Work Experience

Post 1 - Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (MMGS II) Mandatory qualification: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Science & Engineering, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or Electronics & Communications Engineering (or equivalent) from a university/institute recognized by the Government of India, UGC, or AICTE. Preferred certifications include AWS Solutions Architect (Associate/Professional), Azure Administrator, DevOps Engineer, or Google Associate/Professional Cloud Engineer.

Work experience required: Minimum 4 years of post-qualification experience in IT Industry, BFSI, or the IT vertical of an organization, of which at least 2 years must be specifically in cloud administration or cloud engineering roles.

Post 2 - Manager, AI Engineers (MMGS II) Mandatory qualification: Full-time B.E./B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or Machine Learning - OR - full-time MCA/M.Tech in AI, Machine Learning, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field - from a university/institution recognized by the Government of India, AICTE, or UGC. Candidates must also hold at least one professional certification (valid as on the date of eligibility) in AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Data Science, or Generative AI from a recognized university, reputed technology organization, or professional certification body.

Work experience: Minimum 6 years (post B.E./B.Tech/MCA) in AI/ML development, Data Science, or Advanced Analytics, including at least 2 years leading or managing AI/ML projects or teams - OR - Minimum 5 years (post M.Tech) with the same specialization, including the same 2-year leadership requirement.

Post 3 - Senior Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (MMGS III) Same mandatory degree requirement as Post 1. Preferred certifications: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional), Azure Administrator, DevOps Engineer, or Google Associate/Professional Cloud Engineer.

Work experience: Minimum 6 years post-qualification experience in IT/BFSI, of which at least 3 years in cloud architecture or cloud engineering roles.

Post 4 - Senior Manager, AI Engineers (MMGS III) Same mandatory degree and certification requirements as Post 2 (Manager AI Engineers).

Work experience: Minimum 4 years (post B.E./B.Tech/MCA) in AI/ML development, Data Science, or Advanced Analytics - OR - Minimum 3 years (post M.Tech) in the same domains.

Post 5 - Chief Manager, Cloud Centre of Excellence (SMGS IV) Same mandatory degree as Posts 1 and 3, plus a mandatory intermediate certification from Microsoft Azure. Preferred additional qualifications: MCA or M.Tech/M.Sc in Computer Science, IT, or Electronics & Communications Engineering. Preferred certifications: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional), Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or Google Professional Cloud Architect.

Work experience: Minimum 8 years post-qualification experience in IT/BFSI, of which at least 4 years in cloud architecture, cloud engineering, or DevOps roles.

Candidates should note that 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%, and 54.99% as less than 55%, when calculating percentage of marks. Where a university awards CGPA/OGPA, candidates must convert it to percentage and indicate that figure in the online application.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is non-refundable. Payment must be made online only - cash, cheques, money orders, and postal stamps are not accepted. Bank transaction charges for the online payment gateway are borne by the candidate.

Category Application Fee
SC / ST / PwBD ₹100 + applicable taxes + payment gateway charges
General, EWS & OBC ₹850 + applicable taxes + payment gateway charges

Once submitted, an application cannot be withdrawn, and the fee will not be refunded under any circumstances, nor held in reserve for any other examination.

Punjab and Sind Bank Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The bank will use a multi-stage selection process for all posts. All three scales - SMGS IV, MMGS III, and MMGS II - follow the same procedure: Written Test → Short-listing → Personal Interview.

The written test, where conducted, will have the following structure:

Section Questions Maximum Marks Duration
English Language 20 20 15 minutes
General Awareness 20 20 30 minutes
Professional Knowledge 60 60 60 minutes
Total 100 100 105 minutes

The minimum qualifying score in each section is 40% for General and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved Category candidates. However, only Professional Knowledge marks are used for drawing the merit/rank list and shortlisting candidates for the Personal Interview; marks in English Language and General Awareness are not included in the final merit calculation.

Candidates clearing the written test are called for a Personal Interview. The minimum qualifying score for the interview is 40% for Unreserved and EWS candidates and 35% for Reserved categories. Final selection is based on the combined marks from the written test and Personal Interview, in order of merit ranking. Where two candidates tie at the cut-off, they are ranked in descending order of age.

The Personal Interview will be conducted in New Delhi unless otherwise specified. Call letters will be sent by email only. Candidates must attend at their own cost.

The bank shortlists candidates based on experience and suitability at its own discretion - meeting the minimum qualification does not guarantee an interview call.

Examination Centres

The bank has designated examination centres across India. Candidates may opt for a centre in their state, subject to availability. The bank reserves the right to allot a different centre or cancel/add centres. No request for a change of examination centre, date, or session will be entertained. Selected centres include: Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Guwahati (Assam), Patna and Bhagalpur (Bihar), Chandigarh/Mohali, Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Delhi/Delhi-NCR, Panaji (Goa), Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar (Gujarat), Ambala (Haryana), Hamirpur (Himachal Pradesh), Jammu (J&K), Bengaluru (Karnataka), Ernakulam (Kerala), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Mumbai/Thane/Navi Mumbai/MMR (Maharashtra), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Patiala (Punjab), Jaipur (Rajasthan), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), Hyderabad (Telangana), Prayagraj, Lucknow and Meerut (Uttar Pradesh), Dehradun (Uttarakhand), and Asansol and Siliguri (West Bengal), among others.

Terms of Contract

This engagement is on a contractual basis, not a regular/permanent appointment. The initial period is three years, subject to annual performance review. Depending on need and performance, the bank may extend the contract on an annual basis for up to a maximum of two additional years at its discretion.

The bank may terminate the contract at any time without assigning any reason by giving one month's notice or paying one month's fixed component of compensation in lieu. Similarly, the appointee must give the bank one month's clear notice - or equivalent payment - to exit the contract before its expiry.

Additional conditions: the selected individual must not take up any assignment with any other organization during the contract period; no vigilance case or adverse observation from previous employers should be pending; and the candidate must have a minimum CIBIL score of 650 at the time of joining.

How to Apply

Applications are accepted online only through the bank's official website. The steps below reflect the application flow described in the notification.

  1. Visit https://punjabandsind.bank.in/ and navigate to the Recruitment section on the home page.
  2. Click on the relevant notification for Cloud CoE / AI Engineers.
  3. Before starting registration, scan and prepare the following files:
    • Passport-size photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm; 20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG/PNG)
    • Signature on white paper in black ink (10–20 KB)
    • Left thumb impression on white paper (20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG)
    • Hand-written declaration in English, on white paper in black ink - text: "I, [Name], hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." (50–100 KB; JPG/JPEG; NOT in capital letters)
    • Supporting documents in PDF format: Brief Resume, ID Proof, Age Proof, Educational Certificates, Experience Certificates/NOC, Caste Certificate (if applicable)
  4. Complete the online registration form. Keep the registered email ID and mobile number active throughout the process.
  5. Upload all documents at the specified fields. The system will not proceed until photographs and signatures meet specifications.
  6. Pay the application fee online. Transaction charges are borne by the candidate.
  7. Submit the application and save/print the system-generated application form with the registration number.
  8. Apply separately for each post if applying for more than one position.

In case of multiple submissions for the same post, only the last valid completed application will be retained; fees paid for earlier submissions will be forfeited.

Documents Required at Document Verification

Candidates called for the interview stage must bring originals and self-attested photocopies of all relevant documents. Documents not produced on the day of verification will disqualify the candidate from further participation.

Required documents include: Date of Birth proof (SSC/School Leaving Certificate); printout of call letter; system-generated online application printout; all educational certificates and mark sheets from Class X onwards (semester-wise mark sheets and provisional/final degree certificate); all work experience certificates and NOC from the current employer if employed with a public sector bank or government/quasi-government organization; caste/category certificates in the prescribed Government of India format (OBC certificate must be no more than one year old and contain the non-creamy layer clause); disability certificate from District Medical Board (if applicable); Income and Asset Certificate (for EWS candidates, valid as on the date of application); two passport-size photographs identical to the one in the application; and valid photo identity proof (PAN Card, Passport, Driving Licence, Voter's Card, Aadhaar, Employee ID, etc. - Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are not accepted).

No documents should be sent directly to the bank before or after the interview.

Troubleshooting & Common Mistakes

Photo/Signature upload errors are among the most common reasons for application failure. Ensure your photograph is between 20 KB and 50 KB and your signature between 10 KB and 20 KB. Files larger than the specified limit will be rejected by the system. Use a scanner set to at least 200 DPI and save files in JPG/JPEG format. All supporting documents must be in PDF format.

Payment gateway failures can occur during high-traffic periods near the deadline. If a payment is deducted but the fee status is not updated, wait 24 hours and check again before attempting re-payment; duplicate payments are generally not refunded. Avoid applying on the last day to reduce the risk of server overload.

Hand-written declaration errors are a unique pitfall in this recruitment. The declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, in lowercase (not capital letters). A typed or third-party-written declaration will invalidate the application.

Name mismatches between the application and identity documents can cause disqualification at any stage. Ensure the name (and father's/husband's name where applicable) is spelled exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets. Candidates who have changed their name must produce an original Gazette notification, marriage certificate, or affidavit.

CIBIL score is a condition of joining, not selection. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying - a score below 650 will disqualify them at the time of joining even if selected.

The Railway Recruitment Board has released the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 on 22 June 2026, giving candidates their first look at where they'll sit for the second-stage exam on 2 July 2026. If you applied under CEN 05/2025 for Junior Engineer, Depot Material Superintendent, or Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant posts, you can now log in with your registration number and date of birth to check your allotted exam city, ahead of the admit card that follows on 28 June 2026.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

This guide walks you through the direct download link, the zone-wise login portals, exam shift timings, and exactly what the slip does (and doesn't) tell you so you can start planning your travel right away.

What Is the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026?

Before downloading anything, it helps to know exactly what this document is and isn't. Here's the short answer: it's an advance notice of your exam city, not your entry ticket to the exam hall.

The city intimation slip is a preliminary notice issued by RRB purely to tell candidates which city their CBT 2 exam centre will fall in. It does not carry the exact venue address, reporting time, or entry instructions those details arrive only with the admit card. The slip exists so candidates have enough lead time to book trains, buses, or accommodation if their allotted city is far from home, rather than scrambling once the admit card lands just days before the exam.

RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 - Key Details at a Glance

This table sums up the entire update in one place useful if you just want the core facts without scrolling through the full article.

Particulars Details

Posts Covered Junior Engineer (JE), Depot Material Superintendent (DMS), Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA)
Stage CBT 2 (Second Stage Computer-Based Test)
City Intimation Slip Release Date 22 June 2026
CBT 2 Admit Card Release Date 28 June 2026
CBT 2 Exam Date 2 July 2026
Number of Shifts 3
Login Credentials Required Registration Number + Date of Birth/Password
Official Website rrbcdg.gov.in (and respective zonal RRB sites)

RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 Direct Download Link

The Railway Recruitment Board activated the city intimation login link on its official regional portals on 22 June 2026. Candidates need to click through to the login page, enter their registration number and date of birth, and the system will display the allotted exam city on screen.

Direct Link: RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026

Keep in mind that the city slip itself is not downloadable as a print-ready hall ticket the way an admit card is it simply displays your allotted city, state, exam date, and shift on screen after login. Note this down or take a screenshot for your own reference.

How to Check the RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 (Step-by-Step)

If this is your first time accessing the city slip, follow these steps exactly to avoid login errors.

The process is identical across all RRB zones, though each zone uses its own regional website. Here's the complete sequence:

  1. Visit the official website of the RRB zone you applied under (see the zone-wise list below).
  2. On the homepage, look under the "Latest News" or "Notice Board" section for the link reading "CEN 05/2025 RRB JE CBT 2 City Intimation Slip 2026."
  3. Click the link you'll be redirected to a login page.
  4. Enter your Registration Number (the unique ID sent to your email/mobile after form submission) and your Date of Birth in DDMMYYYY format as the password.
  5. Enter the CAPTCHA code shown on screen.
  6. Click Submit/Login to view your allotted exam city, state, date, and shift.
  7. Note down or screenshot the details for your own records, since this isn't a printable document like the admit card.

What Information Does the RRB JE City Slip Actually Contain?

Knowing what's printed on the slip helps you double-check your own details for accuracy the moment you log in.

The city intimation slip is intentionally limited to preliminary identification and location details nothing related to the exact venue. Specifically, it shows:

  • Candidate's full name
  • Registration number
  • Post applied for (JE/DMS/CMA)
  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Assigned shift number

What it does not include: the exact exam centre name, full address, reporting time, or gate closure time. Those appear only on the admit card.

RRB JE CBT 2 Exam Shift Timings 2026

Since the CBT 2 exam runs across three shifts in a single day, knowing your assigned slot matters for planning your morning (or afternoon, or evening).

The exam is conducted as a 120-minute computer-based test, split into three shifts to accommodate the large candidate pool appearing under CEN 05/2025. Reporting and gate closure times are strict, so candidates should plan to arrive well ahead of the listed closure time.

Shift Reporting Time Gate Closure Time Exam Start Time
Shift 1 7:30 AM 8:30 AM 9:00 AM
Shift 2 11:15 AM 12:15 PM 12:45 PM
Shift 3 3:00 PM 4:00 PM 4:30 PM

Your exact shift assignment will be confirmed on both the city intimation slip and, later, the admit card always go by what's printed on your own document rather than assuming a shift based on this table.

RRB JE City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card: What's the Difference?

A lot of candidates confuse the two, so here's a direct comparison to clear that up.

The city slip and the admit card serve entirely different purposes, even though both relate to the same exam. The city slip is informational only; the admit card is your mandatory entry document.

Feature City Intimation Slip Admit Card
Purpose Advance notice to help plan travel Official entry pass for the exam hall
Typical Release Window ~10 days before exam ~4 days before exam
Venue Detail City and state only Full centre name and address
Valid for Exam Entry No Yes, mandatory

RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026: What Comes Next

Once you've checked your city, the next document to watch for is the admit card the one you'll actually need on exam day.

The RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026 will be released on 28 June 2026, four days ahead of the 2 July exam. Unlike the city slip, the admit card carries the complete exam centre address, your final reporting time, gate closure time, and exam-day instructions. It must be downloaded, printed, and carried to the centre along with a valid photo ID entry will not be permitted without it.

To download the admit card when it goes live:

  1. Visit your respective regional RRB website.
  2. Click on the RRB JE CBT 2 Admit Card 2026 link.
  3. Log in using your registration number and date of birth.
  4. Download and print the admit card for exam day.

Why the City Intimation Slip Matters for Your Exam Preparation

Beyond just travel logistics, this slip plays a small but useful role in your overall exam-day planning.

For candidates allotted a city outside their home district or state, the 10-day notice window gives enough time to book economical travel and accommodation before prices spike closer to the exam date. It also lets you start factoring in local travel time to the (eventual) centre address once the admit card is out, rather than discovering on day one that your city is several hours from your stay.

The Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) is expected to release the RRB Group D Result 2026 in the 4th week of June 2026 at the official website rrbcdg.gov.in, following the disposal of the Telangana High Court case that had earlier put a hold on the result. Over 1.08 crore candidates who appeared for the Computer Based Test (CBT) under CEN 08/2024 for 32,438 Level 1 vacancies can check their merit list, scorecard, and zone-wise cut off marks once the result is declared. This article covers everything candidates need to know the latest court case update, how to check the result, scorecard details, cut off expectations, and the next stage of selection.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

RRB Group D Result 2026 - Latest Update

This section explains the most recent development in the RRB Group D result timeline, including the court case status and the revised expected release date.

The Telangana High Court has disposed of the petition concerning Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) weightage marks on 16th June 2026, removing the stay that had earlier delayed the result. With the legal hurdle cleared, the Railway Recruitment Board is now expected to declare the RRB Group D Result 2026 in the 4th week of June 2026, along with the scorecard, merit list, and cut off marks. As a precautionary step, the court has directed RRB to keep 15 vacancies reserved until final disposal of the main writ petition, while the remaining 32,423 posts will be filled through the regular recruitment process. RRB has also opened an application modification window for CCAA candidates from 17th June to 23rd June 2026, allowing them to update NCVT certificate details and marks before the result is finalised.

RRB Group D Result 2026 Overview

This section gives a quick snapshot of the exam, vacancies, and important result-related dates for CEN 08/2024 in one place.

Particulars Details
Exam Name RRB Group D
Conducting Body Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)
Advertisement Number CEN 08/2024
Posts Pointsman, Assistant, Track Maintainer, Assistant Loco Shed, Assistant Operations, Assistant TL & AC
Post Level Level 1 (7th CPC Pay Matrix)
Total Vacancies 32,438
Exam Dates 27th November 2025 to 10th February 2026
Answer Key Released 17th February 2026
CCAA Application Modification Window 17th June to 23rd June 2026
Result Date 4th week of June 2026 (Expected)
Scorecard Release 4th week of June 2026 (Expected)
Total Candidates Appeared 10,822,423
Selection Process CBT, PET, Document Verification, Medical Test
Official Website rrbcdg.gov.in and respective zonal RRB websites

Why Was the RRB Group D Result Delayed?

This section explains the background of the court case that caused the delay in declaring the result.

The result was delayed due to a case filed in the Telangana High Court relating to the weightage given to Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) candidates in the final merit list. The dispute arose after a 2022 policy change by the Skill Development Ministry altered the earlier exemption available to apprenticeship candidates, prompting petitioners to demand restoration of the older selection system. Since the outcome could affect zone-wise rankings and cut off marks, RRB suspended further processing of the result until the court's verdict. With the case now disposed of, the court has directed the Directorate General of Training (DGT) to examine the representations on the 2022 policy change, and has instructed Railway authorities to conduct proper scrutiny of CCAA candidates during document verification.

How to Check RRB Group D Result 2026 at rrbcdg.gov.in

This section lists the step-by-step process candidates need to follow once the result link is activated.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective regional RRB (for example, rrbcdg.gov.in).
  2. Look for the result link titled "CEN-RRB-08/2024 (Pay Level-1 Posts): CBT Result & Score Card."
  3. Click on the relevant zone-wise result/merit list link.
  4. Download the result PDF that appears on the screen.
  5. Use Ctrl + F to search for your registration number or roll number in the PDF.
  6. Log in with your registration number and date of birth to view your individual scorecard.
  7. Download and print the result for future reference.

RRB Group D Scorecard 2026: What It Will Contain

This section explains where the scorecard will be available and what details candidates should verify on it.

The RRB Group D Scorecard 2026 will be released along with the result on the candidate login portal at rrb.digialm.com. Candidates must check every detail on the scorecard carefully to avoid discrepancies later. The scorecard will typically include:

  • Candidate's Name
  • Registration Number
  • Date of Birth and Gender
  • Roll Number
  • Father's/Mother's Name
  • Category and Quota Sub-Category (if applicable)
  • Total Exam Marks and Marks Scored
  • Total Cut-Off Score
  • RRB Region/Zone Venue

RRB Group D Merit List 2026: Zone-Wise Release

This section explains how the merit list will be structured and how candidates can locate their result within it.

The RRB Group D Merit List 2026 will be released separately for each of the RRB's 21 regional zones in PDF format, containing the roll numbers of shortlisted candidates. Since the list runs into thousands of roll numbers, candidates are advised to use the Ctrl + F search function within the PDF to quickly locate their roll number instead of scrolling manually. The result and merit list will be published on each zone's respective official website, including rrbcdg.gov.in (Chandigarh), rrbmumbai.gov.in, rrbchennai.gov.in, rrbkolkata.gov.in, rrbbpl.nic.in, and other zonal RRB portals.

RRB Group D Cut Off 2026: What to Expect

This section explains how the cut off marks will be determined and where they will be published.

The RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 will be released zone-wise and category-wise (UR, OBC, SC, ST, EWS) along with the result and merit list. Since the CBT was conducted across multiple shifts over several months, RRB applies an equi-percentile normalisation method to ensure fairness raw marks in each shift are converted to a percentile scale, and this normalised score (not the raw score) is used to prepare the final merit list. As per the official notification, the minimum qualifying marks are:

Category Minimum Qualifying Marks
UR / EWS 40%
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) / SC 30%
ST 25%

Candidates must clear both the category-wise qualifying marks and the overall zone cut off to be considered for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET).

What Happens After the RRB Group D Result 2026?

This section explains the next stages in the selection process that follow the result declaration.

Candidates who qualify in the CBT will be shortlisted for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET), which is qualifying in nature meaning candidates only need to clear it, and PET marks are not added to the final merit. Those who clear the PET will then proceed to Document Verification, where original certificates, identity proof, and category certificates (including NCVT/CCAA documents, given the recent court directions) must be presented. CCAA candidates should particularly note that RRB will conduct proper scrutiny and eligibility verification of their certificates during this stage, as directed by the Telangana High Court.

The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB) have opened a special CCAA Modification Window 2026 for candidates under CEN No. 08/2024, popularly known as RRB Group D recruitment. The window is open from 17 June 2026 (00:01 hrs) to 23 June 2026 (23:59 hrs), allowing eligible Course Completed Act Apprentice (CCAA) candidates who appeared in the CBT but had not entered their NCVT examination marks to update this information online before the deadline closes.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

This is a one-time, time-bound opportunity. If you are a CCAA candidate and missed filling in your NCVT marks at the time of applying, this article explains exactly who can use this window, what you need to update, the step-by-step process, and what happens if you miss the deadline.

Click Here: RRB CCAA Modification Window 2026

RRB CCAA Modification Window 2026 - Key Highlights

This section gives a quick snapshot of the most important facts about the modification window the recruitment body, notification number, opening and closing dates, and who it applies to so you can confirm at a glance whether this update concerns you.

Detail Information
Recruitment Body Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB)
Notification Number CEN No. 08/2024 (Level-1 / Group D)
Total Vacancies (CEN 08/2024) 32,438
Window Opens 17 June 2026, 00:01 hrs
Window Closes 23 June 2026, 23:59 hrs
Eligible Candidates CCAA candidates who appeared in CBT but did not furnish NCVT marks
Official Notice Date 16 June 2026
Purpose Updating NCVT certificate details and marks for CCAA quota benefits

Who Are CCAAs and Why Does This Update Matter?

Before looking at eligibility and steps, it helps to understand who qualifies as a CCAA and why updating NCVT details carries real weight in the RRB Group D selection process.

Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAAs) are candidates who have completed their apprenticeship training in a Railway Establishment under the Apprentices Act. CCAAs trained in a Railway Establishment receive two specific advantages over general candidates in the RRB Group D selection process:

  • NCVT marks weightage: Marks obtained in the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) examination are given due weightage while preparing the final merit list after the CBT.
  • PET exemption: CCAAs trained in Railway Establishments are fully exempt from the Physical Efficiency Test (PET), which is mandatory for all other Group D candidates.

Because these two benefits directly affect a candidate's final merit position and exam process, any CCAA candidate who has not yet recorded their NCVT marks needs to act within this window to remain eligible for them.

Why Was the CCAA Modification Window Opened?

This section explains the background that led RRB to open this window, helping candidates understand whether their specific situation matches the criteria.

The matter traces back to an earlier notice dated 3 February 2025, which addressed two categories of CCAA applicants:

  • Category 1: CCAAs who had already received their National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) from NCVT at the time of application were instructed to enter their training duration, certificate details, and marks directly in the online form.
  • Category 2: CCAAs who had appeared for the NCVT examination before the application deadline, but whose results were not yet declared, were advised to fill in their exam date and flag the result as "awaited."

Despite this earlier instruction, a number of eligible CCAA candidates who went on to appear in the CBT still had not entered their NCVT marks in the system. To allow these candidates to claim the benefits they are entitled to under the CCAA quota, RRB has now opened this dedicated modification window from 17 to 23 June 2026.

Who Is Eligible for the RRB CCAA Modification Window 2026?

This section lists the exact eligibility conditions, since only candidates meeting all three criteria together can use this facility.

A candidate can use this modification window only if all three of the following conditions are met:

  1. The candidate appeared in the Computer Based Test (CBT) under CEN No. 08/2024.
  2. The candidate had not entered their NCVT examination marks in the original online application.
  3. The candidate had indicated the date of their NCVT examination in the application, typically with a "results awaited" flag.

If even one of these conditions is not met for instance, if you did not appear in the CBT, or if your NCVT marks were already filled in correctly at the time of application you are not eligible to use this window.

What Can Be Updated in the Modification Window?

This part covers exactly what information eligible candidates are permitted to add or change during the 17–23 June window.

During this window, eligible CCAA candidates can:

  • Fill in NCVT certificate details, if not entered earlier
  • Update the marks obtained in the NCVT examination
  • Enter National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) details

Once submitted, RRB uses this information to calculate the applicable NCVT weightage for the candidate's CCAA quota benefit, which then feeds into the preparation of the final merit list.

How to Update NCVT Details: Step-by-Step Process

This section walks through the practical process of making the update, from logging in to final submission.

  1. Visit the official RRB website for your respective zone, or the centralised application portal as indicated in your candidature.
  2. Log in to your CEN 08/2024 application using your registration number and password/date of birth.
  3. Navigate to the "Modification Window" or "CCAA/NCVT Details Update" section.
  4. Enter your NCVT certificate number, marks obtained, date of examination, training duration, and any other requested details.
  5. Upload supporting documents if the system prompts you to do so.
  6. Carefully review every entry before submission, since corrections cannot be made once the window closes.
  7. Submit the form before 23 June 2026, 23:59 hrs, and save or download the confirmation/screenshot for your records.

Always complete this process only through the official RRB website for your zone or the application portal linked in the official notice. Avoid third-party websites claiming to offer "application update services," as these are not authorised by RRB.

What Happens If You Miss the Modification Window?

This section explains the consequences of not updating NCVT details within the given time frame, which is critical information for any eligible candidate still undecided about acting.

Missing this window has direct consequences for a CCAA candidate's selection prospects. If you do not update your certificate details and marks during the 17–23 June period, you will not be treated as a "CCAA Trained in Railway Establishment possessing NAC granted by NCVT." As a result, you will:

  • Lose the NCVT marks weightage benefit in the final merit list
  • Not be considered under the CCAA quota for this benefit
  • Likely be required to appear for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET), which CCAA candidates would otherwise be exempt from

Given how competitive RRB Group D recruitment is, losing either of these advantages can materially affect your final selection chances. There is no indication of any extension beyond 23 June 2026, so candidates are advised not to wait until the last day.

Will NCVT Details Be Verified Later?

This short section addresses a common follow-up concern: whether the information submitted now will be checked later in the process.

Yes. As per the official notice, all NCVT examination details filled in by candidates during this modification window will be verified at the Document Verification (DV) stage. Candidature remains subject to the accuracy of the information submitted, so candidates should ensure that certificate numbers, marks, and dates exactly match their original NAC certificate and mark sheet before final submission.

Documents to Keep Ready

Having these documents on hand before you start the update process will make the modification quicker and reduce the risk of entry errors.

  • National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) issued by NCVT
  • NCVT mark sheet showing marks obtained
  • Proof of apprenticeship training duration
  • Railway Establishment training-related documents

Post Name Qualification
Stenographer
  • Candidates must have passed Senior Secondary (10+2) or equivalent. They should possess a shorthand speed of 80 words per minute and a typing speed of 30 words per minute.   • Age Limit : Maximum 35 Years

  • Candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce or a Bachelor’s degree with Mathematics or Statistics as a subject from a recognized university. Candidates must also qualify the examination prescribed by NBEMS.   • Age Limit : Maximum 27 Years.

How to Check Your JKSSB Answer Key 2026: Series A, B, C, D

This section explains how candidates should use the answer key to verify their responses based on their allotted question paper series.

The OMR exam was conducted using four question paper series A, B, C, and D meaning each candidate received one of these four versions of the question booklet. To check answers correctly:

  • Identify the series printed on your OMR sheet/question booklet (A, B, C, or D)
  • Open the relevant annexure (A for Junior Dental Technician, B for Junior Store Clerk)
  • Match each question number with the correct answer option listed under your specific series
  • Avoid cross-checking with a different series, as correct options vary by series for the same question number

Since all four series contain different answer sequences for identical question numbers, candidates must strictly refer to their own series column to get an accurate result.

JKSSB Answer Key Objection Process 2026

This section explains the step-by-step procedure, required documents, and fee for candidates who wish to challenge any answer in the provisional key.

JKSSB allows candidates to formally challenge any answer they believe is incorrect, provided the objection follows the prescribed format and is backed by supporting evidence. The objection window is short, so candidates should act promptly.

Key objection details:

Particular Details
Objection Format Annexure "C" (prescribed proforma)
Submission Mode Offline only
Objection Window 3 working days, starting 25.06.2026
Timing 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM
Fee ₹200 per question (Demand Draft)
Fee Payable To Accounts Officer, J&K Services Selection Board

Submission Centres JKSSB Office, Muthi, Akhnoor Road, Jammu / JKSSB Office, Zamzam Building, Rambagh, Srinagar
Documents Required Hard copies of documentary proof/evidence supporting the claim
Separate Forms Rule One form per question; if multiple questions are entered on one form, only the first will be considered

Steps to raise an objection:

  • Download Annexure "C" (objection proforma) from the official JKSSB notice
  • Fill in candidate details, application number, roll number, exam centre division, and the specific question number with series
  • State the objection clearly and attach hard-copy documentary proof supporting the claim
  • Prepare a demand draft of ₹200 per question in favour of the Accounts Officer, J&K Services Selection Board
  • Submit the completed form, evidence, and demand draft in person at the Jammu or Srinagar JKSSB office within the 3-working-day window
  • Use a separate form for each question being objected to

JKSSB has clearly stated that objections will not be entertained after the stipulated period expires or if submitted through any mode other than offline in person.

What Happens After Objections Are Submitted?

This section explains the review process JKSSB follows once objections are received, and how it affects the final answer key.

Once the objection window closes, JKSSB reviews all submitted representations. If an objection is found correct, the answer key is revised accordingly for all candidates not just the one who raised it. However, JKSSB has clarified that no individual candidate will be notified about whether their specific objection was accepted or rejected. The final answer key, incorporating any approved corrections, is released subsequently and forms the basis for result preparation.

Cancelled Questions in MPSC LDCE Paper 1 and Paper 2 Final Answer Key 2026

Both the Paper 1 and Paper 2 final answer keys include a notice about cancelled questions. Understanding this cancellation policy is critical before calculating your score, as cancelled questions are excluded entirely from the evaluation process.

In both official PDFs, the following notice appears in Marathi: "# ने दर्शविलेले प्रश्न रद्द करण्यात आलेले आहेत", which translates to: "Questions indicated with the # symbol have been cancelled."

Key points about cancelled questions:

  • Any question preceded by the # symbol in the answer key is officially void for all candidates.
  • These questions are not evaluated and do not affect any candidate's score negatively.
  • As per standard MPSC practice, either marks for cancelled questions are granted to all candidates, or the total score is recalculated on a revised total excluding those questions.
  • This policy applies equally to both Paper 1 and Paper 2.
  • Candidates should download the official PDFs to identify the exact question numbers cancelled in each paper.

How to Download MPSC LDCE Paper 1 and Paper 2 Final Answer Key 2026

Accessing the official MPSC LDCE Final Answer Key PDFs for both papers is a straightforward process. Follow the steps below to download the correct answer key for your paper and begin verifying your responses.

  1. Visit the official MPSC website at mpsc.gov.in or use the direct PDF links provided above.
  2. Go to the Answer Key or Notifications section.
  3. Search for "LDCE Final Answer Key 2026" and select either Paper 1 or Paper 2 as applicable.
  4. Click on the respective PDF link to open or download the document.
  5. Confirm that your roll number appears within the listed range for that paper.
  6. Cross-check your answers question by question with the final answer key.
  7. Identify and skip all questions marked with # as they have been cancelled.
  8. Calculate your estimated score using the official MPSC LDCE marking scheme.

How to Calculate Your Expected Score

After downloading the final answer key for your paper, you can follow a systematic method to arrive at your estimated score. Here is a clear, step-by-step approach for both Paper 1 and Paper 2 candidates.

  • Step 1: Note down all the answers you marked during the examination.
  • Step 2: Identify questions marked with # in the answer key and exclude them entirely from your calculation.
  • Step 3: For all remaining questions, compare your response to the correct answer in the final key.
  • Step 4: Add the allotted marks for every correct response as per the MPSC LDCE marking scheme.
  • Step 5: If negative marking applies, deduct the specified marks for each incorrect answer.
  • Step 6: Total your marks to arrive at your estimated final score for the respective paper.

What Is the RPSC Analyst-cum-Programmer Final Answer Key?

The Final Answer Key is the definitive, officially approved set of correct answers for the RPSC Analyst-cum-Programmer/Deputy Director examination. It is published after the provisional answer key challenge window closes and all valid objections raised by candidates have been carefully reviewed by subject matter experts appointed by RPSC.

The final answer key carries absolute authority it is the version used to calculate the official marks of each candidate. Unlike the provisional answer key, no further objections can be raised against the final answer key. If any question was found to be incorrect, ambiguous, or contested through valid objections, RPSC may either revise the answer, award marks to all candidates who appeared for that question, or delete it entirely and all such changes will be reflected in the final answer key.

RPSC Analyst-cum-Programmer Exam Paper Structure

This section explains the two-paper pattern of the Analyst-cum-Programmer/Deputy Director written examination to help candidates understand the scope of each answer key PDF.

The RPSC Analyst-cum-Programmer examination consists of two papers, each carrying 100 marks and a duration of 2 hours. Together, both papers carry a combined total of 200 marks. Below is a summary of the subject coverage for each paper:

Paper Subject Areas Covered Total Marks Duration
Paper I Reasoning, Numerical Analysis, General Knowledge, Current Affairs 100 Marks 2 Hours
Paper II System Analysis & Design, Software Engineering, Software Project Management, Databases, Computer Networks 100 Marks 2 Hours

The minimum qualifying mark for the written examination is 40% in aggregate for General category candidates, and 36% for candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. RPSC may additionally award up to 3 grace marks as per commission rules.

How to Download RPSC Final Answer Key 2026 for Analyst-cum-Programmer

Difference Between Provisional and Final Answer Key

Understanding the distinction between the provisional and final answer key helps candidates interpret the significance of this release.

RPSC follows a two-stage answer key process for all major examinations. First, a provisional answer key is published shortly after the examination, giving candidates an opportunity to raise objections against any answer they believe is incorrect by paying the prescribed objection fee. Once all objections are received and reviewed by an expert committee, RPSC publishes the final answer key. The final answer key incorporates all validated corrections, if any.

Stage Purpose Can Candidates Object?
Provisional Answer Key Initial set of answers for review Yes, within the objection window
Final Answer Key Verified correct answers for result computation No - final and binding

The score calculated using the final answer key will be the official score considered for merit list preparation.

Candidates who qualify the written examination will be called for the next stages of selection, which typically include document verification and/or a personality test (interview), as per the selection process defined by RPSC for this post.

PSSSB Excise Inspector Exam Pattern and Marking Scheme 2026

Understanding the marking scheme is essential for candidates to accurately calculate their expected scores using the final answer key. The PSSSB Excise Inspector written examination 2026 was divided into two parts.

Section Details
Part A Punjabi Language (Qualifying in Nature)
Qualifying Marks in Part A Minimum 50% marks required to qualify
Marking in Part A No negative marking
Part B Main Subjects (Counted for Merit)

Unattempted Questions 0 Marks
